fix.subject: stm32/usart: restore RE after a half-duplex write instead of relying on the next read()
fix.message:
stm32/usart: restore RE after a half-duplex write instead of relying on the next read()

half_duplex_set_rx_tx_before_write() clears RE (NoReadback) for the
duration of every half-duplex write, and the only code that ever set it
back was the entry check at the top of RingBufferedUartRx::read() /
UartRx::blocking_read() — which only runs when a *new* read() call
starts.

That's fine for a single task alternating write()/read() itself, but
breaks when TX and RX are driven by independent, concurrently running
tasks (e.g. one task perpetually parked in RingBufferedUartRx::read()
listening, another periodically writing). The very first write from
the TX task clears RE out from under the RX task's already in-flight
wait_for_data_or_idle(): with the receiver hardware-disabled, no idle
line and no DMA event will ever fire, nothing wakes that future, and
the RX task never returns to make the fresh read() call that would
have turned RE back on. The link's receive side dies permanently after
the first transmission.

Fix: UartTx::write/blocking_write now restore RE (and clear TE) for
half-duplex links themselves once the transmission genuinely completes
(after flush/blocking_flush, so the last byte has left the shift
register), instead of leaving that to whichever side is polled next.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

claude.title: py32-hal's half-duplex UART write turns the receiver off and never turns it back on, so a reader that is already waiting stops receiving.
claude.summary: On 2026-07-15 embassy (commit 082d3b8a) changed UartTx::write and blocking_write so that, in half-duplex mode, they wait for the transmission to finish and then re-enable the receiver (RE) and disable the transmitter (TE). py32-hal, whose USART driver is copied from embassy, still clears RE at the start of every half-duplex write and leaves it to the next read() call to turn it back on; its ring-buffered reader never turns it back on. If the TX and RX halves of a split half-duplex Uart run in separate tasks, a reader that is already waiting never sees data again after the first write, so the receive side stops for good. The fix uses only functions and register fields that py32-hal already has (flush, blocking_flush, CR3.HDSEL, CR1.RE/TE).

fix.subject: dma: fix else-if in on_irq allowing HTIF to mask TCIF
fix.message:
dma: fix else-if in on_irq allowing HTIF to mask TCIF

When both HTIF and TCIF are set simultaneously (e.g. a higher-priority
interrupt delayed this handler), the previous else-if chain only cleared
HTIF and returned without incrementing complete_count. TCIF was left
pending, requiring a second interrupt invocation.

During the window between the two invocations, dma_sync saw count_diff=0
with pos < self.pos (DMA had wrapped), triggering the cap-1 fallback.
This temporarily under-reported available ring buffer data by the number
of items written into the new DMA lap, causing an unnecessary extra
Poll::Pending in read_exact.

Replace with separate if blocks so both flags are handled (and
complete_count incremented) in a single interrupt invocation.
Applied to both the DMA and BDMA branches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The embassy commit (message "dma: fix else-if in on_irq allowing HTIF to mask TCIF") replaces `} else if isr.tcif(...)` with a separate `if` plus an activity flag, because "When both HTIF and TCIF are set simultaneously ... the previous else-if chain only cleared HTIF and returned without incrementing complete_count"; embassy still has this at dma_bdma/mod.rs:57-77. py32-hal's AnyChannel::on_irq (src/dma/dma.rs:170-188) is the same pre-fix logic: the half-transfer branch at line 170 and the transfer-complete branch, which acknowledges TCIF and increments complete_count (line 178), are joined by `} else if` at line 173. py32-hal's ring buffers enable both interrupts in circular mode (src/dma/dma.rs:585-587), and its dma_sync has the same fallback the commit message describes, `if pos < self.pos && count_diff == 0 { cap - 1 }` (src/dma/ringbuffer/mod.rs:55-56), so the same temporary under-report can happen. The fix only restructures existing branches and uses nothing py32-hal lacks; the extra NDTR check in py32-hal's transfer-complete branch is unaffected.
claude.title: py32-hal's DMA interrupt handler uses else-if, so a pending half-transfer flag hides the transfer-complete flag until a second interrupt.
claude.summary: On 2026-03-17 embassy (commit 1b36829e) replaced the else-if chain in the DMA interrupt handler with two separate checks, so that when the half-transfer and transfer-complete flags are both set the handler clears both and counts the finished buffer lap in one pass. py32-hal's AnyChannel::on_irq still has the else-if: with both flags set it clears only the half-transfer flag, and the transfer-complete flag and the lap counter wait for a second interrupt. In between, the ring buffer's position sync sees the DMA position wrap with no lap counted and falls back to cap - 1, so it briefly reports less received data than there is and read_exact waits one extra round. Nothing is lost, so the effect is a short extra delay, and the embassy change can be copied directly.
claude.impact_note: The transfer-complete flag stays pending and is handled by a second interrupt right afterwards, so no data is lost; the ring buffer only briefly reports less data than it holds and read_exact waits one extra wake-up.

fix.subject: Fix dma nvic issues on dual core lines
fix.message:
Fix dma nvic issues on dual core lines

This commit addresses #3256 by disabling dma NVIC interrupt enablement at startup.
Instead, per-channel NVIC interrupt enablement is now done with the rest of the dma channel configuration.
This ensures that each core will only handle the interrupts of the DMA channels that it uses.

fix.subject: stm32/timer: avoid max_compare_value >= u16::MAX
fix.message:
stm32/timer: avoid max_compare_value >= u16::MAX

With STM32 32 bits timers, the max_compare_value (AKA, ARR register)
can currently be set greater than u16::MAX, which leads to the following
assert!(max < u16::MAX as u32) in max_duty_cycle() when setting up a 1 kHz
SimplePwm on 84 MHz MCU.

The issue is fixed by forcing a max_compare_value that fits into 16 bits
when setting the frequency for a PWM.

claude.evidence: Embassy's fix ("fix incorrect logic for buffered usart transmission complete") changes the TC branch of the buffered UART interrupt handler from if sr_val.tc() to if sr_val.tc() && r.cr1().read().tcie(), so transmission-complete is only reported when the driver itself armed TCIE after loading the last byte (embassy buffered.rs line 105 now). py32-hal's on_interrupt in src/usart/buffered.rs is the same pre-fix code: at line 87 it tests only the TC status bit, then clears TC, disables TCIE, sets tx_done = true and wakes the TX waker (lines 89-95), while TCIE is armed only when the last byte is written (lines 109-111). The handler is shared with RXNE/IDLE/TXE interrupts and is also pended by write() right after write() sets tx_done = false (lines 493 and 509), so any time the TC status bit is already set without TCIE being armed (a stale TC, or TC set between bytes while more data is queued), tx_done becomes true and flush() (line 521) returns before the queued bytes are sent. I checked what could make it inapplicable: py32's CR1 has the TCIE bit (the driver calls set_tcie), clear_interrupt_flags is a no-op on this v1-style USART (usart/mod.rs line 1640) so nothing else clears or filters TC, and no other guard exists. When exactly the TC bit is set is hardware behaviour not visible in the repository, hence medium confidence.
claude.title: The buffered UART interrupt handler treats any set TC flag as end of transmission even when TCIE was not armed, so flush() can finish before the queued bytes are sent.
claude.summary: Embassy fixed its buffered UART in November 2025 (commit 4e80834) so the interrupt handler only reports transmission complete when the TC flag is set and the TC interrupt was actually enabled by the driver after loading the last byte. py32-hal's buffered UART, copied from the older embassy code, still checks only the TC flag: whenever the shared interrupt runs (receive, idle, TX-empty, or the software pend issued by write()) while TC happens to be set, it marks the transmission as done and wakes flush(). As a result flush() can return while bytes are still in the TX buffer, which matters to callers that switch an RS-485 direction pin, power down or reconfigure the UART after flushing. The port is the one-line condition change; how often a stale TC is present depends on hardware timing that the repository does not show.

claude.title: py32-hal's BufferedUartRx embedded-hal serial read() reads the UART data register directly instead of the interrupt-filled receive buffer.
claude.summary: Embassy fixed this on 2025-02-24 (commit 76756ee7): the embedded-hal 0.2 / embedded-hal-nb non-blocking read of BufferedUartRx now takes bytes from the ring buffer that the UART interrupt fills. py32-hal's copy in src/usart/buffered.rs (lines 739-765) still checks the status register and reads the data register itself, while its interrupt handler is reading the same data register into the ring buffer. As a result, code that uses nb::block!(rx.read()) on a py32 buffered UART will mostly get WouldBlock and never see the bytes already received into the buffer, and a direct read can occasionally take a byte away from the interrupt handler, so received data is effectively lost through this API. The fix carries over with only the names unchanged, because py32-hal uses the same State and RingBuffer types as embassy.

claude.title: py32-hal's buffered UART blocking flush returns when the software buffer is empty, before the last bytes have actually been transmitted.
claude.summary: Embassy fixed this on 2025-09-10 (commit 88c42745, PR #4648): the buffered UART's blocking_flush now waits for the transmission-complete flag set by the TC interrupt, and blocking_write clears that flag first. py32-hal copied the async version of this logic, but its blocking_flush (src/usart/buffered.rs line 555) still only waits until the ring buffer is empty, and blocking_write never clears the flag. Without the fix, flush() on the blocking, embedded-io and embedded-hal paths returns while the final byte or two are still being shifted out, so anything done right after flush, such as releasing an RS-485 driver-enable line, changing the baud rate, entering low power or dropping the UART (which turns off its clock), can truncate the end of the message. The upstream patch, both the blocking_flush line and the blocking_write line, applies to py32-hal unchanged; embassy later hardened the same flag logic against races (4e808345, fe45c6e7), which a port may also want to take.

[stm32] fix flex reborrowing

The previous behavior was for a reborrowed Flex to set the pin as
disconnected when dropped. This is sane behavior for Flexs that own
their Peri, because we want the pin to be reset to its default state,
so it can be re-used in a predictable manner. But in the case of a

since a Flex handle to it still exists.

splitting a BufferedUart into Tx and Rx halves using
BufferedUart::split_ref. The UART should remain usable after these
halves are dropped, but it currently isn't because the pins get reset.

claude.title: py32-hal's timer get_frequency divides by ARR instead of ARR + 1, so it reports a frequency that is too high and divides by zero when ARR is 0.
claude.summary: Embassy fixed stm32/timer get_frequency on 2026-07-13 (commit c184286a) so that it divides by (arr + 1), matching how the period is programmed as ARR + 1 counts. py32-hal's Timer::get_frequency in src/timer/low_level.rs still computes timer_f / arr / (psc + 1) in both its 16-bit and 32-bit arms, while its own set_frequency writes arr = divide_by - 1. claude.evidence: The embassy commit 'Dead-time computation in complementary PWM fixed (missing DTG msbs added)' ORs the DTG[7:5] mode bits into the value returned by compute_dead_time_value; for the 110 and 111 ranges the old value 32 + target/8 (or /16) lacks those bits, while the 10x change is a no-op because 64 + target/2 already lies in 128..191. py32-hal copied this function from embassy-stm32 and still has the exact pre-fix lines (src/timer/complementary_pwm.rs lines 251, 253, 255) in the same function, whose own comment documents the same encoding (lines 215-216), and set_dead_time passes the result straight to BDTR.DTG (low_level.rs line 664); the module is built unconditionally. For example a request of 400 ticks returns DTG = 82 (its own test at line 311 expects exactly this), which under the documented encoding is a 0xx value meaning 82 tDTS instead of 400. Nothing in py32-hal handles the mode bits another way; the only gap in evidence is that the PY32 register description lives in the external py32-metapac crate, so the encoding match rests on the copied comment and the identical BDTR.DTG field.
claude.title: py32-hal's complementary PWM dead-time encoder leaves out the DTG mode bits for long dead times, so the timer inserts a much shorter dead time than requested.
claude.summary: embassy-stm32 fixed compute_dead_time_value in April 2025 (commit d1555f4) by setting the DTG[7:5] mode bits (110 and 111) for dead times of 255 ticks and more, and its later rewrite still sets them. py32-hal copied the function from embassy-stm32 in November 2024 and still has the pre-fix lines, with a comment that documents the same DTG encoding. When the chosen encoding falls in the 110 or 111 range (for example a request of 400 ticks, or large requests above about 1020 ticks), the value written to BDTR.DTG is read by the timer as a plain 0xx count, so the real dead time is a fraction of the requested one (82 instead of 400 tDTS). The 10x range is not affected. The PY32 timer register description is in the external py32-metapac crate, so the match of the encoding rests on the copied comment and the identical field name.

fix.subject: stm32/usb: add optional VBUS detection
fix.message:
stm32/usb: add optional VBUS detection

The full-speed USB peripheral has no VBUS input and its suspend event only
means the host stopped traffic for 3 ms, so a self-powered device cannot
tell a suspended bus from an unplugged cable. Endpoint transfers then block
until a timeout instead of failing.

Add Driver::new_with_vbus, which takes an ExtiInput and reports
PowerRemoved/PowerDetected from Bus::poll. When VBUS drops, disable all
endpoints so pending transfers return EndpointError::Disabled, and clear
DPPU to signal disconnect to the host. PowerDetected restores DPPU and the
host reset re-enumerates.

The constructor is gated on the exti feature; Driver::new is unchanged.

Fixes #3740

fix.subject: feat: CH32H4 family bring-up, AFIO mux refactor and dual-core examples (#180)
fix.message:
feat: CH32H4 family bring-up, AFIO mux refactor and dual-core examples (#180)

- Bump dependencies to the published ch32-metapac 0.1.2 and qingke / qingke-rt 0.8.2, with no local patches.
- The HAL enables qingke/unsafe-trust-wch-atomics. Custom targets use native atomics (atomic-cas: true) instead of critical-section-emulated cross-core CAS.
- Existing chips keep const REMAP: u8 and peripheral-group remapping, so new::<0> / new_ch1::<1> call sites stay valid.
- H4 uses per-pin AF numbers and writes AFIO.GPIO_AFR. GPIO initialization enables the AFIO clock.
- Shared AfType, new_pin!, and set_as_af! helpers unify driver pin configuration, and fix a CAN remap bug along the way.
- H4 gets GPIO/USART, the existing V3-layout I2C driver, timers with GLOBAL IRQs, and a polling SysTick delay.
- ADC/DAC/SPI/CAN/flash/USBPD stay cfg-gated out on H4, left as follow-up.
- H4 DMA drives the DMAMUX from the request number in metadata: dma_trait_impl! gains a {dmamux} arm, and every H4 channel implements MuxChannel.
- The Embassy SysTick time driver is excluded on H4.
- Add init_secondary for the core that does not own the chip. It reads the clock tree back instead of reprogramming the PLL, which would switch SYSCLK out from under the boot core.
- init_secondary leaves the AFIO reset off, since that pulse clears GPIO_AFR back to AF0, and leaves the DMA interrupt enables off, since enabling an interrupt above 31 assigns it to the enabling core.
- A transfer unmasks only its own channel's interrupt. build.rs now records that interrupt per channel.
- H4 RCC: HSI/HSE 400/480 MHz EVT presets, auxiliary PLLs, prescalers, and clock mux configuration.
- rcc::refresh(hse) reads registers back, and the Clocks cache is unified, recording both v3f and v5f frequencies on H4.
- Default-HSE recipes pass the real 25 MHz crystal into the cache refresh instead of panicking after PLL initialization.
- Polling delay picks the calling hart's counter and cached frequency, splitting long waits into 32-bit compare chunks. Fractional cycles round up, and zero-length waits are no-ops.
- CH641: RCC_CFGR0.HPRE = 0b1100 divides by 32, not 16. Both the prescaler table and the register read-back are fixed.
- H4 prescaler decoding is corrected: HPRE 0b1100 divides by 64, not 32, and FPRE 0b11 divides by 4 since the field encodes ÷4 as 1x.
- The PLL multiplier now comes from the Pllmul enum, so the half-step codes and the holes in the table are right, and the multiply is widened to u64 because an auxiliary-PLL reference times ×59 overflows
a u32.
- examples/ch32h417/ is split into v3f/, v5f/, a shared IPC crate, and a host xtask.
- Flashing programs only the boot core by default. --dual-core programs both halves, and --jump-v5f pairs a launcher with the selected V5F image.
- The V5F crate now depends on the HAL. The BME280 half calls init_secondary and reads PCLK1 from rcc::clocks() instead of keeping its own copy of the PLL table. The halves that need no driver still skip
it.
- The empty examples/ch32h417/v5f/device.x is removed, so it no longer shadows metapac's rt script and leaves the interrupt handlers undefined.
- Both cores share one SRAM_SHARED region at 0x20178000 holding a single Mailbox<T>. The boot core defines it via shared.x, and the V5F image only reads MAILBOX_ADDR.
- xtask report cross-checks the mailbox address by parsing the ELF32 symtab in Rust, so CI needs no llvm-nm.
- Examples cover blinky (nanoCH32H417 PF2), I2C scan/BME280, SDI printing, dual-core handover and CPU-ID, ping-pong, cross-core atomics, SysTick delay, and rcc_delay_check.
- Cross-core CAS litmus: each core does 1,000,000 fetch_add operations on one shared word, totaling exactly 2,000,000.
- build.rs rebuilds the signal tables as one table with rows removed per chip. Generated output for ch32v203c8t6 is byte-identical to the pre-refactor script.
- CI builds the ch32h417 examples and enables Xwchc per chip rather than globally.

claude.evidence: The embassy commit message says the old initial value {complete_count:0, pos:len} and the new one {complete_count:1, pos:0} "represent the same linear position (one full buffer ahead of read_index)", and that the only visible problem was that "write_pos() returned cap instead of 0"; write_pos() is a public getter that returns the raw `self.write_index.pos` and was added to embassy just before this fix. py32-hal's WritableDmaRingBuffer has no write_pos() (no match anywhere under src/), and DmaIndex is a private struct, so the raw pos cannot be read from outside src/dma/ringbuffer/mod.rs. claude.title: py32-hal's non-blocking serial write on UartTx blocks until the transmit register is free instead of returning WouldBlock.
claude.summary: On 2025-07-03 embassy-stm32 fixed its `embedded_hal_nb::serial::Write` impl for `UartTx`: `write` now calls a new `nb_write` that returns WouldBlock when TXE is not set, where before it called `blocking_write`. py32-hal, which copied this USART driver from embassy-stm32, still has the old body, so every non-blocking `write` busy-waits on TXE with no timeout. The irq handler could drain the TX ring and wake between a failed push
and the waker registration; its final drain pops an empty ring and does
not wake again, parking the writer forever on an empty buffer with the

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The rp commit message says the irq handler "could drain the TX ring and wake between a failed push and the waker registration" and that its final drain does not wake again, parking the writer forever; the fix moves state.tx_waker.register(cx.waker()) in front of the check in write() and says "Same fix for flush()". embassy-stm32's BufferedUartTx::write() still calls tx_writer.push_slice() first and registers the tx_waker only inside if data.is_empty() (line 861), and flush() still loads tx_done first and registers only inside if !tx_done (line 881), which is the same check-then-register order as the rp code before the fix. In the stm32 interrupt handler the only tx_waker.wake() for this State is in the TC branch when tx_buf is empty (line 121), which also clears TCIE, so it is a one-shot final wake just like rp's final drain; if it lands between the check and the register (for example on the first wait, when no waker is stored yet), nothing wakes the task again. Both drivers use the same embassy_sync AtomicWaker, the stm32 code neither re-checks after registering nor polls, and nothing hardware-specific is involved; confidence is medium only because the race depends on interrupt timing and cannot be shown by reading alone.
claude.title: embassy-stm32 BufferedUartTx write() and flush() register the TX waker only after checking the buffer state, so a TX-complete wake that arrives in between is lost and the task can hang.
claude.summary: On 2026-09-25 embassy-rp (commit f1fff55) moved the TX waker registration in its buffered UART write() and flush() ahead of the state check, because an interrupt that drained the ring and woke in between left the writer parked forever. embassy-stm32's buffered USART at the pinned commit still checks first and registers only on the pending path, in write() at line 861 and in flush() at line 881, and its interrupt wakes the TX waker only once, when TC fires with an empty ring. If that wake falls between the check and the registration, write() or flush() can stay pending until some unrelated event re-polls the task, so for example an RS-485 sender waiting in flush() stalls. The race depends on interrupt timing and was judged from code reading only; the fix is to register the waker before the check, as rp now does.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: Besides cleanup, the listed hunk rewrites the error path of imx9_lpi2c_isr_process, which is what the commit message means by 'handle error cases properly': on any LPI2C_MSR_ERROR_MASK bit the new code clears the TX and RX FIFOs (LPI2C_MCR_RTF | LPI2C_MCR_RRF), clears all error flags, sets msgc and dcnt to 0 and then sends STOP or ends the transfer, whereas the old code only recorded the status, sent STOP when I2C_M_NOSTOP was clear and cleared NDF/ALF/FEF/EPF. imxrt_lpi2c_isr_process is the old imx9 handler line for line (a whitespace-insensitive diff of the two functions differs only in the DMA channel names, and imxrt_lpi2c_sem_waitdone likewise matches the old imx9 version): its error branch (lines 1582-1603) leaves dcnt, msgc, the FIFOs and the TDIE/RDIE enables untouched, so later TDF/RDF interrupts go back through the normal branch, which keeps writing bytes while dcnt > 0 and starts the next message at line 1512, and the waiting thread is woken only when EPF and SDF are seen together (line 1616). Nothing else in the imxrt driver ends a failed transfer early: imxrt_lpi2c_transfer only checks priv->status after the wait, and this interrupt path is the default because IMXRT_LPI2C_DMA defaults to n. Every bit the 08949dec version uses (LPI2C_MCR_RTF/RRF, LPI2C_MSR_ERROR_MASK, EPF/SDF, the MIER bits, LPI2C_MTDR_CMD_STOP) is defined for imxrt, and the current imx9 handler still flushes the FIFOs and zeroes the counts on error; only a later imx9 refinement (3afa58cdd) switched to LPI2C_MCFG0_ABORT, which imxrt does not define. Confidence is medium because the commit message names no concrete failure, the bus-level effect depends on controller behaviour the repository does not document, and parts of the rewrite (message chaining, ignoring NACK on the last RX byte) are design changes rather than this fix.

claude.title: The imxrt LPI2C interrupt handler does not end a transfer on a NACK or lost arbitration, so later interrupts can keep sending the remaining bytes and messages.
claude.summary: In September 2024 the imx9 LPI2C driver (commit 08949dec, 'Cleanups and error fixes') rewrote its interrupt handler so that on an error it flushes the TX/RX FIFOs, clears all error flags, zeroes the remaining message and byte counts and ends the transfer, sending STOP if none was seen. The imxrt LPI2C driver still has the old handler: on NACK or lost arbitration it records the status, queues STOP only if the message lacks I2C_M_NOSTOP and clears the flags, but leaves the counts, FIFOs and TX/RX interrupts as they are and wakes the caller only when end-of-packet and STOP are seen together. As a result, after an error later interrupts can keep queuing the remaining bytes and start the next messages on the bus, and with I2C_M_NOSTOP no STOP is sent, so the caller may only get a timeout instead of a quick error. The exact bus effect depends on controller behaviour the repository does not document, and the imx9 rewrite also changed how messages are chained and was refined by later commits (one uses an ABORT bit imxrt does not define), so only the error-path part should be carried over, with testing on hardware.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/stm32h5/stm32_usbdrdhost.c: Disable host channel when freed
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/stm32h5/stm32_usbdrdhost.c: Disable host channel when freed

The host interrupt callback was incorrectly using the wrong IRQ for
disconnected. In host mode the same IRQ is used for connect/disconnected
and it must check a status bit to know which one.

When a USB device was unplugged, the host channels were free'd,
but if they happen to be mid-transfer, that transfer was never cancelled
so the USB hardware might still be trying to perfrom a transfer after
was free'd. Fixed by cancelling any transfers on free.

Signed-off-by: daniellizewski <daniellizewski@geotab.com>

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/stm32h5/stm32_usbdrdhost.c: Disable host channel when freed
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/stm32h5/stm32_usbdrdhost.c: Disable host channel when freed

The host interrupt callback was incorrectly using the wrong IRQ for
disconnected. In host mode the same IRQ is used for connect/disconnected
and it must check a status bit to know which one.

When a USB device was unplugged, the host channels were free'd,
but if they happen to be mid-transfer, that transfer was never cancelled
so the USB hardware might still be trying to perfrom a transfer after
was free'd. Fixed by cancelling any transfers on free.

Signed-off-by: daniellizewski <daniellizewski@geotab.com>

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The picked hunk belongs to the feature work named in the commit message, 'Added DMA support for H5. Also added ADC DMA support.': before this commit the H5 ADC rejected DMA outright (the same diff removes '#  error "STM32H5 ADC does not have DMA support."' under ADC_HAVE_DMA), so the replaced block never built on H5, and the hunk rewrites it for the H5 GPDMA driver added in the same commit (stm32_dmachannel(GPDMA_TTYPE_P2M), adc_dmacfg() filling a struct stm32_gpdma_cfg_s, two-argument stm32_dmasetup). On the other side, adc_dma_start() in both stm32_adc_m0_v1.c and stm32_adc_m3m4_v1v2.c calls the five-argument stm32_dmasetup(), which is exactly the API declared in common/stm32/stm32_dma_channel_stream.h. common/stm32/stm32_dma.h only switches to the two-argument GPDMA header when CONFIG_STM32_HAVE_IP_DMA_GPDMA is set, and the families that build these ADC drivers select the channel/stream DMA instead (for example stm32g0 selects STM32_HAVE_IP_ADC_M0_V1 with STM32_HAVE_IP_DMA_V1, and stm32f4 selects STM32_HAVE_IP_ADC_M3M4_V1 with STM32_HAVE_IP_DMA_V2), while stm32h5 selects STM32_HAVE_IP_DMA_GPDMA. The old lines are therefore correct for their own DMA driver, and the hunk is new-feature adaptation, not a bug fix.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk is the declaration half of the stm32_getstatus fix (elapsed/reload become remaining/counter for the new computation in the same function); the commit message says 'stm32_getstatus() returned the time elapsed since the last keepalive as timeleft' and that 'the time left is the ticks above T_MAX scaled by the timeout', and also 'The debug print also showed the flags instead of the time left.' at32_wwdg.c is the same WWDG driver: at32_start/at32_keepalive load WWDG_CR_T_RESET | priv->reload, settimeout caps priv->reload at WWDG_CR_T_MAX, at32_wdg.h defines the same T_MASK/T_SHIFT/T_MAX (0x3f)/T_RESET (0x40), and at32_getstatus still declares 'uint32_t elapsed; uint16_t reload;' and returns timeout * elapsed / (reload + 1) under the comment 'Get the time remaining'. Its elapsed is computed as 'priv->reload - reload' without the T_RESET bit, so while the counter is at or above 0x40 the subtraction is negative and wraps in uint32_t, which makes the reported timeleft meaningless rather than merely inverted; the debug line still prints status->flags as timeleft. The other file in this packet, at32_iwdg.c, does not need the change: its at32_getstatus measures clock_systime_ticks() since the last ping and already returns priv->timeout - elapsed. Every macro the fix uses exists in arch/arm/src/at32/hardware/at32_wdg.h, so nothing on AT32 makes the fix inapplicable.

claude.title: The AT32 window watchdog reports a wrong time left in WDIOC_GETSTATUS instead of the time remaining before reset.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-20 commit 14f2daaa2 fixed stm32_getstatus() in the shared STM32 WWDG driver, which reported the time elapsed since the last keepalive as timeleft: it now takes the counter value above WWDG_CR_T_MAX, scales it by the timeout, and prints timeleft instead of the flags. The AT32 WWDG driver, a copy of the same driver with the same register definitions, still has the old variables and formula, and its elapsed value 'priv->reload - reload' even lacks the T_RESET bit, so the subtraction goes negative and wraps. As a result WDIOC_GETSTATUS and reads of the watchdog device return a meaningless time left on AT32, and the debug print shows the flags in place of the time left; the reset timing itself is not affected. The new lines carry over with only the stm32 names changed to at32. The AT32 independent watchdog (at32_iwdg.c), also in this packet, already computes the time left from system ticks and needs no change.

claude.title: The GD32W51x window watchdog reports the elapsed time instead of the time left in WDIOC_GETSTATUS.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-20 commit 14f2daaa2 fixed stm32_getstatus() in the STM32 WWDG driver, which returned the time elapsed since the last keepalive as timeleft, by taking the counter value above WWDG_CR_T_MAX instead. claude.title: The GD32VW55x window watchdog reports the elapsed time instead of the time left in WDIOC_GETSTATUS.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-20 commit 14f2daaa2 fixed stm32_getstatus() in the STM32 WWDG driver, which returned the time elapsed since the last keepalive as timeleft, by taking the counter value above WWDG_CR_T_MAX instead. The GD32VW55x WWDGT driver (added 2026-07-16, before that fix) uses the same counter scheme (loaded with CNT_RESET | reload, timeout of reload + 1 ticks) and still computes 'elapsed = priv->reload - (counter & WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX)', returning timeout * elapsed / (reload + 1) as timeleft. WDIOC_GETSTATUS and reads of the watchdog device therefore report about 0 ms right after a keepalive and nearly the full timeout just before the reset, the reverse of the real time left; the reset timing itself is not affected. The fix carries over by replacing the two computation lines with 'counter > WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX ? counter - WWDGT_CTL_CNT_MAX : 0' scaled the same way; the debug-print part of the STM32 fix is not needed because this driver already prints timeleft.

fix.subject: riscv: Fix page table traversal for SV39
fix.message:
riscv: Fix page table traversal for SV39

With CONFIG_PAGING enabled and the RISC-V SV39 MMU active, the page fault
handler incorrectly tracked page table levels: `ptprev` pointed to the L1
page table while `ptlevel` indicated L2. This inconsistency caused faulty
virtual address resolution.

This commit fixes the traversal logic to ensure consistent level tracking
across all three page table levels (L1–L3), enabling reliable page fault
handling and on-demand paging.

Additional changes:
- Set PGT_L3_SIZE to 2048 to enable mapping up to 8MB of address space.
- Update knsh_paging config to avoid crashes caused by excessive memory
  alignment requirements.
- Add knsh64_paging config to verify this commit works as expected.

Signed-off-by: liang.huang <liang.huang@houmo.ai>

lines: #define PGT_L3_SIZE     (1024) /* Enough to map 4 MiB (2MiB x 2) */
#define PGT_L3_SIZE     (2048) /* Enough to map 8 MiB (2MiB x 4) */
#define PGT_L3_SIZE      (1024) /* Enough to map 4 MiB (2MiB x 2) */

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The picked hunk only enlarges qemu-rv's static L3 page-table pool from 1024 to 2048 entries; the commit message lists it under 'Additional changes' as 'Set PGT_L3_SIZE to 2048 to enable mapping up to 8MB of address space', next to the new knsh64_paging config, while the traversal fix itself is in riscv_exception.c. In both qemu-rv and bl808 this pool is used only by map_region for the kernel text and data (KFLASH and KSRAM), and the page pool is mapped with L2 entries, so the size needed depends on the board's kernel memory map: qemu-rv's ld-kernel.script sets KSRAM_SIZE to CONFIG_RAM_SIZE, and knsh64_paging sets CONFIG_RAM_SIZE=4194304 (the older knsh64 uses 2097152), which with the 2 MiB kernel text no longer fits two 2 MiB L3 tables. On bl808, KFLASH_SIZE and KSRAM_SIZE come from the linker symbols of the only bl808 board, ox64, whose ld.script fixes kflash at 2048K from 0x50200000 and ksram at 2048K from 0x50400000, i.e. 4 MiB in two 2 MiB-aligned blocks, exactly what bl808's comment '(1024) /* Enough to map 4 MiB (2MiB x 2) */' provides. The larger table therefore answers a qemu-rv configuration that bl808 does not have, and bl808 needs no change.

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The behavioural fix is in the 4-bit SD hunk: when the board asks for more than 25 MHz, imx9 now uses CMD6 to switch a card that reports high-speed support into high-speed mode and drops to 25 MHz if the switch fails, which the commit message describes as fixing 'an error where cards are being operated in standard mode at over 25MHz speeds'; the IDMODE, MMC and 1-bit hunks only replace the board's PRESCALER/DIVISOR macros with a requested frequency that the driver turns into divisors, a change of the board interface rather than a behaviour fix. imxrt_usdhc.c already prevents the same problem another way: the normal CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_4BIT case keeps the board's default-speed divisors (the in-tree imxrt boards set them to about 24.8 MHz, documented as '24.8MHz for other modes'), and a faster clock is only applied in a separate CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_4BIT_HS case, 'sent only after the card has confirmed the CMD6 high speed switch'. fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32: Fix RNG read hang on seed or clock error.
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32: Fix RNG read hang on seed or clock error.

On a seed error (SEIS) or clock error (CEIS) the interrupt handler
returned without clearing the flag, so the interrupt fired forever and
read() never returned.

Now the handler clears the flag and:

- seed error: restarts the RNG,
- clock error: read() fails with -EIO.

This is how the removed STM32H7 driver handled errors.  Also affects
STM32F2, STM32F4 and STM32G4.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5-1
Signed-off-by: raiden00pl <raiden00@railab.me>

/* Wait until the buffer is filled */
_err("ERROR: RNG clock error, check the RNG kernel clock\n");
/* We've got the device semaphore, proceed with reading */
/* Reset the operation semaphore with 0 for blocking until the
/* Wait until the buffer is filled */
/* Free RNG via the device mutex for next use */

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The commit fixes a read hang that happened because on SEIS or CEIS 'the interrupt handler returned without clearing the flag, so the interrupt fired forever and read() never returned'; the picked hunk (g_rngdev.rd_error = 0 in the read function) only resets the new error code that lets read() fail with -EIO after a clock error. The STM32F7 driver does not have the uncleared-flag handler: stm32_rnginterrupt() writes CEIS back to zero and returns ('Clear it, we will try again.'), and on SEIS it clears the flag and toggles RNGEN off and on, which is equivalent to the seed-error restart the fix adds. Its struct has no rd_error and its read() simply waits for data, because the F7 design retries after a clock error instead of reporting it (stm32l4_rng.c uses the same clear-and-retry handler). The one remaining difference is error policy, not the interrupt storm: if the RNG kernel clock is permanently missing, an F7 read() keeps waiting instead of returning -EIO, so a reviewer may still want the -EIO reporting there, hence medium confidence.

fix.subject: arch/arm/nrf52: fix the TX state handling
fix.message:
arch/arm/nrf52: fix the TX state handling

- With unslotted CSMA-CA the RADIO interrupt is raised on PHYEND and on
  CCABUSY. nrf52_radioi8_state_tx() ran the TX done path first for both,
  so a busy channel started the ACK wait timer or queued the TX done
  work although no frame was sent. The retry after CCABUSY triggered
  CCA again without SHORTS and INTEN, which the interrupt handler clears
  on entry.
- When CSMA-CA gave up, nrf52_radioi8_work_busy() confirmed
  txdelayed_desc instead of csma_desc and left csma_busy set, so no
  other CSMA transaction was taken from the MAC. The interrupt handler
  left waitack set for the frame that was not sent and restored RX, so
  received frames were dropped as not being the ACK until the work ran.
- nrf52_radioi8_work_tx() and nrf52_radioi8_work_rx() enabled RX after
  the next CSMA transaction was armed. RX enable sets SHORTS, INTEN,
  PACKETPTR and the state for RX, so the armed transaction was replaced
  by RX. RX is now enabled only when the radio is disabled, and the MAC
  is polled for the next CSMA transaction after a completed or failed
  one.
- nrf52_radioi8_txdelayed() set txdelayed_busy and returned -EBUSY when
  a CSMA transaction was in progress. The MAC does not check the return
  value, so the frame, for example the data frame sent after a data
  request, was neither sent nor confirmed. It is now kept pending and
  started when the CSMA transaction is done, and txdelayed_busy and the
  ACK TX state are checked with interrupts disabled, since the ACK TX
  interrupt starts a busy transaction.

fix.subject: arch/arm/nrf52: fix the TX state handling
fix.message:
arch/arm/nrf52: fix the TX state handling

- With unslotted CSMA-CA the RADIO interrupt is raised on PHYEND and on
  CCABUSY. nrf52_radioi8_state_tx() ran the TX done path first for both,
  so a busy channel started the ACK wait timer or queued the TX done
  work although no frame was sent. The retry after CCABUSY triggered
  CCA again without SHORTS and INTEN, which the interrupt handler clears
  on entry.
- When CSMA-CA gave up, nrf52_radioi8_work_busy() confirmed
  txdelayed_desc instead of csma_desc and left csma_busy set, so no
  other CSMA transaction was taken from the MAC. The interrupt handler
  left waitack set for the frame that was not sent and restored RX, so
  received frames were dropped as not being the ACK until the work ran.
- nrf52_radioi8_work_tx() and nrf52_radioi8_work_rx() enabled RX after
  the next CSMA transaction was armed. RX enable sets SHORTS, INTEN,
  PACKETPTR and the state for RX, so the armed transaction was replaced
  by RX. RX is now enabled only when the radio is disabled, and the MAC
  is polled for the next CSMA transaction after a completed or failed
  one.
- nrf52_radioi8_txdelayed() set txdelayed_busy and returned -EBUSY when
  a CSMA transaction was in progress. The MAC does not check the return
  value, so the frame, for example the data frame sent after a data
  request, was neither sent nor confirmed. It is now kept pending and
  started when the CSMA transaction is done, and txdelayed_busy and the
  ACK TX state are checked with interrupts disabled, since the ACK TX
  interrupt starts a busy transaction.

fix.subject: espressif: stop leaking a Wi-Fi interrupt handle on every esp_wifi_start()
fix.message:
espressif: stop leaking a Wi-Fi interrupt handle on every esp_wifi_start()

set_intr_wrapper() allocates a new intr_handle_data_t from the kernel
heap each time the Wi-Fi driver calls it, and the driver calls it on
every esp_wifi_start() -- twice per start on esp32s3 -- not only the
first time.  clear_intr_wrapper() is a no-op, so the IRQ still holds the
handle from the previous start: esp_set_handle() refuses to replace it
with -EINVAL, the return value is ignored, and the new block is lost.

Any application that stops and restarts Wi-Fi to save power therefore
loses a few bytes of kernel heap per cycle, without bound.

Look up the vector descriptor first, then reuse the handle already
registered for the IRQ and only allocate and register one when there is
none.  A failed descriptor lookup no longer touches the registered
handle.

The same code is present in the esp32, esp32s2, esp32s3, esp32c3 and
esp32c6 Wi-Fi adapters; all five are fixed the same way.

Signed-off-by: Felipe Moura <moura.fmo@gmail.com>
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

claude.title: The ESP32-C2 Wi-Fi adapter allocates a new interrupt handle on every Wi-Fi start and leaks it because the IRQ already has one registered.
claude.summary: On 2026-09-30 commit 1c6ed642b changed set_intr_wrapper in the esp32, esp32s2, esp32s3, esp32c3 and esp32c6 Wi-Fi adapters to reuse the interrupt handle already registered for the IRQ instead of allocating a new one each time. The ESP32-C2 adapter, added two weeks later, still has the old code: each call allocates a new handle from the kernel heap and passes it to esp_set_handle, which refuses it with -EINVAL because the handle from the first start is still registered, and the new block is never freed. An application that stops and restarts Wi-Fi on ESP32-C2 (for example to save power) therefore loses a few bytes of kernel heap per cycle without bound. The same patch applies with no changes; the only part not visible in the repository is the closed Wi-Fi library itself, whose repeated calls on every start are stated by the fix commit message.

fix.subject: arch/xtensa/esp32s3: Don't overrun buffers in SPI poll exchange.
fix.message:
arch/xtensa/esp32s3: Don't overrun buffers in SPI poll exchange.

esp32s3_spi_poll_exchange() moves data to and from the W0-W15 registers
one 32-bit word at a time, always copying a full word. When the transfer
length is not a multiple of 4, the last copy reads up to 3 bytes past the
end of txbuffer and writes up to 3 bytes past the end of rxbuffer,
silently corrupting whatever follows the receive buffer in memory.

Copy only the bytes that remain in the final partial word. Full-word
transfers are unchanged.

Found on an ESP32-S3 board with a Qorvo DW3000 UWB transceiver, SPI DMA
disabled: 125-byte frame reads (64 + 61 bytes per chunk) corrupted the
field following the receive buffer. The fix has been running on a
network of these boards since and the corruption is gone.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5
Signed-off-by: Max Kriegleder <max.kriegleder@gmail.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The fix commit says esp32s3_spi_poll_exchange() always copies a full 32-bit word, so 'When the transfer length is not a multiple of 4, the last copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of txbuffer and writes up to 3 bytes past the end of rxbuffer, silently corrupting whatever follows the receive buffer in memory'; the picked hunk limits the final receive copy to chunk = MIN(sizeof(uint32_t), transfer_size - i). The esp32s2 esp32s2_spi_poll_exchange has the same structure: it computes total_bytes = nwords * (priv->nbits / 8), splits it into chunks of transfer_size = MIN(SPI_MAX_BUF_SIZE, bytes_remaining) with SPI_MAX_BUF_SIZE 64 (16 registers W0-W15), and its receive loop runs i in steps of sizeof(uintptr_t) up to transfer_size and does memcpy(rp, &r_wd, sizeof(uintptr_t)) for every step, so a final chunk whose length is not a multiple of 4 writes up to 3 bytes past the end of rxbuffer. Its transmit loop has the matching over-read (memcpy(&w_wd, tp, sizeof(uint32_t)) for every step), which the esp32s3 commit fixed in its other hunk. The function is reached from esp32s2_spi_exchange whenever SPI DMA is off, and with DMA on for every transfer at or below CONFIG_ESP32S2_SPI_DMATHRESHOLD (default 64), and nothing on the esp32s2 side pads or rounds the caller's buffers. The fix needs only MIN and the existing loop variables, both already used in this function, and esp32s2_spi.c has not been touched since the 2026-10-23 esp32s3 fix except for the exchange return type change.
claude.title: The ESP32-S2 SPI polling exchange writes up to 3 bytes past the end of the receive buffer when the transfer length is not a multiple of 4.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-23 commit 236b47dd0 changed the ESP32-S3 SPI polling exchange to copy only the bytes left in the last partial 32-bit word, after it was found corrupting the field after the receive buffer on a real board. The ESP32-S2 polling exchange is the same code: its receive loop still copies a full 4-byte word on every step, and its transmit loop still reads a full word from the transmit buffer. Any polled SPI transfer whose byte count is not a multiple of 4 (for example a 61-byte or 3-byte read, which goes through this path when DMA is off or the transfer is under the DMA threshold) therefore writes up to 3 bytes past the caller's receive buffer and reads up to 3 bytes past its transmit buffer, silently corrupting nearby memory. The same two-line change per loop applies with only the names changed.

claude.title: The i.MX RT uSDHC driver does not compile with DMA on and the D-cache option off, because it uses priv->rxbuffer outside the CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE guard that declares it.
claude.summary: In August 2024 commit 23e0bf595 fixed a build error in the i.MX9 uSDHC driver: rxbuffer only exists when the data cache is in use, but the DMA preflight check and the receive setup still referred to it. The i.MX RT driver has the same code: rxbuffer is declared only under CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE, yet imxrt_dmapreflight compares the buffer with priv->rxbuffer and imxrt_dmarecvsetup uses sizeof(priv->rxbuffer) in a DEBUGASSERT that is compiled even with assertions off. A configuration with USDHC DMA (default on) and 'Use D-Cache' off (default off) therefore stops with a compile error; the shipped board configurations all enable the D-cache, so only custom configurations hit it. Carrying the fix over means using the imxrt guard CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE instead of CONFIG_ARM64_DCACHE_DISABLE, or declaring rxbuffer for every DMA build.
claude.impact_note: Only a build with USDHC DMA on and the D-cache option off fails to compile, every in-tree imxrt USDHC configuration turns the D-cache on, and the running driver behaves the same.

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit message is 'Get i2c reset improvement from ARM64 driver and fix kconfig entries', and the only picked hunk changes the format string of a debug message in the transfer function from 'len %d' to 'len %ld' for msgs->length; the reset rework and the Kconfig changes are not among the picked hunks. msgs->length is a ssize_t (include/nuttx/i2c/i2c_master.h), and on ARM int and long have the same range (arch/arm/include/limits.h defines INT_MAX as 2147483647 and LONG_MAX as 2147483647L), so the printed value is the same with either conversion and the change at most silences a format warning. claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk is a behavioural fix: the commit message says 'Drop a received packet instead of asserting when no buffer is free to replace the one in the RX descriptor.' pic32mx_rxdone has the same pre-fix logic: it moves the RX buffer to d_buf, takes a replacement with pic32mx_allocbuffer (sq_remfirst on the free list, documented as returning NULL on failure), only checks it with DEBUGASSERT (which compiles to nothing without CONFIG_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS), and then writes PHYS_ADDR(rxbuffer), i.e. address 0, into the descriptor. The buffer pool (NRXDESC + NTXDESC + 1) and pic32mx_bufferinit are the same as in the pre-fix pic32mz, and bufferinit appends every buffer again on each ifup (also called from the TX-timeout work) without emptying the list, which the later pic32mz commit 58b2989c6 says 'truncates the list and loses buffers', so an empty free list is reachable on pic32mx too. Everything the fix uses exists on pic32mx: pic32mx_rxreturn(rxdesc) has the same one-argument form as the pre-fix pic32mz_rxreturn, NETDEV_RXDROPPED is already used in this function, and the driver has no other handling of a failed allocation at this point.

refs.quote: Pointer to the allocated buffer (or NULL on failure)
nwarn("WARNING: No free buffer, packet dropped\n");

claude.title: The pic32mx Ethernet driver asserts, or points the RX DMA at address 0, when no free buffer is left to replace a received one.
claude.summary: In October 2026 the pic32mz Ethernet driver (commit 2851f1c09) stopped asserting when no free buffer is left to replace the one in a completed RX descriptor; it now drops the packet and gives the descriptor back with its current buffer, and the current pic32mz code still does this. pic32mx_rxdone still allocates the replacement with pic32mx_allocbuffer, checks it only with DEBUGASSERT, and writes PHYS_ADDR(rxbuffer) into the descriptor. If the free list is empty, a debug build stops on the assertion, and a release build hands the Ethernet DMA a descriptor that points at address 0, so the next frame is written outside the driver's buffers and that address is later treated as a driver buffer. The free list can run short on pic32mx the same way the later pic32mz commit 58b2989c6 describes, because pic32mx_bufferinit re-appends every buffer on each ifup without emptying the list. Confidence is medium because with an intact free list the pool (one buffer per descriptor plus one) should leave exactly one buffer for this allocation, so the failure depends on that buffer loss or a similar leak.

claude.title: The AT32 WWDG interrupt passes no instance to the watchdog capture callback, so when the IWDG is also registered the auto-monitor stops reloading the WWDG.
claude.summary: In July 2026 commit 2bf7d987 made the common watchdog upper half look up the capture auto-monitor instance from the callback argument, and changed the STM32 WWDG lower halves to pass their own instance (priv) instead of the NULL interrupt argument. at32_wwdg.c still passes arg, which is NULL because its interrupt is attached with a NULL argument. The upper half accepts a NULL argument only when exactly one watchdog is in its capture list, and every registered watchdog is added to that list, so an AT32 build that registers both the IWDG and the WWDG with CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_CAPTURE ignores the WWDG early-wakeup callback and the WWDG resets the board. With only the WWDG registered the NULL argument still resolves and nothing changes, so the impact is limited to that two-watchdog configuration, which is the multi-device case the STM32 change was made for (STM32 also has only an IWDG without a capture callback next to its single WWDG). The one-line change (pass priv) carries over as is.

claude.title: The GD32VW55x WWDGT early-wakeup interrupt passes a NULL context to the watchdog capture callback, so the watchdog core cannot tell which watchdog fired when more than one is registered.
claude.summary: In July 2026 NuttX changed the STM32 WWDG interrupt handlers to pass their own driver instance to the watchdog core's capture callback; the core now looks the watchdog up from that pointer and accepts a NULL pointer only when a single watchdog is in its capture list. The GD32VW55x WWDGT driver follows the same design but still forwards the NULL interrupt argument. Reading the code, with capture-based automonitor and a second watchdog registered (for example the chip's own FWDGT), the WWDGT callback would find no watchdog and skip the keepalive, so the WWDGT would reset the chip; this was not run on hardware. With only the WWDGT registered it behaves as before. The fix is the same one-line change: pass priv instead of arg.

arch/xtensa: Fix esp32s2 SPI errors

Fix esp32s2 SPI DMA and SPI3 errors

Signed-off-by: Eren Terzioglu <eren.terzioglu@espressif.com>

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The picked hunk corrects esp32s2_spi3_config, the SPI3 bus, which had been given the FSPI (SPI2) GPIO-matrix signals; the commit message says 'Fix esp32s2 SPI DMA and SPI3 errors', and the fixed file keeps FSPICS0_IN_IDX and the other FSPI signals in its SPI2 config (esp32s2_spi.c line 325) while using SPI3_CS0_IN_IDX and friends only for SPI3 (line 410). The flagged lines 259-266 in esp32c3_spi.c sit inside esp32c3_spi2_config (line 240), the SPI2 bus with SYSTEM_SPI2_* clock bits, where the FSPI signals are the matching ones, so only the text is the same. The esp32c3-legacy driver has no SPI3 bus at all: its Kconfig offers only ESP32C3_SPI2, the driver defines only esp32c3_spi2_config, and hardware/esp32c3_gpio_sigmap.h defines no SPI3_* signal index. There is therefore nothing for the SPI3 signal fix to apply to.

fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32h7: Fix and enhance WWDG (Window Watchdog) support

This patch addresses several issues and adds enhancements to the WWDG
(Window Watchdog) implementation for the STM32H7 platform. The changes
include:

- Extend the definitions of WWDG_CFR_PCLK1 macros to support dividers
  up to 128, and update the stm32_settimeout() function to consider this
  extended range.
- Fix the "elapsed" calculations in the stm32_getstatus() function to
  ensure correct time remaining calculations.
- Clear the EWIF (Early Wakeup Interrupt Flag) bit in the stm32_start()
  function, as this bit might be set by hardware before the watchdog is
  actually started.
- Initialize the WWDG clock in the RCC_APB3ENR register and set the
  RCC_GCR_WW1RSC bit as per the STM32 reference manual to ensure proper
  behavior when enabling the WWDG1.

Signed-off-by: Szymon Magrian <szymon.magrian@hexagon.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: Two of the three at32_wwdg.c hunks do not apply: dividing WWDG_FMIN by 128 (line 65 here) and stopping the settimeout loop at wdgtb == 7 (line 552) need the STM32H7's 3-bit WDGTB field, while hardware/at32_wdg.h defines only WDGTB[1:0] at bits 8:7 with EWI at bit 9 (lines 117, 124); the at32_iwdg.c pair does not apply either, because the IWDG has no early-wakeup flag (its SR only has PVU/RVU/WVU) and that driver sets .capture = NULL. The remaining hunk, described as 'Clear the EWIF (Early Wakeup Interrupt Flag) bit in the stm32_start() function, as this bit might be set by hardware before the watchdog is actually started', meets the same logic in at32_start: it sets WDGA in WWDG_CR (line 343) without touching WWDG_SR, while at32_capture enables WWDG_CFR_EWI and the IRQ (lines 649, 652) and at32_interrupt calls the user handler whenever WWDG_SR_EWIF is set (lines 291, 302). Everything the fix uses exists on AT32: the header defines WWDG_SR_EWIF as bit 0 of AT32_WWDG_SR (line 128) and the file includes arm_internal.h, which declares modifyreg32. The clear is not tied to the H7 prescaler change: upstream's unified STM32 WWDG driver now does it unconditionally in stm32_start (common/stm32/stm32_wwdg.c line 345), including for the STM32 IP whose WDGTB[1:0] at bits 8:7 layout (common/stm32/hardware/stm32_wdg.h line 157) is the one AT32 uses. The repository does not say whether the AT32 counter itself can set EWIF before WDGA is written, so this rests on the shared register design, hence medium confidence.

claude.title: The AT32 window watchdog is started without clearing a possibly stale early-wakeup flag (EWIF), so the early-warning handler can fire at the wrong time.
claude.summary: In September 2025 (commit 2e85eae6b2ec) the STM32H7 window watchdog driver started clearing the EWIF flag in stm32_start before enabling the watchdog, because the flag can already be set before the watchdog is started; the unified STM32 driver now does the same for every STM32 window watchdog version. The AT32 copy, at32_start in arch/arm/src/at32/at32_wwdg.c, still enables the watchdog straight away without clearing EWIF, while at32_capture enables the early-wakeup interrupt and at32_interrupt calls the user handler whenever EWIF is set. If the flag is stale, the handler can run right away instead of shortly before expiry, and the handler is expected to reload the counter, which causes a reset if a window is configured and the counter is still above it (lines 245-248). Only the one-line flag clear needs porting (modifyreg32(AT32_WWDG_SR, WWDG_SR_EWIF, 0)); the prescaler-range hunks must not be copied because AT32 only has a 2-bit timer base field. The repository does not show whether AT32 hardware can set EWIF before activation, no in-tree board calls at32_wwdginitialize, and outside this candidate at32_getstatus (line 458) still has the pre-fix elapsed formula that the same commit corrected.

fix.subject: esp32/ble: Fix task_create_wrapper CPU core ID passed as argument
fix.message:
esp32/ble: Fix task_create_wrapper CPU core ID passed as argument

The registered `task_create_wrapper` receives the `core_id`, but
the current implementation ignores this parameter while calling
`esp_task_create_pinned_to_core`. This commit fix this.

lines: *   task_handle - Task handle pointer which is used to pause, resume
*   task_handle - Task handle pointer which is used to pause, resume

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The commit says the registered task_create_wrapper 'receives the `core_id`, but the current implementation ignores this parameter while calling `esp_task_create_pinned_to_core`'; on ESP32 this matters because that helper uses core_id under CONFIG_SMP to pin the new thread with nxsched_set_affinity (esp32_ble_adapter.c line 2360-2364), and ARCH_CHIP_ESP32 selects ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU. In esp32c3-legacy the wrapper still passes UINT32_MAX (line 1215), but the local esp_task_create_pinned_to_core (lines 535-560) never reads core_id at all: it only calls kthread_create and stores the pid. ARCH_CHIP_ESP32C3_LEGACY in arch/risc-v/Kconfig does not select ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU, and there is no CONFIG_SMP or nxsched_set_affinity code anywhere under arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3-legacy. Passing core_id instead of UINT32_MAX would therefore change nothing at run time; the fix depends on SMP CPU pinning that this port does not have.

fix.subject: arch/arm/rp23xx: Set priority for svcall exception
fix.message:
arch/arm/rp23xx: Set priority for svcall exception

Fixes https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/15503.

Signed-off-by: Ian Douglas Scott <ian@iandouglasscott.com>

lines: /* Attach the SVCall and Hard Fault exception handlers.  The SVCall
* exception is used for performing context switches; The Hard Fault
* must also be caught because a SVCall may show up as a Hard Fault
/* Attach all other processor exceptions (except reset and sys tick) */
/* Attach the SVCall and Hard Fault exception handlers.  The SVCall
* exception is used for performing context switches; The Hard Fault
* must also be caught because a SVCall may show up as a Hard Fault
/* Attach all other processor exceptions (except reset and sys tick) */

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The commit ('Set priority for svcall exception') adds rp23xx_prioritize_syscall(NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY) to up_irqinitialize; rp23xx selects ARCH_CORTEXM33 (ARMv8-M), whose up_irq_save masks interrupts by raising BASEPRI to NVIC_SYSH_DISABLE_PRIORITY (armv8-m/irq.h line 371), so SVCall has to be placed one step above that level (armv8-m/nvicpri.h line 76) or an SVC made with interrupts masked becomes a Hard Fault, which the armv8-m arm_hardfault does not forward. kl_irq.c attaches the same SVCall and Hard Fault handlers (lines 200-201) without setting an SVCall priority, but ARCH_CHIP_KL selects ARCH_CORTEXM0, which selects ARCH_ARMV6M (arch/arm/Kconfig lines 263 and 1150). On ARMv6-M, up_irq_save disables interrupts with PRIMASK ('cpsid  i', armv6-m/irq.h line 257), which blocks SVCall whatever its priority, and the armv6-m arm_hardfault forwards an escalated 'svc 0' to arm_svcall (arm_hardfault.c lines 107-110), exactly as the comment at kl_irq.c line 196 describes. NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY is defined only in the armv7-m and armv8-m nvicpri.h headers, and none of the ARMv6-M ports (kl, nuc1xx, rp2040, samd2l2, s32k11x, common/stm32/stm32_irq_m0_v1.c) set it while their ARMv7/8-M siblings do (for example s32k14x_irq.c line 357), so the fix depends on BASEPRI masking that this core lacks.

fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32h7: remove non-existent QSPI_CR_DMAEN references
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32h7: remove non-existent QSPI_CR_DMAEN references

In STM32H7 (RM0433), QUADSPI_CR Bit 2 is reserved and does not contain a DMAEN bit (unlike STM32F7/L4). DMA requests are generated automatically by hardware based on the FIFO threshold.

This commit removes all references to QSPI_CR_DMAEN in stm32_qspi.c, fixing compilation failure when CONFIG_STM32_QSPI_DMA is enabled.

Fixes: #16366

Signed-off-by: Sarthak Pandey <sarthak@email.com>

lines: /* this extra verbose output may be helpful in some cases; you'll need
* to make sure your syslog is large enough to accommodate extra output.
spiinfo("  EN:%1d ABORT:%1d DMAEN:%1d TCEN:%1d SSHIFT:%1d\n"
"  TEIE:%1d TCIE:%1d FTIE:%1d SMIE:%1d TOIE:%1d APMS:%1d PMM:%1d\n"
/* this extra verbose output may be helpful in some cases; you'll need
* to make sure your syslog is large enough to accommodate the extra
spiinfo("  EN:%1d ABORT:%1d DMAEN:%1d TCEN:%1d SSHIFT:%1d\n"
"  TEIE:%1d TCIE:%1d FTIE:%1d SMIE:%1d TOIE:%1d APMS:%1d PMM:%1d\n"

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit ('remove non-existent QSPI_CR_DMAEN references') fixes an H7 'compilation failure when CONFIG_STM32_QSPI_DMA is enabled', but the only hunk picked out is the control-register print in qspi_dumpregs, which in stm32h7 sits inside an '#if 0' block (stm32h7/stm32_qspi.c line 501, with its '#else' at line 563 at the pinned commit, and the same layout before the fix), so it was never compiled; changing it fixes neither run-time behaviour nor the build and only edits dead logging code. The functional H7 changes (dropping the QSPI_CR_DMAEN writes in qspi_memory_dma) are not among the picked hunks. In stm32f7 the same print (lines 485 and 491) is likewise inside '#if 0' (line 477, '#else' at line 539), and here QSPI_CR_DMAEN is a real bit: the F7 header defines it as (1 << 2) with the comment 'DMA enable' (hardware/stm32_qspi.h line 82), whereas the H7 header goes straight from QSPI_CR_ABORT to QSPI_CR_TCEN, and F7 really sets it in qspi_memory_dma (line 1483). The picked hunk is therefore a logging cleanup, and even as live code the F7 print would build and report an existing bit.

fix.subject: arch/arm/imx9: irq: replace hardcoded NVIC register lists with loops.
fix.message:
arch/arm/imx9: irq: replace hardcoded NVIC register lists with loops.

Use NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(n) and NVIC_IRQ_PRIORITY(n) macros in
imx9_dumpnvic() to iterate over all NVIC registers programmatically
based on CONFIG_ARCH_NINTS (IMX9_IRQ_NEXTINT), rather than
enumerating named per-range register defines. Output is grouped
4-per-line for priority and 4-per-line for enable registers,
matching the original layout.
This avoids accessing registers which don't exist when extending
the interrupt count.

Also replace named NVIC_IRQxx_yy_ENABLE constants in imx9_irqinfo()
with NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(n), avoiding naming conflicts between chips
with different IRQ counts.

Fix the upper boundary in the >192 IRQ branch from 219 to 224 to
align with the 32-interrupt register granularity.

Change %08x to %08lx to silence warnings from the compiler for
the debug dump.

No functional change for existing i.MX95-M7 builds.

Signed-off-by: Maarten Zanders <maarten@zanders.be>

lines: static void imx9_dumpnvic(const char *msg, int irq)
irqinfo("  SYSH ENABLE MEMFAULT: %08x BUSFAULT: %08x USGFAULT: %08x "
(40 more lines in this hunk, not shown)
static void at32_dumpnvic(const char *msg, int irq)
irqinfo("  SYSH ENABLE MEMFAULT: %08x BUSFAULT: %08x USGFAULT: %08x "

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The only hunk picked out for this pair changes one debug print in imx9_dumpnvic from %08x to %08lx, and the commit message says this was done "to silence warnings from the compiler for the debug dump" and that there is "No functional change for existing i.MX95-M7 builds." The matching at32 line 85 is the same INTCTRL/VECTAB print inside at32_dumpnvic, which is compiled only under CONFIG_DEBUG_IRQ_INFO (line 77) and logs through irqinfo, a macro that is a no-op unless CONFIG_DEBUG_IRQ_INFO is set (include/nuttx/debug.h). The printed values come from getreg32, a uint32_t read, and the shared arch/arm/include/types.h may make uint32_t an unsigned long while noting that sizes are 4 bytes, so %08x only draws a compiler format warning and the printed value does not change. A log-format change that only silences a warning is not a behavioural fix, so nothing was missed on at32.

Use NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(n) and NVIC_IRQ_PRIORITY(n) macros in
imx9_dumpnvic() to iterate over all NVIC registers programmatically
based on CONFIG_ARCH_NINTS (IMX9_IRQ_NEXTINT), rather than
enumerating named per-range register defines. Output is grouped
4-per-line for priority and 4-per-line for enable registers,
matching the original layout.
This avoids accessing registers which don't exist when extending
the interrupt count.

Also replace named NVIC_IRQxx_yy_ENABLE constants in imx9_irqinfo()
with NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(n), avoiding naming conflicts between chips
with different IRQ counts.

Fix the upper boundary in the >192 IRQ branch from 219 to 224 to
align with the 32-interrupt register granularity.

Change %08x to %08lx to silence warnings from the compiler for
the debug dump.

No functional change for existing i.MX95-M7 builds.

Signed-off-by: Maarten Zanders <maarten@zanders.be>

The matching line 84 on the nrf52 side is in nrf52_dumpnvic(), which is compiled only under CONFIG_DEBUG_IRQ_INFO and only prints NVIC registers through irqinfo; the rest of that function prints a fixed list of named registers (line 94 onward), so the new locals would have no use there. getreg32() reads a volatile uint32_t, and arch/arm/include/types.h makes uint32_t either the compiler's __UINT32_TYPE__ or unsigned long while stating that size_t (unsigned int or unsigned long) is 4 bytes, so %08x and %08lx print the same 32-bit value and the only difference is a format-type warning. The listed hunk therefore only silences a compiler warning in debug output and changes no runtime behaviour, so it is not a bug fix.

fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32h5: Fix ADC interrupt dispatch
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32h5: Fix ADC interrupt dispatch

Only handle ADC interrupts that are enabled in IER, so a shared
interrupt no longer services flags of an ADC that did not raise it.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5
Signed-off-by: Darryl Ring <darryl@bluerobotics.com>

lines: static int adc12_interrupt(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
static int adc12_interrupt(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
static int adc3_interrupt(int irq, void *context, void *arg)

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk changes the ADC1/ADC2 dispatcher adc12_interrupt so that each ADC is serviced only for flags that are set in its ISR and enabled in its IER, and passes that masked value to adc_interrupt instead of the raw ISR; the commit message says 'Only handle ADC interrupts that are enabled in IER, so a shared interrupt no longer services flags of an ADC that did not raise it'. The STM32H7 adc12_interrupt is the same pre-fix code (pending = regval & ADC_INT_MASK at lines 2174/2183, adc_interrupt(&g_adcdevN, regval) at 2177/2186), and on H7 ADC1 and ADC2 really share one vector (both have .irq = STM32_IRQ_ADC12). Flags are set there without being enabled: the ANIOC_WDOG_UPPER/LOWER ioctls call adc_wdog_enable, which turns on continuous conversion and removes ADC_INT_EOC from IER, and adc_rxint(false) clears all IER bits, while the H7 adc_interrupt, like the H5 one, acts on every bit it is given (its EOC branch reads DR and calls au_receive). So an interrupt from the other ADC, or the ADC's own AWD1 interrupt in watchdog mode, still runs the EOC path for an ADC whose EOC interrupt is disabled. The registers the fix reads exist on H7 (STM32_ADC1_IER and STM32_ADC2_IER in hardware/stm32_adc.h), so the change applies as written; the unshared adc3_interrupt (line 2213) has the same pattern but was not part of the H5 change.
claude.title: The STM32H7 ADC1/ADC2 shared interrupt handler acts on status flags that are not enabled in IER, so it can read data and report samples for an ADC whose interrupt is disabled.
claude.summary: In November 2026 commit 39572c4 changed the STM32H5 adc12_interrupt to mask each ADC's ISR with its IER and to pass only those bits to adc_interrupt, so the shared handler no longer services flags of an ADC that did not raise the interrupt. The STM32H7 adc12_interrupt still computes ISR & ADC_INT_MASK and passes the raw ISR, although on H7 ADC1 and ADC2 share the single vector STM32_IRQ_ADC12. When one ADC is in watchdog mode (EOC removed from IER while it converts continuously) or has its interrupts disabled, any interrupt on the shared vector, or its own watchdog interrupt, still runs the end-of-conversion path for it: the handler reads its data register and pushes samples to its upper half that the driver had switched off. Adding the IER mask to both pending computations and passing pending instead of regval, as in the H5 driver, fixes it.

fix.subject: esp_i2s: fix I2S RX DMA path for ESP32-S3
fix.message:
esp_i2s: fix I2S RX DMA path for ESP32-S3

Fix multiple bugs in the I2S RX receive path on ESP32-S3 with GDMA:

- Set streaming=true in i2s_rxdma_start so completed buffers are not
  incorrectly marked AUDIO_APB_FINAL
- Restore up_enable_irq calls for DMA interrupt after esp_dma_load
  resets the channel
- Skip i2s_hal_rx_reset/rx_reset_fifo on ESP32-S3 which clears the
  TDM slot configuration set by i2s_configure
- Accept 1-16 RX channels on ESP32-S3 (was limited to 2)
- Add getreg32 read-back after DMA start to flush CPU write buffer
- Auto-stop RX channel when no pending buffers remain, preventing
  hardware from running without DMA descriptors after stop
- Remove duplicate return OK in i2s_rxdma_start
- Fix i2s_ll_tx_enable_mono_mode to i2s_ll_rx_enable_mono_mode in
  i2s_rxchannels
- Fix tx_slot_cfg.std to rx_slot_cfg.std in RX PCM slot config
- Fix DMA direction, peripheral ID, data_width, rx_start sequencing,
  and rx_eof_num word count in RX path
- Fix esp32s3_board_i2s.c I2S port index

Signed-off-by: wangjianyu3 <wangjianyu3@xiaomi.com>

lines: /* If there is already an active transmission in progress, then bail
/* If there are no pending transfer, then bail returning success */
/* Mark as streaming so that completed buffers are not flagged as FINAL.
* When I2S is used as a transport for a codec (e.g. ES7210), the codec
* receives AUDIOIOC_START but does not forward it to I2S, so streaming
* would remain false and the first completed buffer would be marked
* AUDIO_APB_FINAL, causing nxrecorder to stop prematurely.
/* If there isn't already an active transmission in progress,
/* rx_eof_num: on ESP32-S3 with GDMA, the I2S peripheral has an internal
* RX bit counter.  When it reaches (RX_BITS_MOD+1)*(RX_EOF_NUM+1) bits,
* it signals SUC_EOF to the GDMA.  So RX_EOF_NUM is a *sample count*,
* not a byte count.  Convert buffer bytes → sample count:
/* Full channel stop + start to reinitialize I2S RX and DMA.
* This is required because the I2S RX byte counter does not
* auto-reset after SUC_EOF — only RX_RESET clears it.
* channel_start does: DMA reset → RX_RESET → FIFO_RESET →
* rx_update (re-applies slot config) → enable IRQ + SUC_EOF.
/* Set RXEOF_NUM (sample count) and latch via rx_update */
/* Flush descriptor cache lines before DMA reads them */
* esp_dma_load does DMA_IN_RST which clears DMA_IN_INT_ENA_CH0,
* so we must re-enable the SUC_EOF interrupt after loading.
/* Add container to active queue before starting RX */
/* Start RX — this starts BCLK/WS clocks (master mode) */
*   Setup the next TX DMA transfer

claude.evidence: The commit ('Decode saved M0 USB setup requests') moves the decoding of value/index/len out of the first-entry branch of stm32_ep0setup so that, in its words, 'the fields are initialized when the EP0 handler is entered again to complete an OUT control transfer', which 'also fixes Clang builds that treat the resulting maybe-uninitialized diagnostics as errors'. The fix can be copied over unchanged.

fix.subject: arch/mips/pic32mz: fix the Ethernet RX descriptor ring handling.
fix.message:
arch/mips/pic32mz: fix the Ethernet RX descriptor ring handling.

Under load the RX path delivered frames out of order, lost responses and
stopped receiving for good after an RX overflow, until ifdown/ifup:

- ETHSTAT.BUFCNT was decremented (BUFCDEC) before the descriptor was
  given back to the hardware.  When the RX DMA has stopped on a
  descriptor because none was available, the decrement makes it fetch
  that descriptor again; at that time it was still owned by software,
  so the reception stalled.  BUFCDEC is now written after the
  descriptor is returned, with EOWN set.
- pic32mz_rxdesc() returned the first software owned descriptor of the
  array instead of the next one in ring order, so frames could be
  delivered out of order.  A ring index (pd_rxnext) is now kept.
- When no TX descriptor was available for a response, the response was
  left pending in d_buf, but pic32mz_rxdone() kept receiving into d_buf
  and then freed it.  RX processing now stops while a response is
  pending and resumes after pic32mz_txdone() sends it.  txavail no
  longer polls over a pending response, and ifup drops it.
- The RX descriptors are also processed on RX overflow and buffer not
  available events, so that they are given back to the hardware.

Tested on an EV49N51A derived board (PIC32MZ-W1, 100 Mbit/s full

claude.evidence: The listed hunks belong to the pic32mz commit 'fix the Ethernet RX descriptor ring handling', which says pic32mz_rxdesc() 'returned the first software owned descriptor of the array instead of the next one in ring order, so frames could be delivered out of order' (hunks 1-2 add the ring index pd_rxnext and pass priv to rxreturn so it can advance it), that rxdone 'kept receiving into d_buf and then freed it' while a response was pending (hunk 4 is the txavail part of that fix), and that RX descriptors are now also processed on RX overflow and buffer-not-available events (hunk 3). pic32mx has the same pre-fix ring logic: pic32mx_rxdesc still scans the array from index 0 (lines 965, 969) although pic32mx_rxdescinit links the RX descriptors into a ring (line 810), the driver struct has only pd_txnext (line 302) and pic32mx_rxreturn takes no priv (line 367), so frames can be taken out of order once the hardware wraps around. claude.title: The pic32mx Ethernet driver takes received frames out of ring order and loses responses that are waiting for a free TX descriptor.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-10 the pic32mz Ethernet driver fixed its RX path: it now takes RX descriptors in ring order using a ring index, stops receiving while a response waits for a free TX descriptor (and txavail no longer polls over that response), and also processes RX descriptors on overflow and buffer-not-available events. The pic32mx driver, which has the same structure, still scans its RX descriptor ring from index 0 in pic32mx_rxdesc, keeps receiving after pic32mx_response has marked a response as pending and then frees that response's buffer, and reacts only to RXDONE. Under load this can deliver frames out of order and lose responses, and with assertions enabled pic32mx_transmit asserts when txdone sends the pending packet with a NULL buffer. The patch has to be adapted rather than copied: pic32mx never decrements BUFCNT in its RX path, so the BUFCDEC reordering does not carry over and the effect of the overflow-event hunk on pic32mx is not shown by the code, and nothing here was tested on PIC32MX hardware.

fix.subject: arch/risc-v/gd32vw55x: add the deep-sleep power management
fix.message:
arch/risc-v/gd32vw55x: add the deep-sleep power management

With CONFIG_PM, the PM_STANDBY state of the IDLE domain is the PMU
deep-sleep mode: the core and bus clocks stop, SRAM and registers keep
their contents, the LDO runs in low power and low-driver mode.

- idle: custom up_idle() that runs the PM state machine; PM_STANDBY
  enters deep-sleep and goes back to PM_NORMAL on wake-up.  Otherwise
  the core waits for an interrupt, as the common up_idle() does.
- pm: riscv_pminitialize() keeps the debugger connection in deep-sleep
  (DBG_CTL0 DSLP_HOLD).  gd32vw55x_pmstop() sleeps until the next alarm
  of the system timer, at most CONFIG_GD32VW55X_PM_WAKEUP_MS, waits on
  WFI with the SLEEPVALUE CSR set, sets the PLL up again and advances
  the system timer, stopped in deep-sleep, by the time spent asleep.
- rtc: the wake-up timer (RTC clock / 16, EXTI line 21) ends the sleep.
  The time asleep is measured on the calendar counters, bypassing the
  shadow registers, which are not updated in deep-sleep; both readings
  are taken at the start of a sub-second unit, since the wake-up comes
  at a fixed point of a unit.  The asynchronous prescaler is lowered to
  2, for units of about 60 us.
- serial: received characters are reported as PM activity.
- boards/gd32vw553k-start: new pm configuration, NSH with the power
  management (activity governor), the RTC and the PM procfs entries,
  and its documentation.

Tested on the GD32VW553K-START: 78 to 93 percent of the idle time in
deep-sleep, NSH answers the first key, "sleep 3" lasts 3.00 s, and the
system time follows the IRC32K while the chip sleeps: 600 ppm off over
2 minutes of standby.
