fix.subject: arch/arm: Bound SDMMC/SDIO command response wait by time
fix.message:
arch/arm: Bound SDMMC/SDIO command response wait by time

Follow up on commit 62b41ad9b4 to fix the same SDMMC/SDIO polling
timeout starvation issue across the remaining STM32 families and clone
architectures (stm32f7, stm32h5, stm32h7, stm32l4, at32, gd32f4).

The command waitresponse functions previously polled the status register
bounded only by an iteration counter (up to 0x7fffffff iterations).
If the card clock stops or the peripheral freezes, the hardware CTIMEOUT
flag is never generated and the loop spins for INT32_MAX iterations
while holding the filesystem lock, causing high CPU load and starving
lower-priority threads.

Bound the wait by time using clock_systime_ticks(): 250 ms for
response-bearing commands (the maximum timeout allowed by the SD
physical layer specification) and 10 ms for no-response/R3/R7 commands.

Fixes #19792

Signed-off-by: Swatantra Yadav <maverickswatantra@gmail.com>

* when the command response is received.  If this status bit is 0, it

* SD/MMC Command using the CMD line. CIHB should always be clear before
* this function is called, but this check is performed here to provide
/* Then wait for the Command Complete (CC) indication (or timeout).  The
* CC bit is set when the end bit of the command response is received

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The commit replaces the iteration-counter bound of stm32_waitresponse (SDMMC_CMDTIMEOUT 100000 and SDMMC_LONGTIMEOUT 0x7fffffff loop passes) with a time bound, in its words 'Bound the wait by time using clock_systime_ticks(): 250 ms for response-bearing commands ... and 10 ms for no-response/R3/R7 commands'. The sama5 lines that match ('timeout = SDMMC_CMDTIMEOUT;' at lines 2256, 2521 and 2540) only share the text: in sam_sdmmc.c these macros are already tick counts, MSEC2TICK(100) and MSEC2TICK(500) (lines 99-100), and timeout is a clock_t (line 2509). sam_waitresponse takes start = clock_systime_ticks() (line 2554) and leaves the loop with -ETIMEDOUT once clock_systime_ticks() - start reaches the timeout (lines 2559-2560), and the CIHB wait in sam_sendcmd is bounded by elapsed ticks in the same way (lines 2256-2264). So sama5 already bounds the command-response wait by time, only with other limits (100 ms and 500 ms instead of 10 ms and 250 ms), and cannot spin for INT32_MAX iterations the way the fixed drivers could.

fix.subject: arch/arm/rp23xx: Fix PWM frequency and duty cycle calculation.
fix.message:
arch/arm/rp23xx: Fix PWM frequency and duty cycle calculation.

Fixed three bugs in the RP23XX PWM driver:

* setup_period: The previous divisor calculation used integer arithmetic
  that caused overflow and loss of precision. The divider is now computed
  as a 16-bit fixed-point value (div16) using 64-bit arithmetic, and
  clamped to the valid hardware range (0x10 to 0xFFF).

* setup_pulse: The compare value was incorrectly scaled by TOP instead
  of 65535, producing wrong duty cycles. The formula is now corrected
  to ((duty * (top + 1)) / 65535) with an overflow guard.

* pwm_start: The driver was not updated as part of the breaking change
  introduced in commit 4df80e19 ("!drivers/pwm: remove PWM_MULTICHAN
  option"). Access to single channel API is now info->channels[0].duty
  instead of info[0].duty.

Signed-off-by: Brunocor26 <bruno.correia@ubi.pt>

claude.title: The RP2040 PWM driver still computes the clock divider and duty-cycle compare values wrongly, and its single-channel build still uses a removed field, the same three bugs fixed in the RP23XX copy.
claude.summary: On 2026-05-25 commit 53ef7c06 fixed three bugs in the RP23XX PWM driver: the period/divider math, the duty-cycle compare formula, and pwm_start still reading info[0].duty after struct pwm_info_s lost its duty member. The RP2040 driver is the same code on the same register layout and still has all three pre-fix versions; it has not been touched since 2026-04-07. With the Pico's 125 MHz clock, almost any requested frequency above about 1.9 kHz gets a divider whose integer part is 0, from about 3.8 kHz the compare value is too large by 65535/TOP so duty cycles come out wrong (larger duties exceed TOP or spill into the channel-B field), and below about 7.5 Hz the divider overflows its 12-bit field. With the default single-channel setting (CONFIG_PWM_NCHANNELS=1) the file does not compile at all. The fix can be copied with only the rp23xx/RP23XX names changed; what the hardware does with an integer divider of 0 is not visible in the repository, but the RP23XX fix treats 0x10 to 0xFFF as the valid range.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/imxrt: Fix FlexCAN TX timeout aborting live mailboxes.
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/imxrt: Fix FlexCAN TX timeout aborting live mailboxes.

imxrt_txtimeout_work() had four defects that together let one expired frame
take the interface down permanently.

It aborted mailbox RXMBCOUNT + mbi while the deadline it consulted belongs to
RXMBCOUNT + 1 + mbi, so every abort landed one mailbox low and mbi == 0 wrote
CAN_TXMB_ABORT into the buffer reserved for the ERR005829 workaround, while
the highest TX mailbox was never aborted at all.

Its expiry test read `now.tv_sec > d.tv_sec || now.tv_usec > d.tv_usec`, which
declares any deadline that crosses a second boundary expired: in that case the
deadline's microsecond field is always the smaller of the two. The `now` it
compared against was a struct timespec cast to a struct timeval, so writing
tv_usec wrote over tv_nsec and tv_sec was whatever the cast happened to line
up with.

imxrt_txdone() cancelled the watchdog but left txmb[].deadline set, so a
retired mailbox looked expired forever and the next watchdog expiry on any
other mailbox aborted whatever frame had since been loaded there.

The walk ran to TXMBCOUNT, which counts the reserved mailbox as well, so its
last iteration addressed mailbox TOTALMBCOUNT - one past the ring, and
mb_address[] one past its end. Only txmb[] never being written that far kept
it in bounds. TXMBRINGSIZE now names the ring size that the rest of the driver
already assumes.

Aborting a frame that is already on the wire raises a bit error, so the
transmit error counter climbs and the node goes error passive. Since
imxrt_txmb_next() only hands out a mailbox above every pending one, a mailbox
left in DATAORREMOTE also pins the allocator at TOTALMBCOUNT and transmit
never recovers.

Measured on an ARK FMU-v6XRT with a DroneCAN GNSS node on the bus, offering
736 frames/s (9% of a 1 Mbit/s bus) from the PX4 uavcan driver: before, the
interface transmitted 0 frames/s with ECR[TXERRCNT] pinned at 128 and
ESR1[FLTCONF] error passive, and stayed dead across a reboot. After, 734
frames/s, 0.1% loss, TXERRCNT 0, error active.

Signed-off-by: Jacob Dahl <dahl.jakejacob@gmail.com>

claude.title: The i.MX9 FlexCAN TX-deadline timeout handler still aborts the mailbox next to the one that timed out and treats unexpired or already-sent frames as expired, the bugs just fixed in the i.MX RT copy.
claude.summary: On 2026-08-27 commit 58181135 fixed the i.MX RT FlexCAN TX-deadline timeout handling (active when CONFIG_NET_CAN_RAW_TX_DEADLINE is set): the timeout work now aborts mailbox RXMBCOUNT + 1 + mbi, the one whose deadline it checked, compares seconds before microseconds, walks only the real TX ring, and txdone clears the deadline of a finished mailbox. imx9_flexcan.c is a copy of the same driver and still has all of the pre-fix code: deadlines are stored for mailbox RXMBCOUNT + 1 + k but the abort goes to RXMBCOUNT + k, the expiry test fires whenever the current microseconds exceed the deadline's, and finished mailboxes keep their old deadline. When any TX watchdog fires, frames whose deadline has not passed can be aborted, finished mailboxes look expired forever, the abort lands on a neighbouring TX mailbox (possibly one still sending) or on the mailbox reserved for the ER005829 workaround, and the last TX mailbox is never aborted; the commit message reports that on i.MX RT this drove the node error passive and stopped transmission. The imx9 transmit path picks the first free mailbox rather than one above all pending ones, so the permanent allocator lock-up described for i.MX RT may play out differently, but the wrong aborts apply unchanged; the whole commit (including the TXMBRINGSIZE define and the txdone deadline reset) can be copied with only the imxrt/IMXRT names changed.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/imxrt: Fix FlexCAN TX timeout aborting live mailboxes.
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/imxrt: Fix FlexCAN TX timeout aborting live mailboxes.

imxrt_txtimeout_work() had four defects that together let one expired frame
take the interface down permanently.

It aborted mailbox RXMBCOUNT + mbi while the deadline it consulted belongs to
RXMBCOUNT + 1 + mbi, so every abort landed one mailbox low and mbi == 0 wrote
CAN_TXMB_ABORT into the buffer reserved for the ERR005829 workaround, while
the highest TX mailbox was never aborted at all.

Its expiry test read `now.tv_sec > d.tv_sec || now.tv_usec > d.tv_usec`, which
declares any deadline that crosses a second boundary expired: in that case the
deadline's microsecond field is always the smaller of the two. The `now` it
compared against was a struct timespec cast to a struct timeval, so writing
tv_usec wrote over tv_nsec and tv_sec was whatever the cast happened to line
up with.

imxrt_txdone() cancelled the watchdog but left txmb[].deadline set, so a
retired mailbox looked expired forever and the next watchdog expiry on any
other mailbox aborted whatever frame had since been loaded there.

The walk ran to TXMBCOUNT, which counts the reserved mailbox as well, so its
last iteration addressed mailbox TOTALMBCOUNT - one past the ring, and
mb_address[] one past its end. Only txmb[] never being written that far kept
it in bounds. TXMBRINGSIZE now names the ring size that the rest of the driver
already assumes.

Aborting a frame that is already on the wire raises a bit error, so the
transmit error counter climbs and the node goes error passive. Since
imxrt_txmb_next() only hands out a mailbox above every pending one, a mailbox
left in DATAORREMOTE also pins the allocator at TOTALMBCOUNT and transmit
never recovers.

Measured on an ARK FMU-v6XRT with a DroneCAN GNSS node on the bus, offering
736 frames/s (9% of a 1 Mbit/s bus) from the PX4 uavcan driver: before, the
interface transmitted 0 frames/s with ECR[TXERRCNT] pinned at 128 and
ESR1[FLTCONF] error passive, and stayed dead across a reboot. After, 734
frames/s, 0.1% loss, TXERRCNT 0, error active.

claude.evidence: None of the three picked hunks changes behaviour by itself. Two shrink txtimeout[] and txmb[] from TXMBCOUNT to TXMBRINGSIZE (TXMBCOUNT - 1), which only fits imxrt, where TXMBCOUNT is CONFIG_IMXRT_FLEXCAN_TXMB + 1 and includes the mailbox reserved for the ERR005829 workaround (its IFLAG1_TX uses -2); kinetis has no reserved mailbox (TXMBCOUNT is 5, IFLAG1_TX uses -1, priv->tx starts at mailbox RXMBCOUNT, and kinetis_transmit uses txmb[mbi] and txtimeout[mbi] for every mbi < TXMBCOUNT), so its arrays already equal the ring size. The third replaces the cast 'struct timeval *now = (struct timeval *)&ts' with a separate struct, but at the pinned commit struct timeval is {time_t tv_sec; long tv_usec;} (include/sys/types.h) and struct timespec is {time_t tv_sec; long tv_nsec;} (include/time.h), so now->tv_sec is exactly ts.tv_sec and now->tv_usec gets the right microseconds, and NuttX builds with -fno-strict-aliasing; the value of now is the same before and after. claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk adds writes of 0 to CCR1-CCR4 at the end of the stm32f7 pwm_stop, after the counter and the outputs are disabled; the commit message says 'when executing pwm STOP command in multichannel mode, the channel still outputting. This commit fixes this issue.', and the same block is present in the pwm_stop of stm32h7 and stm32h5 at the pinned commit. The at32 pwm_stop (lines 3698-3733) is the pre-fix copy: it zeroes DIER and SR, calls pwm_timer_enable(dev, false), takes the outputs from pwm_outputs_from_channels and calls pwm_outputs_enable(dev, outputs, false), then leaves the critical section without touching the compare registers; its helpers pwm_timer_enable, pwm_outputs_from_channels and pwm_outputs_enable have the same bodies as on stm32f7 (the other matched lines, 3021/3025 and 3260, are only the same text inside pwm_configure and pwm_timer). claude.title: The at32 PWM stop routine leaves the CCR1-CCR4 compare registers set, which stm32f7 started clearing because a channel kept outputting after a STOP in multichannel mode.
claude.summary: In February 2024 (commit 5975b259) stm32f7's pwm_stop gained four writes of 0 to CCR1-CCR4 after the counter and outputs are disabled, because 'when executing pwm STOP command in multichannel mode, the channel still outputting'; stm32h7 and stm32h5 carry the same block at the pinned commit. fix.subject: arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support
fix.message:
arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support

Adds the Data Transfer Controller (DTC) as a generic register-triggered
DMA engine (ra_dtc.c/.h, hardware/ra8m1_dtc.h, CONFIG_RA_DTC, normal
mode only), and generalizes SCI_B's 16-stage FIFO and DTC support from
SCI9-only to every instance (SCI0-4, SCI9): CONFIG_RA_SCIn_FIFO and
CONFIG_RA_SCIn_TXDTC/RXDTC are mutually exclusive, not combinable --
TX DTC moves queued ring-buffer data in the background through
CONFIG_SERIAL_TXDMA, RX DTC moves each byte as it arrives, and measured
on hardware the FIFO's standing multi-byte buffer gives far better
high-baud overrun margin than this one-byte-per-activation RX DTC
design, which also had a real arming bug fixed here (up_rxint()'s old
"first enable" check could never fire, so the DTC was never armed),
alongside a FIFO register-clear/ordering fix.  up_ioctl() also gains
TCGETS/TCSETS (baud rate, parity, stop bits), board.h gains SCI0's
GPIO pins (P609/P610) to exercise it on this board, and comments
throughout ra_serial.c/Kconfig are condensed from the narrative
debugging form they accumulated down to the essential fact each one
needs.  Tested on hardware: SCI0 and SCI9 simultaneously, FIFO and DTC
independently and mutually exclusive; FIFO (TTRG=15/RTRG=0) holds up
cleanly to 3 Mbps for transfers within the RX ring buffer, well past
RX DTC's ceiling (see below).

A separate, more serious bug was also found and fixed while hardware-
testing the overrun path at high baud: up_erinterrupt() never cleared
its ICU IELSRn.IR flag (RA8M1 User's Manual section 13.5.1 is explicit
that this causes the NVIC to re-enter the handler indefinitely), which
livelocked the whole system on any receive error, in every
configuration, not something specific to this series.  Fixed by
clearing it like the other two SCI interrupt handlers already did, by
draining RDR/the FIFO on an error before clearing it (SCIn_ERI fires
instead of SCIn_RXI for every receive error, so data already received
was otherwise never picked up), and by having the RX DTC path also
recognize a byte stuck via CSR.RDRF directly, not just its own
bookkeeping, since its event can be silently dropped by the ICU while
an earlier byte's IR is still pending.  Also added CONFIG_SERIAL_
TIOCGICOUNT (frame/overrun/parity counters via the standard
TIOCGICOUNT ioctl), matching stm32's precedent, since nothing in the
generic NuttX serial core surfaces a receive error to an application
otherwise.  Confirmed on hardware: nsh on SCI9 stays fully responsive
through a sustained 3 Mbps overrun on SCI0 that previously froze the
whole board.

fix.subject: arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support
fix.message:
arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support

Adds the Data Transfer Controller (DTC) as a generic register-triggered
DMA engine (ra_dtc.c/.h, hardware/ra8m1_dtc.h, CONFIG_RA_DTC, normal
mode only), and generalizes SCI_B's 16-stage FIFO and DTC support from
SCI9-only to every instance (SCI0-4, SCI9): CONFIG_RA_SCIn_FIFO and
CONFIG_RA_SCIn_TXDTC/RXDTC are mutually exclusive, not combinable --
TX DTC moves queued ring-buffer data in the background through
CONFIG_SERIAL_TXDMA, RX DTC moves each byte as it arrives, and measured
on hardware the FIFO's standing multi-byte buffer gives far better
high-baud overrun margin than this one-byte-per-activation RX DTC
design, which also had a real arming bug fixed here (up_rxint()'s old
"first enable" check could never fire, so the DTC was never armed),
alongside a FIFO register-clear/ordering fix.  up_ioctl() also gains
TCGETS/TCSETS (baud rate, parity, stop bits), board.h gains SCI0's
GPIO pins (P609/P610) to exercise it on this board, and comments
throughout ra_serial.c/Kconfig are condensed from the narrative
debugging form they accumulated down to the essential fact each one
needs.  Tested on hardware: SCI0 and SCI9 simultaneously, FIFO and DTC
independently and mutually exclusive; FIFO (TTRG=15/RTRG=0) holds up
cleanly to 3 Mbps for transfers within the RX ring buffer, well past
RX DTC's ceiling (see below).

A separate, more serious bug was also found and fixed while hardware-
testing the overrun path at high baud: up_erinterrupt() never cleared
its ICU IELSRn.IR flag (RA8M1 User's Manual section 13.5.1 is explicit
that this causes the NVIC to re-enter the handler indefinitely), which
livelocked the whole system on any receive error, in every
configuration, not something specific to this series.  Fixed by
clearing it like the other two SCI interrupt handlers already did, by
draining RDR/the FIFO on an error before clearing it (SCIn_ERI fires
instead of SCIn_RXI for every receive error, so data already received
was otherwise never picked up), and by having the RX DTC path also
recognize a byte stuck via CSR.RDRF directly, not just its own
bookkeeping, since its event can be silently dropped by the ICU while
an earlier byte's IR is still pending.  Also added CONFIG_SERIAL_
TIOCGICOUNT (frame/overrun/parity counters via the standard
TIOCGICOUNT ioctl), matching stm32's precedent, since nothing in the
generic NuttX serial core surfaces a receive error to an application
otherwise.  Confirmed on hardware: nsh on SCI9 stays fully responsive
through a sustained 3 Mbps overrun on SCI0 that previously froze the
whole board.

claude.title: The RA4 serial error interrupt handler never clears its ICU IELSR.IR flag, the bug the RA8M1 copy fixed because it livelocked the system on receive errors.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-06 commit 5c3c2cbf fixed the RA8M1 serial driver's up_erinterrupt() to call ra_clear_ir(irq), after hardware testing showed that leaving the ICU IELSR.IR flag set made the NVIC re-enter the handler and livelocked the board on any receive error. The RA4 driver, whose ra_serial.c has the same handler structure, still has the old handler at the pinned commit: up_erinterrupt() only saves and clears the SSR error bits, while its RX and TX handlers already call ra_clear_ir(irq). Because RA4 routes SCIn_ERI through the same IELSR mechanism and has the same ra_clear_ir() helper, a parity, framing or overrun error on an RA4 UART would most likely leave the error interrupt pending and hang the system. Adding ra_clear_ir(irq) at the top of the handler carries over directly; the RA8M1 receive-drain part relies on SCI_B behaviour that the repository does not document for the RA4M1 SCI, so whether it is also needed is uncertain. None of this has been confirmed on RA4 hardware.

fix.subject: arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support
fix.message:
arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support

Adds the Data Transfer Controller (DTC) as a generic register-triggered
DMA engine (ra_dtc.c/.h, hardware/ra8m1_dtc.h, CONFIG_RA_DTC, normal
mode only), and generalizes SCI_B's 16-stage FIFO and DTC support from
SCI9-only to every instance (SCI0-4, SCI9): CONFIG_RA_SCIn_FIFO and
CONFIG_RA_SCIn_TXDTC/RXDTC are mutually exclusive, not combinable --
TX DTC moves queued ring-buffer data in the background through
CONFIG_SERIAL_TXDMA, RX DTC moves each byte as it arrives, and measured
on hardware the FIFO's standing multi-byte buffer gives far better
high-baud overrun margin than this one-byte-per-activation RX DTC
design, which also had a real arming bug fixed here (up_rxint()'s old
"first enable" check could never fire, so the DTC was never armed),
alongside a FIFO register-clear/ordering fix.  up_ioctl() also gains
TCGETS/TCSETS (baud rate, parity, stop bits), board.h gains SCI0's
GPIO pins (P609/P610) to exercise it on this board, and comments
throughout ra_serial.c/Kconfig are condensed from the narrative
debugging form they accumulated down to the essential fact each one
needs.  Tested on hardware: SCI0 and SCI9 simultaneously, FIFO and DTC
independently and mutually exclusive; FIFO (TTRG=15/RTRG=0) holds up
cleanly to 3 Mbps for transfers within the RX ring buffer, well past
RX DTC's ceiling (see below).

A separate, more serious bug was also found and fixed while hardware-
testing the overrun path at high baud: up_erinterrupt() never cleared
its ICU IELSRn.IR flag (RA8M1 User's Manual section 13.5.1 is explicit
that this causes the NVIC to re-enter the handler indefinitely), which
livelocked the whole system on any receive error, in every
configuration, not something specific to this series.  Fixed by
clearing it like the other two SCI interrupt handlers already did, by
draining RDR/the FIFO on an error before clearing it (SCIn_ERI fires
instead of SCIn_RXI for every receive error, so data already received
was otherwise never picked up), and by having the RX DTC path also
recognize a byte stuck via CSR.RDRF directly, not just its own
bookkeeping, since its event can be silently dropped by the ICU while
an earlier byte's IR is still pending.  Also added CONFIG_SERIAL_
TIOCGICOUNT (frame/overrun/parity counters via the standard
TIOCGICOUNT ioctl), matching stm32's precedent, since nothing in the
generic NuttX serial core surfaces a receive error to an application
otherwise.  Confirmed on hardware: nsh on SCI9 stays fully responsive
through a sustained 3 Mbps overrun on SCI0 that previously froze the
whole board.

fix.subject: arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support
fix.message:
arch/arm/ra8m1: Add DTC and per-instance SCI FIFO/DTC/termios support

Adds the Data Transfer Controller (DTC) as a generic register-triggered
DMA engine (ra_dtc.c/.h, hardware/ra8m1_dtc.h, CONFIG_RA_DTC, normal
mode only), and generalizes SCI_B's 16-stage FIFO and DTC support from
SCI9-only to every instance (SCI0-4, SCI9): CONFIG_RA_SCIn_FIFO and
CONFIG_RA_SCIn_TXDTC/RXDTC are mutually exclusive, not combinable --
TX DTC moves queued ring-buffer data in the background through
CONFIG_SERIAL_TXDMA, RX DTC moves each byte as it arrives, and measured
on hardware the FIFO's standing multi-byte buffer gives far better
high-baud overrun margin than this one-byte-per-activation RX DTC
design, which also had a real arming bug fixed here (up_rxint()'s old
"first enable" check could never fire, so the DTC was never armed),
alongside a FIFO register-clear/ordering fix.  up_ioctl() also gains
TCGETS/TCSETS (baud rate, parity, stop bits), board.h gains SCI0's
GPIO pins (P609/P610) to exercise it on this board, and comments
throughout ra_serial.c/Kconfig are condensed from the narrative
debugging form they accumulated down to the essential fact each one
needs.  Tested on hardware: SCI0 and SCI9 simultaneously, FIFO and DTC
independently and mutually exclusive; FIFO (TTRG=15/RTRG=0) holds up
cleanly to 3 Mbps for transfers within the RX ring buffer, well past
RX DTC's ceiling (see below).

A separate, more serious bug was also found and fixed while hardware-
testing the overrun path at high baud: up_erinterrupt() never cleared
its ICU IELSRn.IR flag (RA8M1 User's Manual section 13.5.1 is explicit
that this causes the NVIC to re-enter the handler indefinitely), which
livelocked the whole system on any receive error, in every
configuration, not something specific to this series.  Fixed by
clearing it like the other two SCI interrupt handlers already did, by
draining RDR/the FIFO on an error before clearing it (SCIn_ERI fires
instead of SCIn_RXI for every receive error, so data already received
was otherwise never picked up), and by having the RX DTC path also
recognize a byte stuck via CSR.RDRF directly, not just its own
bookkeeping, since its event can be silently dropped by the ICU while
an earlier byte's IR is still pending.  Also added CONFIG_SERIAL_
TIOCGICOUNT (frame/overrun/parity counters via the standard
TIOCGICOUNT ioctl), matching stm32's precedent, since nothing in the
generic NuttX serial core surfaces a receive error to an application
otherwise.  Confirmed on hardware: nsh on SCI9 stays fully responsive
through a sustained 3 Mbps overrun on SCI0 that previously froze the
whole board.

The esp32c3-legacy driver is a separate register-level driver: esp32c3_rxflowcontrol (lines 985-1021) calls esp32c3_lowputc_set_iflow(), which is declared in esp32c3_lowputc.h (included by esp32c3_serial.c) and defined unconditionally in esp32c3_lowputc.c, and UART_RX_FIFO_SIZE is defined as 128 in esp32c3_lowputc.h. So these lines build on this side, and the helper enables RX flow control (UART_RX_FLOW_EN) and writes the threshold, which is what the HAL call does on the fixed side. The legacy driver has no priv->hal and does not use hal/uart_hal.h, so the replacement the fix depends on does not exist here and nothing needs to change.

fix.subject: arch/nrf5x: fix USBD data IN back-to-back packet loss
fix.message:
arch/nrf5x: fix USBD data IN back-to-back packet loss

A data IN endpoint has a single hardware buffer, but the driver armed
the next packet before the host had read the previous one, silently
overwriting it and dropping data under sustained bulk IN traffic. Track
an armed-packet-in-flight state per endpoint (epinflight) and defer
re-arming until the host read completes (EPDATASTATUS), sending the next
packet from nrf52_epdatainterrupt(). Also release the DMA lock right
after the busy-wait for ENDEPIN on data endpoints so other endpoints do
not stall on an interrupt round-trip.

fix.subject: esp32/ble: fix saving/restoring the interrupt status flags
fix.message:
esp32/ble: fix saving/restoring the interrupt status flags

Whenever we enter/leave a critical section, the interrupt status is
saved and, then, restored. However, for the ESP32's BLE adapter,
entering/leaving a critical section is done on separate functions
that need to be registered as a callback.

The status flag was being saved as a global variable. However,
calling nested enter_critical_section would overwrite this global
variable that was storing the previous flag and, when leaving the
last critical section, the restored status would be different from
the one expected. The proposed solution for this issue is to create
a global array to store the interrupt status flags for nested calls.

lines: *   Exit from critical section by enabling interrupts and releasing the spin
*   Exit from critical section by enabling interrupts and releasing the spin

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The ESP32 commit replaces the single saved flag used by the BLE controller callbacks interrupt_disable()/interrupt_restore() with a list of saved flags because 'calling nested enter_critical_section would overwrite this global variable that was storing the previous flag and, when leaving the last critical section, the restored status would be different from the one expected'. esp32c3-legacy/esp32c3_ble_adapter.c still has exactly the pre-fix code: one static irqstate_t g_inter_flags, interrupt_disable() doing g_inter_flags = enter_critical_section(), interrupt_restore() doing leave_critical_section(g_inter_flags), and both are handed to the BLE controller library through the same ._interrupt_disable/._interrupt_restore callback slots as on ESP32. The fix uses only generic NuttX code (sq_queue lists, or the nesting counter g_ble_int_count that ESP32 uses today) and no chip feature, and the legacy adapter has no nesting guard of any kind, while the ESP32 and ESP32-S3 adapters and the newer ESP32-C3 adapter arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_ble_adapter.c all keep one. The legacy OSI table also uses the same OSI_VERSION 0x00010006 as the ESP32-S3 adapter that received the same fix (commit 6521bdfa1). Confidence is medium because whether the binary legacy ESP32-C3 controller library really nests these calls cannot be seen in the repository.
claude.title: The legacy ESP32-C3 BLE adapter keeps the saved interrupt state of BLE critical sections in one global variable, so a nested call loses the outer state.
claude.summary: On 2023-11-10 the ESP32 BLE adapter (commit 606190d9b) stopped saving the interrupt state of the controller's interrupt_disable/interrupt_restore callbacks in a single global, because a nested call overwrote the outer saved state; the ESP32, ESP32-S3 and newer ESP32-C3 adapters all still guard against nesting today, now with a nesting counter. The legacy ESP32-C3 adapter still writes every enter_critical_section() result into the one static g_inter_flags and restores that value on every interrupt_restore. If the controller library nests these calls, the outermost interrupt_restore restores the already-disabled state, so interrupts can stay disabled after the BLE critical section ends. The repository cannot show whether the binary legacy ESP32-C3 controller library actually nests these calls; the case rests on the identical callback code and interface and on the fixes made to the sibling adapters.
claude.same_problem_note: Same saved-interrupt-state global in esp32c3_ble_adapter.c as nuttx-180: the same fix was made in the ESP32-S3 BLE adapter on 2023-10-05 and in the ESP32 adapter on 2023-11-10.

fix.subject: risc-v/bl808: Flush MMU Cache after updating SATP
fix.message:
risc-v/bl808: Flush MMU Cache after updating SATP

Ox64 BL808 crashes with a Page Fault when we run `getprime` then `hello`. This is caused by the T-Head C906 MMU incorrectly accessing the MMU Page Tables of the Previous Process (`getprime`) while starting the New Process (`hello`).

To fix the problem, this PR flushes the MMU Cache whenever we point the MMU SATP Register to the New Page Tables. We execute 2 RISC-V Instructions that are specific to T-Head C906:

- DCACHE.IALL: Invalidate all Page Table Entries in the D-Cache
- SYNC.S: Ensure that all Cache Operations are completed

This is derived from the T-Head Errata for Linux Kernel. More details here: https://lupyuen.github.io/articles/mmu#appendix-flush-the-mmu-cache-for-t-head-c906

Modified Files:

- `arch/risc-v/src/common/riscv_mmu.h`: If needed, `mmu_write_satp()` calls `mmu_flush_cache()` (weak function) to flush the MMU Cache. (Like for T-Head C906)

- `arch/risc-v/src/bl808/bl808_mm_init.c`: Flush the MMU Cache for T-Head C906. Extend `mmuflags` from 32-bit to 64-bit to be consistent with `mmu_ln_setentry()`.

- `boards/risc-v/bl808/ox64/configs/nsh/defconfig`: Enable `ostest` in the Build Config. Update `CONFIG_BOARD_LOOPSPERMSEC` according to `calib_udelay`.

lines: *  mappings. Function also sets the first address environment (satp value).
/* Enable MMU (note: system is still in M-mode) */
*   Flush the MMU Cache for T-Head C906.  Called by mmu_write_satp() after
*   updating the MMU SATP Register, when swapping MMU Page Tables.
*   This operation executes RISC-V Instructions that are specific to
/* DCACHE.IALL: Invalidate all Page Table Entries in the D-Cache */
/* SYNC.S: Ensure that all Cache Operations are completed */
*  Setup kernel mappings when using CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL. Sets up kernel MMU
*  mappings. Function also sets the first address environment (satp value).

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The selected hunk adds a weak mmu_flush_cache() to bl808_mm_init.c that runs two custom opcodes, and the commit message says 'We execute 2 RISC-V Instructions that are specific to T-Head C906' (DCACHE.IALL and SYNC.S); the only other change in the hunk rewords the comment to 'Enable MMU'. eic7700x_mm_init() has the same kernel-mapping and mmu_enable() lines and its comment already reads 'Enable MMU', so only the T-Head cache flush is absent. In arch/risc-v/Kconfig the two chips that define mmu_flush_cache (BL808 and SG2000) both 'select ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD' ('Enable T-Head MMU extension support'), while ARCH_CHIP_EIC7700X does not select it, and nothing under arch/risc-v/src/eic7700x mentions T-Head or C906. The common mmu_write_satp() in riscv_mmu.h already issues 'sfence.vma x0, x0' for every chip and calls mmu_flush_cache only when a chip provides it ('Flush the MMU Cache if needed (T-Head C906)'), so the T-Head-only flush does not apply to EIC7700X.

refs.quote: Flush the MMU Cache if needed (T-Head C906)
Flush the MMU Cache for T-Head C906.

Signed-off-by: chenwen@espressif.com <chenwen@espressif.com>

extern int cache_dbus_mmu_set(uint32_t ext_ram, uint32_t vaddr,

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The only selected hunk adds the ROM prototype 'extern int cache_invalidate_addr(uint32_t addr, uint32_t size);' to esp32s3_spiram.c, and a declaration by itself changes no behaviour. In the commit ('Fix issue of system blocking when SPIRAM is used as stack', 'Support Ext-SRAM-Cache mmu mapping in SMP mode') the function is called only from the newly added cache_dbus_mmu_map(), which serves himem bank switching through esp32s3_set_bank(); the behavioural change lives in that new function and in esp32s3_himem.c and esp32s3_spiflash_mtd.c, not in the selected hunk. So the picked-out hunk is not a fix on its own, and the code it supports has no equivalent on ESP32-S2.

fix.subject: esp32s3/ble: fix saving/restoring the interrupt status flags
fix.message:
esp32s3/ble: fix saving/restoring the interrupt status flags

Whenever we enter/leave a critical section, the interrupt status is
saved and, then, restored. However, for the ESP32-S3's BLE adapter,
entering/leaving a critical section is done on separate functions
that need to be registered as a callback.

The status flag was being saved as a global variable. However,
calling nested enter_critical_section would overwrite this global
variable that was storing the previous flag and, when leaving the
last critical section, the restored status would be different from
the one expected. The proposed solution for this issue is to create
a global array to store the interrupt status flags for nested calls.

lines: /* pm_lock to prevent light sleep due to incompatibility currently */
*   Exit from critical section by enabling interrupts and releasing the spin
*   Perform a solicited context switch on FreeRTOS. Do nothing in NuttX.
*   task_handle - Task handle pointer which is used to pause, resume
*   Exit from critical section by enabling interrupts and releasing the spin
*   task_handle - Task handle pointer which is used to pause, resume

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The ESP32-S3 commit replaces the single saved flag used by the BLE controller callbacks interrupt_disable()/interrupt_restore() with free/used lists of saved flags (hunks 1-3, initialised in esp32s3_bt_controller_init() by hunk 5) because 'calling nested enter_critical_section would overwrite this global variable that was storing the previous flag and, when leaving the last critical section, the restored status would be different from the one expected'. esp32c3-legacy/esp32c3_ble_adapter.c still has exactly the pre-fix code (static irqstate_t g_inter_flags, g_inter_flags = enter_critical_section(), leave_critical_section(g_inter_flags)) registered through the same ._interrupt_disable/._interrupt_restore slots, its struct osi_funcs_s is identical to the ESP32-S3 one at the fix commit with the same OSI_VERSION 0x00010006, and esp32c3_bt_controller_init() sets up no list. The fix needs only generic NuttX code, and the ESP32-S3, ESP32 and newer ESP32-C3 (arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_ble_adapter.c) adapters all still guard against nesting today with g_ble_int_count, while the legacy adapter has no guard. Hunk 4 (passing core_id instead of UINT32_MAX in task_create_wrapper()) does not matter here, because the legacy esp_task_create_pinned_to_core() ignores core_id and only calls kthread_create(), and ARCH_CHIP_ESP32C3_LEGACY does not select ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU. Confidence is medium because whether the binary legacy ESP32-C3 controller library really nests these calls cannot be seen in the repository.
claude.title: The legacy ESP32-C3 BLE adapter keeps the saved interrupt state of BLE critical sections in one global variable, so a nested call loses the outer state.
claude.summary: On 2023-10-05 the ESP32-S3 BLE adapter (commit 6521bdfa1) stopped saving the interrupt state of the controller's interrupt_disable/interrupt_restore callbacks in a single global, because a nested call overwrote the outer saved state; the ESP32-S3, ESP32 and newer ESP32-C3 adapters all still guard against nesting today, now with a nesting counter. The legacy ESP32-C3 adapter, whose controller interface matched the ESP32-S3 one at that time, still writes every enter_critical_section() result into the one static g_inter_flags and restores that value on every interrupt_restore. If the controller library nests these calls, the outermost interrupt_restore restores the already-disabled state, so interrupts can stay disabled after the BLE critical section ends. The core_id part of the same commit does not apply, because the legacy task-creation helper ignores the core and the chip has no multi-CPU support in Kconfig; whether the binary legacy controller library actually nests these calls is not visible in the repository.

fix.subject: risc-v/mpfs: ihc: fix to work with the latest NuttX OpenAMP version
fix.message: risc-v/mpfs: ihc: fix to work with the latest NuttX OpenAMP version

lines: /* Set to VIRTIO_CONFIG_STATUS_DRIVER_OK when master is up */

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The listed hunk only adds rsc->rpmsg_vdev.notifyid = VDEV_NOTIFYID (4) in mpfs_rptun_get_resource(), and the commit message says only "fix to work with the latest NuttX OpenAMP version". In mpfs the vring notify IDs are fixed numbers (VRING0_NOTIFYID is 0 on channel 1) and mpfs_rptun_notify() sends an IHC message only when notifyid == VRING0_NOTIFYID, while OpenAMP also notifies with the vdev's own ID (rpvdev->notify(rpvdev->priv, vdev->notifyid) in the openamp/0009 patch context), so a vdev ID left at 0 collides with vring0; am67_boot.c likewise notes notify IDs "must be unique across all resources". nrf53_rptun_get_resource() (line 201) builds the same table, but its vrings use RSC_NOTIFY_ID_ANY instead of fixed IDs (lines 66-67), nrf53_rptun_notify() ignores vqid and always raises the single RX IPC signal (lines 292-301), and the RX thread always calls the callback with RPTUN_NOTIFY_ALL (line 463). Nothing on the nrf53 side acts on a particular notify ID, so the vdev ID at 0 cannot collide with anything; the other rptun drivers with this design (stm32h7, k230, qemu-rv) do not set it either.

fix.subject: esp32s3/spi: Add SPI bus init in bringup and fix SPI bus 2 and 3 conflict
fix.message:
esp32s3/spi: Add SPI bus init in bringup and fix SPI bus 2 and 3 conflict

1. Add spi bus init in esp32s3_bringup.c
2. Fix IOMUX conflict between spi bus 2 and 3
3. Add spi defconfig
4. Follow the standard of NuttX

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The listed hunk changes only esp32s3_spi3_config, replacing the FSPI* GPIO-matrix signals (the SPI2 bus signals) with SPI3_* signals; the commit message calls this "Fix IOMUX conflict between spi bus 2 and 3". The matched lines in esp32c3_spi.c (259-266) are inside esp32c3_spi2_config (line 240), i.e. the SPI2 bus, and the fixed esp32s3 driver still uses exactly these FSPI* signals for its own SPI2 config (esp32s3_spi.c lines 236 and 257). The esp32c3-legacy port has no SPI3 bus at all: its Kconfig offers only ESP32C3_SPI2 (line 277), the driver has no spi3 config, and hardware/esp32c3_gpio_sigmap.h defines FSPI signals such as FSPICS0_IN_IDX but no SPI3_* signals. So the text matches only by coincidence; the SPI2 signal choice is correct and there is no second bus that could conflict.

fix.subject: risc-v/mmu: Fix map_region() for incorrect page table setup when vaddr is unaligned
fix.message:
risc-v/mmu: Fix map_region() for incorrect page table setup when vaddr is unaligned

When the vaddr parameter passed to map_region() is not aligned to the page directory,
it causes incorrect address mapping for later regions.

For example, in the sv32 case, `PGPOOL` started at `0x80a00000` with a size of `1024*4096B`,
leading to page table errors for the range `0x80c00000~0x80e00000`.

This patch fixes the issue by ensuring map_region() correctly handles unaligned vaddr cases.

Signed-off-by: wushenhui <wushenhui@xiaomi.com>

lines: *   paddr - Beginning of the physical address mapping
*   vaddr - Beginning of the virtual address mapping
*   size - Size of the region in bytes
*   mmuflags - The MMU flags to use in the mapping
static void map_region(uintptr_t paddr, uintptr_t vaddr, size_t size,
/* No, allocate 1 page, this must not fail */
/* Map it to the new table */
for (j = 0; j < RV_MMU_PAGE_ENTRIES && vaddr < endaddr; j++)
/* No, allocate 1 page, this must not fail */
/* Map it to the new table */
for (j = 0; j < RV_MMU_PAGE_ENTRIES && vaddr < endaddr; j++)

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The fix rewrites map_region() in qemu_rv_mm_init.c so that the inner loop stops at the next section boundary (ALIGN_UP_MASK(vaddr + 1, RV_MMU_SECTION_ALIGN_MASK)) and the outer loop runs while vaddr < endaddr; the commit message says an unaligned vaddr "causes incorrect address mapping for later regions". map_region() in bl808_mm_init.c (line 186) still has the identical pre-fix loops (lines 197, 200, 221): it looks up one L3 table for vaddr and then writes up to RV_MMU_PAGE_ENTRIES entries into it, while mmu_ln_setentry() picks the slot only from the vaddr bits (riscv_mmu.c line 130), so a region that starts off a 2 MiB boundary wraps into the wrong slots of that table and the next 2 MiB never gets its own table. BL808 is SV39-only (arch/risc-v/Kconfig line 471) and both macros the fix uses exist for it (RV_MMU_SECTION_ALIGN_MASK in riscv_mmu.h line 127, ALIGN_UP_MASK in include/nuttx/nuttx.h line 55), so nothing on this side makes the fix inapplicable. However, the only in-tree board (ox64 ld.script lines 25-26) puts kflash and ksram at 2 MiB-aligned origins with 2 MiB lengths, so the calls at lines 274 and 278 never pass an unaligned start today and the defect is latent.

refs.quote: static void map_region(uintptr_t paddr, uintptr_t vaddr, size_t size,
for (j = 0; j < RV_MMU_PAGE_ENTRIES && vaddr < endaddr; j++)
#define PGT_L3_SIZE (1024) /* Enough to map 4 MiB (2MiB x 2) */

claude.title: bl808 map_region() builds wrong page tables when a region does not start on a 2 MiB boundary
claude.summary: In June 2025 qemu-rv fixed map_region() so that each L3 page table is filled only up to the next 2 MiB (section) boundary before the next table is looked up; before that, a region with an unaligned start wrapped around inside one table, overwriting earlier entries and leaving the following range unmapped. bl808_mm_init.c still has the old loop, which maps up to 512 pages into one table regardless of where vaddr starts. Today the ox64 linker script puts kernel text at 0x50200000 and kernel data at 0x50400000, each 2 MiB, so nothing goes wrong in the in-tree configuration. A board or linker-script change that starts kernel text or data off a 2 MiB boundary would silently get broken kernel mappings; note that the L3 pool (PGT_L3_SIZE, two tables) would also need to grow for unaligned regions, as qemu-rv did.
claude.impact_note: With the only in-tree board's linker script, both regions passed to map_region() start on a 2 MiB boundary and are exactly 2 MiB long, so the wrong mappings appear only if a board places kernel text or data at an unaligned address.

fix.subject: arch/arm/imxrt: LPUART DMA fixes
fix.message:
arch/arm/imxrt: LPUART DMA fixes

- Only submit and account for a wrapped second TX segment when scatter/gather descriptors
  are available. Without in-memory TCDs, submitting the second segment overwrites the
  active hardware descriptor and incorrectly advances the serial buffer past unsent data.
- Invalidate DMA RX buffer initially

Signed-off-by: Jukka Laitinen <jukka.laitinen@tii.ae>

lines: static void imxrt_dma_txcallback(DMACH_HANDLE handle, void *arg, bool done,
/* Update 'nbytes' indicating number of bytes actually transferred by DMA.
* This is important to free TX buffer space by 'uart_xmitchars_done'.
/* Adjust the pointers and unblock writers */
static void s32k1xx_dma_txcallback(DMACH_HANDLE handle, void *arg, bool done,
/* Update 'nbytes' indicating number of bytes actually transferred by DMA.
* This is important to free TX buffer space by 'uart_xmitchars_done'.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The listed hunk makes imxrt_dma_txcallback() count dmatx.nlength as sent only when CONFIG_IMXRT_EDMA_NTCD > 1 (the same commit also stops imxrt_dma_send() from queuing the wrapped second segment otherwise), because, in the commit message's words, 'Without in-memory TCDs, submitting the second segment overwrites the active hardware descriptor and incorrectly advances the serial buffer past unsent data.' s32k1xx_dma_txcallback() still sets nbytes = length + nlength unconditionally (line 1744), and s32k1xx_dma_send() still calls s32k1xx_dmach_xfrsetup() a second time for the wrapped part whenever dmatx.nbuffer is set (lines 1826-1831), with no check of CONFIG_S32K1XX_EDMA_NTCD. That option defaults to 0 (Kconfig line 580), and in that build s32k1xx_dmach_xfrsetup() programs the channel TCD registers directly and returns -EBUSY when the TCD CSR is non-zero and not DONE (s32k1xx_edma.c lines 1046-1048), which holds after the first segment set DREQ and INTMAJOR, so the second segment is never queued (dma_send ignores the return value) while uart_xmitchars_done() still moves the tail by nbytes (serial_dma.c line 185), dropping the wrapped bytes unsent. Nothing else in the s32k1xx driver compensates; the port needs the NTCD guard (renamed to CONFIG_S32K1XX_EDMA_NTCD) in both the callback and dma_send, and since s32k1xx's callback only posts txdmasem (line 1752) instead of restarting the next transfer as imxrt's does, the remaining bytes should also be kicked from the callback, hence adapt.
claude.title: S32K1xx LPUART TX DMA marks the wrapped part of the TX buffer as sent although it was never transmitted when scatter/gather descriptors are not configured.
claude.summary: In September 2026 (commit 6b0f85b7) the i.MX RT LPUART driver was changed to queue and count the wrapped second part of the TX ring buffer only when CONFIG_IMXRT_EDMA_NTCD > 1, that is, only when scatter/gather descriptors exist. The S32K1xx LPUART driver has the same TX DMA code: it always tries to queue the second part and its completion callback always reports both parts as sent. With the default CONFIG_S32K1XX_EDMA_NTCD=0 the eDMA driver refuses the second part with -EBUSY, so only the first part is transmitted, yet the serial layer frees both, and any write whose data wraps around the end of the TX buffer silently loses the wrapped bytes. This only affects builds that enable LPUART TX DMA (CONFIG_LPUARTn_TXDMA), which no in-tree s32k1xx defconfig does. The fix is the same NTCD guard in s32k1xx_dma_txcallback() and s32k1xx_dma_send(), plus restarting the next transfer from the callback so the remaining bytes do not wait for the next write.

claude.title: S32K1xx LPSPI DMA exchange counts 4 bytes per 16-bit word, so 9-16-bit transfers overrun the caller's buffers.
claude.summary: In October 2024 the i.MX9 LPSPI driver fixed its DMA exchange for 9-16-bit words: it now counts 2 bytes per word instead of 4 and programs the DMA with the number of words instead of that byte count. The S32K1xx LPSPI DMA exchange is the same older code: it still counts 4 bytes per word and uses that count as the number of 16-bit DMA items, while the DMA reads and writes the caller's buffers directly. A 9-16-bit SPI exchange on a DMA-enabled LPSPI therefore clocks out four times as many frames, reads past the end of the TX buffer and writes past the end of the RX buffer, corrupting memory. claude.title: S32K3xx LPSPI DMA exchange counts 4 bytes per 16-bit word, so 9-16-bit transfers overrun the caller's buffers.
claude.summary: In October 2024 the i.MX9 LPSPI driver fixed its DMA exchange for 9-16-bit words: it now counts 2 bytes per word instead of 4 and programs the DMA with the number of words. The S32K3xx LPSPI DMA exchange still has the older code: it counts 4 bytes per word and uses that count as the number of 16-bit DMA items on the caller's buffers, so a 9-16-bit exchange clocks four times as many frames and reads and writes past the ends of the TX and RX buffers. Because the DMA threshold option cannot be enabled on this chip, every exchange on a DMA-enabled LPSPI goes this way. The port needs care: the in-tree FS26 safety chip driver uses 32-bit frames on a DMA-enabled LPSPI3 (mr-canhubk3 'net' defconfig), so the change should be limited to 9-16-bit frames rather than copied as is; whether the current 32-bit path is itself correct cannot be decided from the code.

fix.subject: arch/xtensa/esp32: Fix buffer overflow in SPI poll exchange
fix.message:
arch/xtensa/esp32: Fix buffer overflow in SPI poll exchange

The esp32_spi_poll_exchange() function previously used a hardcoded
length of sizeof(uint32_t) (4 bytes) for memcpy() operations and
pointer increments, disregarding the actual remaining transfer_size.

When an SPI transaction involved a data length not aligned to 4 bytes
(such as a 1-byte payload commonly used in sub-GHz radio drivers),
the driver forced a 4-byte memory transfer. This caused out-of-bounds
reads and writes, leading to stack smashing and fatal CPU exceptions
(e.g., EXCCAUSE=0000).

This patch resolves the memory corruption vulnerability by:
1. Calculating a precise `chunk` size for each iteration, strictly
   bounded by the remaining `transfer_size`.
2. Limiting the memcpy() operations and the subsequent pointer
   increments (tp and rp) to this exact chunk size.
3. Zero-initializing the temporary TX register (w_wd) before copying
   to clear padding and prevent reading uninitialized memory.
4. Adding a NULL check for the receive pointer (rp) prior to the
   memcpy operation to prevent unintended memory writes.

Signed-off-by: Chip L. <chplee@gmail.com>

claude.title: ESP32-C3 (legacy) SPI polling exchange copies whole 4-byte words past the end of buffers whose length is not a multiple of 4.
claude.summary: In February 2026 the ESP32 SPI driver fixed esp32_spi_poll_exchange() so that each memcpy() copies only the bytes left in the transfer instead of always 4, because 1-byte and other unaligned transfers were reading and writing past the caller's buffers and smashing the stack. The ESP32-C3 legacy driver's esp32c3_spi_poll_exchange() is the same code and still copies 4 bytes per data register in both the transmit and receive loops. Any polled exchange whose length is not a multiple of 4 bytes (every such exchange without SPI DMA, and the short ones with it) writes up to 3 bytes past the end of the receive buffer and reads up to 3 bytes past the transmit buffer, which can corrupt the stack or neighbouring data. The fix ports unchanged: take the chunk as the smaller of 4 and the bytes left, and use it for both copies and pointer steps.

claude.title: AT32 PWM stop does not clear the channel compare registers, so a channel can come back with its old duty after a stop.
claude.summary: In February 2024 the STM32 PWM driver started zeroing the four channel compare registers (CCR1-CCR4) in pwm_stop(), because after a STOP in multichannel mode a channel was still outputting; the same lines are now also in the STM32F7, H7 and H5 drivers. fix.subject: rp2040/gpio: Fix debug assertion for interrupts.
fix.message:
rp2040/gpio: Fix debug assertion for interrupts.

The previous interrupt implementation allowed only one single interrupt
mode to be selected. The debug assertion is now updated to allow the
entire range of possible interrupt combinations (a 4-bit field), up to
0xf.

Signed-off-by: Matteo Golin <matteo.golin@gmail.com>

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The commit message says "The previous interrupt implementation allowed only one single interrupt mode to be selected. The debug assertion is now updated to allow the entire range of possible interrupt combinations (a 4-bit field), up to 0xf." It follows the earlier RP2040 change ac583fc58 ("Allow simultaneous selection of multiple interrupt modes"), which turned the RP2040 modes into bit flags (RP2040_GPIO_INTR_EDGE_HIGH is now 0x8) and enables them with ((uint8_t)g_gpio_irq_modes[gpio] & 0xf) << ((gpio % 8) * 4), so the old bound rejected valid combinations. In arch/arm/src/rp23xx the modes are still plain indices 0..3 (RP23XX_GPIO_INTR_EDGE_HIGH is 3), and rp23xx_gpio_enable_irq() sets exactly one bit with 0x1 << ((gpio % 8) * 4 + g_gpio_irq_modes[gpio]). With that encoding, intrmode <= RP23XX_GPIO_INTR_EDGE_HIGH in rp23xx_gpio_irq_attach() is the correct bound, and widening it to 0xf would let values 4..15 shift into the next pin's enable bits. The multi-mode change that the fix depends on was never ported to rp23xx, so the fix does not apply.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR

The STM32 DMA NDTR/CNDTR transfer-count register is 16 bits wide on
every STM32 series the in-tree driver supports (IPv1 CNDTR, IPv2
SxNDTR).  spi_exchange()'s DMA path forwarded the caller's full
nwords to stm32_dmasetup(), so a single SPI_EXCHANGE() of >= 65536
words silently programmed NDTR to (nwords & 0xffff).  When the
truncated count was zero - the typical case for an exact 64 KiB
transfer (flash erase block, FAT cluster, common DMA staging
buffer) - the stream completed instantly with no transfer-complete
interrupt and the caller deadlocked in spi_dmarxwait().

Walk the request in chunks of at most 65535 words inside the
existing DMA branch, reusing the same spi_dma{rx,tx}{setup,start,
wait}() sequence per chunk.  Single-descriptor transfers (every
in-tree caller today) are byte-for-byte identical.  CONFIG_SPI_TRIGGER
is honored for the first chunk only; subsequent chunks must run
unconditionally because re-arming between chunks of one logical
exchange was never part of the SPI_TRIGGER contract.

Drive-by: rescale priv->buflen-clamped nwords so the DMA
descriptor matches the actually-copied byte count, promote the
spiinfo() format specifier from %d to %zu, and fix two adjacent
comment typos.

See the PR description for reproduction, NSH log and benchmark
numbers (5.12 MB/s, 97.5% of SCK/8 @ 42 MHz on STM32F407 + W25Q128).

The DMA spi_exchange() in at32_spi.c has the same pre-fix code: it clips nbytes to priv->buflen without touching nwords (lines 1575-1577) and calls spi_dmarxsetup()/spi_dmatxsetup() with the full nwords (lines 1587-1588), which pass it unchanged to at32_dmasetup() (lines 802-803). The AT32 DMA setup only has DEBUGASSERT(ntransfers < 65536), the same check as the STM32 IPv1 DMAMUX driver (common/stm32/stm32_dma_m3m4_v1_8ch_dmamux.c line 735), and then writes ntransfers into the CNDTR register, while spi_dmarxwait() loops on nxsem_wait_uninterruptible() until the DMA callback sets rxresult, with no timeout. claude.title: The AT32 SPI DMA exchange does not split requests larger than the 16-bit DMA transfer count and does not shrink nwords when the copy is clipped to the driver buffer.
claude.summary: Upstream commit 8302295dd018 (2026-05-15) changed the STM32 SPI driver to run DMA exchanges in chunks of at most 65535 words and to shrink nwords when the copy into the driver's own DMA buffer is clipped to buflen. The AT32 copy in at32_spi.c still hands the full nwords to spi_dmarxsetup()/spi_dmatxsetup() and on to at32_dmasetup(), whose only guard is a debug assertion before the value is written into the CNDTR register, and it then waits for the DMA callback with no timeout. An exchange of 65536 words or more therefore trips the assertion in debug builds and otherwise programs a truncated count, which per the STM32 commit hangs the caller (for an exact 64 Ki-word transfer) or silently exchanges fewer words than requested. When an in-driver DMA buffer is configured and the request is larger than it, the DMA is still programmed with the unclipped nwords and can run past that buffer. The fix has to be adapted so that each chunk keeps the SPIEN disable/enable steps that the AT32 version performs around the DMA setup.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR

The STM32 DMA NDTR/CNDTR transfer-count register is 16 bits wide on
every STM32 series the in-tree driver supports (IPv1 CNDTR, IPv2
SxNDTR).  spi_exchange()'s DMA path forwarded the caller's full
nwords to stm32_dmasetup(), so a single SPI_EXCHANGE() of >= 65536
words silently programmed NDTR to (nwords & 0xffff).  When the
truncated count was zero - the typical case for an exact 64 KiB
transfer (flash erase block, FAT cluster, common DMA staging
buffer) - the stream completed instantly with no transfer-complete
interrupt and the caller deadlocked in spi_dmarxwait().

Walk the request in chunks of at most 65535 words inside the
existing DMA branch, reusing the same spi_dma{rx,tx}{setup,start,
wait}() sequence per chunk.  Single-descriptor transfers (every
in-tree caller today) are byte-for-byte identical.  CONFIG_SPI_TRIGGER
is honored for the first chunk only; subsequent chunks must run
unconditionally because re-arming between chunks of one logical
exchange was never part of the SPI_TRIGGER contract.

Drive-by: rescale priv->buflen-clamped nwords so the DMA
descriptor matches the actually-copied byte count, promote the
spiinfo() format specifier from %d to %zu, and fix two adjacent
comment typos.

See the PR description for reproduction, NSH log and benchmark
numbers (5.12 MB/s, 97.5% of SCK/8 @ 42 MHz on STM32F407 + W25Q128).

claude.title: The STM32L4 SPI DMA exchange puts the whole request into the 16-bit DMA CNDTR count without splitting it, so exchanges of 65536 or more words get a truncated count.
claude.summary: In May 2026 apache/nuttx commit 8302295dd0 changed the STM32 (F1/F2/F3/F4/G4/L1) SPI driver to split DMA exchanges into chunks of at most 65535 words, because the DMA count register is 16 bits wide and an exact 64 KiB exchange left the caller blocked in spi_dmarxwait(). The STM32L4 SPI driver still sets up one DMA transfer with the caller's full nwords, and the L4 DMA driver writes that value into CNDTR, whose count field is 16 bits, with only a debug assertion as a guard. If not fixed, an exchange of 65536 or more words would move only the low 16 bits' worth of data, and with exactly 65536 words the commit reports a hang. At the pinned commit, however, the Kconfig offers no way to enable SPI DMA on STM32L4, so the problem is latent; a human should confirm whether that missing switch is intended before deciding how much the port matters.
claude.impact_note: At the pinned commit no in-tree STM32L4 configuration can turn on CONFIG_STM32_SPI_DMA (the symbol has no prompt and its selectors depend on other families), so the affected DMA path is not built today; it would become a run-time problem for exchanges of 65536 or more words once SPI DMA is selectable for L4.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/stm32/stm32_spi: chunk DMA exchanges to honor 16-bit NDTR

The STM32 DMA NDTR/CNDTR transfer-count register is 16 bits wide on
every STM32 series the in-tree driver supports (IPv1 CNDTR, IPv2
SxNDTR).  spi_exchange()'s DMA path forwarded the caller's full
nwords to stm32_dmasetup(), so a single SPI_EXCHANGE() of >= 65536
words silently programmed NDTR to (nwords & 0xffff).  When the
truncated count was zero - the typical case for an exact 64 KiB
transfer (flash erase block, FAT cluster, common DMA staging
buffer) - the stream completed instantly with no transfer-complete
interrupt and the caller deadlocked in spi_dmarxwait().

Walk the request in chunks of at most 65535 words inside the
existing DMA branch, reusing the same spi_dma{rx,tx}{setup,start,
wait}() sequence per chunk.  Single-descriptor transfers (every
in-tree caller today) are byte-for-byte identical.  CONFIG_SPI_TRIGGER
is honored for the first chunk only; subsequent chunks must run
unconditionally because re-arming between chunks of one logical
exchange was never part of the SPI_TRIGGER contract.

Drive-by: rescale priv->buflen-clamped nwords so the DMA
descriptor matches the actually-copied byte count, promote the
spiinfo() format specifier from %d to %zu, and fix two adjacent
comment typos.

See the PR description for reproduction, NSH log and benchmark
numbers (5.12 MB/s, 97.5% of SCK/8 @ 42 MHz on STM32F407 + W25Q128).

claude.title: The STM32WB SPI DMA exchange puts the whole request into the 16-bit DMA CNDTR count without splitting it, so exchanges of 65536 or more words get a truncated count.
claude.summary: In May 2026 apache/nuttx commit 8302295dd0 changed the STM32 (F1/F2/F3/F4/G4/L1) SPI driver to split DMA exchanges into chunks of at most 65535 words, because the DMA count register is 16 bits wide and an exact 64 KiB exchange left the caller blocked in spi_dmarxwait(). The STM32WB SPI driver still sets up one DMA transfer with the caller's full nwords, and the WB DMA driver writes that value into CNDTR, whose count field is 16 bits, with only a debug assertion as a guard. If not fixed, an exchange of 65536 or more words would move only the low 16 bits' worth of data, and with exactly 65536 words the commit reports a hang. At the pinned commit the WB SPI DMA option that existed until June 2026 is no longer offered by Kconfig, so the problem is latent; a human should confirm whether that option is meant to come back before deciding how much the port matters.
claude.impact_note: At the pinned commit no in-tree STM32WB configuration can turn on CONFIG_STM32_SPI_DMA (the symbol has no prompt and its selectors depend on other families), so the affected DMA path is not built today; it would become a run-time problem for exchanges of 65536 or more words once SPI DMA is selectable for WB again.

claude.summary: In May 2026 apache/nuttx commit 8302295dd0 made the STM32 SPI driver split DMA exchanges into chunks of at most 65535 words, because the DMA transfer count is 16 bits wide and an exact 64 KiB exchange left the caller blocked in spi_dmarxwait(). fix.subject: risc-v/espressif: Fix I2C polling wait timeout comparison.
fix.message:
risc-v/espressif: Fix I2C polling wait timeout comparison.

clock_t is an unsigned type unless CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64 is selected, as
documented in sys/types.h.  The difference in

    while (current - timeout < 0 && priv->error == 0)

therefore underflows to a large positive value instead of being
negative, the comparison is always false, and the loop body never runs.
status keeps its initial value of zero and the function returns OK
without having waited for the transfer at all.

Because the polling path reports completion immediately, every transfer
looks successful: no timeout is ever raised and register reads return
whatever the RX FIFO happens to contain.  The function is compiled in
under CONFIG_I2C_POLLED, which boards use when the I2C interrupt is not
wired up.

Cast the difference to int32_t to get the intended signed comparison.
The result also stays correct across the counter wrap, as long as the
timeout is shorter than the counter range, which SEC2TICK(10) satisfies.

Since this file is modified by this commit, the pre-existing nxstyle
violations reported by the check job are fixed as well, as asked in
CONTRIBUTING.md section 2.1 (adapt all modified files even if you did
not introduce the problem yourself):

* esp_i2c.c:1267      - statement over-indented inside its enclosing
                        block (8 spaces where the block body is at 6)
* esp_i2c.c:1303      - missing blank line after declarations
* esp_i2c.c:1592      - missing blank line after declarations
* esp_i2c.c:1710-1725 - 'case'/'default' labels inside switch(port)
                        sat at the same indent as the brace opening
                        the switch body; they belong one level further
                        in, with the case logic one more level in from
                        the label

Signed-off-by: Aurora-QIU0 <2170685247@qq.com>

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The hunk casts the tick difference to int32_t because, per the commit message, 'clock_t is an unsigned type unless CONFIG_SYSTEM_TIME64 is selected, as documented in sys/types.h', so 'current - timeout < 0' would always be false and the polling loop would never run. That premise does not hold in this tree: include/sys/types.h at the pinned commit has 'typedef int64_t clock_t;' with a note that a signed type is used 'to allow expressing negative tick differences directly', and the unsigned variant was already removed by commit c47b1e2c5 ('!sys/types.h: change time_t and clock_t to int64_t to align with other OSes', 2026-05-19), which is an ancestor of the fix commit. With a signed 64-bit clock_t, the esp32c3-legacy loop 'while (current - timeout < 0 && priv->error == 0)' (line 849, with clock_t current and timeout at lines 832-833 and timeout = current + SEC2TICK(10)) already starts negative and polls until the transfer ends or 10 s pass, so the cast does not change run-time behaviour on either side. The rest of the commit is nxstyle formatting, so the picked hunk is not a behavioural fix here.

fix.message:
arch/arm/rp23xx: Fix IRQ prioritize

Fixes the reg addresses that were copied from armv6 rp2040 to the actual
armv8 spec

Signed-off-by: Serg Podtynnyi <serg@podtynnyi.com>

lines: /* ARMV6M_NVIC_IPR() maps register IPR0-IPR7 with four settings per
/* NVIC_IRQ_PRIORITY maps register IPR0-IPR7 with four settings per
/* Handle processor exceptions.  Only SVCall, PendSV, and SysTick can be
* reprioritized.  And we will not permit modification of SVCall through
/* ARMV6M_NVIC_IPR() maps register IPR0-IPR7 with four settings per
/* Handle processor exceptions.  Only SVCall, PendSV, and SysTick can be
* reprioritized.  And we will not permit modification of SVCall through

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The commit message says it "Fixes the reg addresses that were copied from armv6 rp2040 to the actual armv8 spec", but only the second hunk changes behaviour: the first hunk swaps ARMV6M_NVIC_IPR(irq >> 2) for NVIC_IRQ_PRIORITY(irq), which give the same address (0xe000e400 + 4*(irq >> 2) by armv6-m/nvic.h and armv8-m/nvic.h), so it is only a rename that ARMv6-M code does not need, while the second hunk moves the PendSV and SysTick writes from SHPR2 (0xe000ed1c) to NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY (0xe000ed20, "System handler 12-15 priority register") with the same shift values 16 and 24. In nuc1xx up_prioritize_irq() (nuc_irq.c 347-356, built with CONFIG_ARCH_IRQPRIO, which this chip can enable because ARCH_CHIP_NUC1XX selects ARCH_CORTEXM0 and that selects ARCH_HAVE_IRQPRIO) the PendSV and SysTick branches are the same pre-fix lines, still writing ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR2 with SYSCON_SHPR3_PRI_14_SHIFT / SYSCON_SHPR3_PRI_15_SHIFT. The armv6-m/nvic.h that nuc_irq.c includes as "nvic.h" puts PendSV (bits 16-23) and SysTick (bits 24-31) in System handler priority register 3 at offset 0x0020 and gives SHPR2 only the SVCall field in bits 24-31, and nuc_timerisr.c itself sets the SysTick priority through ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR3. So the register error is not specific to ARMv8: a SysTick request rewrites the SVCall priority, which the function comment says must not be modified, and neither the PendSV nor the SysTick priority changes; the other ARMv6-M copies (rp2040, kl, samd2l2) carry the same lines, so none shows a different handling.

refs.quote: And we will not permit modification of SVCall through

claude.title: nuc1xx up_prioritize_irq() writes the PendSV and SysTick priorities into SHPR2 instead of SHPR3, so a SysTick request changes the SVCall priority instead.
claude.summary: On 2025-04-16 commit 8ac09bcf fixed rp23xx up_prioritize_irq() so that PendSV and SysTick priorities go to System Handler Priority Register 3 (0xe000ed20) instead of SHPR2 (0xe000ed1c); that code had been copied from the ARMv6-M rp2040 driver. The nuc1xx copy still uses ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR2 with the SHPR3 field shifts, although its own armv6-m header places PendSV and SysTick in SHPR3 and SVCall in SHPR2 bits 24-31, and its timer code already uses SHPR3 for SysTick. With CONFIG_ARCH_IRQPRIO enabled, asking for a new SysTick priority silently changes the SVCall priority, asking for a new PendSV priority writes unused SHPR2 bits, and in both cases the requested priority never takes effect although the function returns OK. Only the register part of the fix applies (use ARMV6M_SYSCON_SHPR3 in both branches); the rename to ARMv8-M macro names does not, and nothing in arch/arm/src/nuc1xx or arch/arm/src/armv6-m calls this function, so the problem only shows when board or application code reprioritizes PendSV or SysTick.

fix.subject: stm32h7/ethernet: allow restricting autonegotiation to 10BASE-T full duplex
fix.message:
stm32h7/ethernet: allow restricting autonegotiation to 10BASE-T full duplex

On the linum-stm32h753bi, Ethernet throughput collapses in proportion to
what the display panel is showing. With the LTDC scanning a black screen
a 1.2 MiB TCP transfer to a wired peer takes 0.7 s; solid white takes 20
to 55 s and noise over 130 s, all at the same negotiated 100BASE-TX full
duplex, with the same bytes read from the same SDRAM. The display's
switching couples into the PHY hard enough to corrupt 100BASE-TX
signalling, and TCP grinds through the losses at whatever rate survives.

10BASE-T signals at 2.5 V with Manchester coding at a tenth of the
frequency, and does not care: black, white and noise all move at the
link rate. The same transfer that took five minutes with the display
rendering takes 5.6 seconds.

Restricting the ANAR advertisement is deliberately not the same as
disabling autonegotiation. A forced MCR leaves the partner to parallel
detection, which cannot sense duplex and picks half, a genuine
mismatch, verified here to stall bulk traffic completely. Advertising
only 10BASE-T full duplex keeps the negotiation and lands both ends on
the same mode.

Also fix the never-compiled !CONFIG_STM32_AUTONEG path, which still
called stm32_phywrite(); this driver has only ever had mdio_write().
And say what was negotiated at link-up: a duplex mismatch looks exactly
like a bad cable, and nothing else reports which of the two it is.

The vnc configuration of the linum board enables the new option, and its
packet pool sizing from a few commits ago stays: at any link speed, 24
buffers of 196 bytes was never going to stream a display.


Assisted-by: Claude:opus-5
Signed-off-by: Jorge Guzman <jorge.gzm@gmail.com>

lines: /* mdio_write, not stm32_phywrite:  this driver never had the latter.
* The call was carried over from the F7 driver and nothing had ever
nerr("ERROR: Failed to write the PHY MCR: %d\n", ret);
/* Remember the selected speed and duplex modes */
/* Diagnostic: say what was negotiated even without net debug.  A
* duplex mismatch looks exactly like a bad cable and nothing else
* says which of the two it is.
/* Remember the selected speed and duplex modes */

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit mixes a new option (CONFIG_STM32_AUTONEG_10FD_ONLY, advertising only 10BASE-T full duplex), a build fix in the !CONFIG_STM32_AUTONEG path and a logging change, but the only picked hunk is the logging change: at the end of stm32_phyinit() the ninfo("Duplex: %s Speed: %d MBps") debug message becomes an unconditional syslog(LOG_INFO, "stm32_eth: link %s-duplex %d Mbps") with the same two values. The commit message gives the reason as "say what was negotiated at link-up: a duplex mismatch looks exactly like a bad cable, and nothing else reports which of the two it is", and the new comment calls it a "Diagnostic" shown "even without net debug"; this hunk does not change the PHY setup or the duplex and speed values kept in priv. In at32_phyinit() of at32_eth.c the same ninfo() call is still at 3237-3239, and it only decides whether and how the link-up message is printed. Changing log output is not a behavioural fix, so there is nothing here to carry over.

fix.subject: arch/mips/pic32mz: fix the Ethernet D-Cache coherency.
fix.message:
arch/mips/pic32mz: fix the Ethernet D-Cache coherency.

VIRT_ADDR() converted the DMA buffer addresses to KSEG1, while the
buffers come from g_buffers, which is linked in KSEG0 when the data
memory is cached.  Buffers then ended up in the free list under both
aliases.  Use the segment g_buffers is linked in instead.

A buffer handed to an RX descriptor may still have dirty D-Cache lines,
at least the free list link written into it.  If such a line is evicted
while the DMA writes the frame, it overwrites part of the frame.
Discard the buffer from the D-Cache before giving it to the DMA.

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
Signed-off-by: Daniel P. Carvalho <danieloak@gmail.com>

lines: /* Buffers are always accessed through the segment g_buffers is linked in
* (KSEG0 or KSEG1), so that no buffer is ever reached through two aliases.
/* This union type forces the allocated size of RX descriptors to be the
* padded to a exact multiple of the PIC32MZ D-Cache line size.
/* The pic32mx_driver_s encapsulates all state information for a single

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The commit message ties both changes to the PIC32MZ data cache: VIRT_ADDR() mapped buffers to KSEG1 although g_buffers "is linked in KSEG0 when the data memory is cached", and an RX buffer "may still have dirty D-Cache lines", so the fix takes the segment from g_buffers and adds pic32mz_rxbuffer(), which calls up_invalidate_dcache() before a buffer is given to the DMA. The repository gives PIC32MX no data cache: the PIC32MZ chip entries select MIPS32_HAVE_DCACHE, ARCH_CHIP_PIC32MX7 (like every PIC32MX family) selects only ARCH_MIPS_M4K, "Use D-Cache" (MIPS32_DCACHE) depends on MIPS32_HAVE_DCACHE, ARCH_DCACHE is a hidden option selected only by MIPS32_DCACHE and JZ4780, so on PIC32MX up_invalidate_dcache() is the empty macro of include/nuttx/cache.h, and mips_cache.S is built only by pic32mz/Make.defs. pic32mx_ethernet.c also has no cache maintenance anywhere and keeps its buffers in pd_buffers inside the static g_ethdrvr (there is no g_buffers), and all 19 linker scripts under boards/mips/pic32mx place .bss in KSEG1 data memory (0xa0000200), so the buffers already live in the segment that VIRT_ADDR() at line 273 converts to and are never reached through two aliases. The fix therefore depends on cached data memory, which the PIC32MX port does not have.

The legacy esp_wifi_sta_essid (lines 5319-5330) only copies the SSID and calls esp_wifi_set_config, and nothing under arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3-legacy references sae_pwe_h2e, sae_h2e_identifier, SAE_H2E_IDENTIFIER_LEN, WIFI_AUTH_WPA3_PSK or IW_AUTH_WPA_VERSION_WPA3; its station connect path only sets an OPEN or WEP threshold (lines 657/661) and its station auth setter just returns OK (line 5653). The legacy Wi-Fi code is also built against a different external library, the esp-wireless-drivers-3rdparty snapshot 45701c0 (Make.defs lines 193-194 and 215), not the esp-hal-3rdparty Wi-Fi library esp32s3 used at the fix, and the header that would define the identifier field for that library is not in this repository. The maintained RISC-V path, arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_wifi_api.c lines 836-837, already has both the H2E setting and the identifier clear. Confidence is medium because the legacy library does advertise CONFIG_FEATURE_WPA3_SAE_BIT (line 608), so plain SAE connections may still occur there, and whether that library even has the identifier field cannot be checked from the repository.

fix.subject: s32k3xx:Serial refactor out tx dma semaphore
fix.message:
s32k3xx:Serial refactor out tx dma semaphore

  Fixes stuttering output.

  The use of the semaphore was causing blocking
  on non blocking callers. This ensured that
  the TX DAM would be restated, but when it
  was switched to trywait in 8362e314, it left
  data in the xmit queue unsent.

  This solution removes the semaphore and restart
  the DMA on completion if there is more data in
  the xmit queue to be sent.

lines: /* Update 'nbytes' indicating number of bytes actually transferred by DMA.
* This is important to free TX buffer space by 'uart_xmitchars_done'.

The repository does not explain how the output could keep running after that reset, or why zeroing CCR1-CCR4 right after it changes anything; whether the reset already leaves the compare registers at zero is a hardware question that no header or comment here answers. So it cannot be decided from the repository whether this driver has the problem the stm32h7 commit describes, or whether the added writes would be redundant here (and possibly on stm32h7 too).

fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32h5: Use au_receive_batch in adc_dmaconvcallback
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32h5: Use au_receive_batch in adc_dmaconvcallback

The adc_dmaconvcallback routine was far too slow and inefficient. This was not caught until recently when I was testing faster sample rates. When in circular mode for the adc (dma and constant conversions), the adc_dmaconvcallback function would overwhelm the OS and lock it up. I looked into this and did a lot of testing. First I tried minimally improving the dma callback by removing the % operator from the algorithm, this was slow and inefficient. I also tried increasing the batch size considerably as well as the fifo size. This helped but the OS would still lockup with the fastest sample rate (5 Msps). au_receive_batch was the solution. In order to use this, I needed to change the dmabuffer to be of type uint32_t to match the data pointer in au_receive_batch. I also needed to create a channel buffer, which is initialized once in adc_setup. stm32_gpdma_cfg_s->tr1 needed to be updated for the uint32_t dmabuffer. Once I made changes to use au_receive_batch, I could reliably use the fastest sample rate without locking up the OS. Calling au_receive for every single conversion in a batch is far less efficient than calling au_receive_batch. I also snuck in some changes for the ADC watchdog defines and guards. These were fixes that were tested while testing these changes.

claude.evidence: The picked hunk only changes the DEBUGASSERT at the top of the stm32h5 adc_dmaconvcallback from au_receive to au_receive_batch, because the same commit replaced that callback's per-sample au_receive loops with au_receive_batch calls (the message: 'Calling au_receive for every single conversion in a batch is far less efficient than calling au_receive_batch').
