fix.subject: arch/risc-v/rp23xx-rv: Fix PWM frequency and duty cycle calculation.
fix.message:
arch/risc-v/rp23xx-rv: Fix PWM frequency and duty cycle calculation.

Fixed three bugs in the RP23XX (RISC-V) PWM driver, mirroring the fix
previously applied to the ARM variant:

* setup_period: The previous divisor calculation used integer arithmetic
  that caused overflow and loss of precision. The divider is now computed
  as a 16-bit fixed-point value (div16) using 64-bit arithmetic, and
  clamped to the valid hardware range (0x10 to 0xFFF).

* setup_pulse: The compare value was incorrectly scaled by TOP instead
  of 65535, producing wrong duty cycles. The formula is now corrected
  to ((duty * (top + 1)) / 65535) with an overflow guard.

* pwm_start: The driver was not updated as part of the breaking change
  introduced in commit 4df80e19 ("!drivers/pwm: remove PWM_MULTICHAN
  option"). Access to single channel API is now info->channels[0].duty
  instead of info[0].duty.

Signed-off-by: Brunocor26 <bruno.correia@ubi.pt>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The commit message says it fixed "three bugs" in the rp23xx-rv PWM driver, "mirroring the fix previously applied to the ARM variant": setup_period's divisor "used integer arithmetic that caused overflow and loss of precision", setup_pulse's compare "was incorrectly scaled by TOP instead of 65535, producing wrong duty cycles", and pwm_start still used info[0].duty after commit 4df80e19 removed PWM_MULTICHAN. arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_pwm.c still has all three pre-fix pieces with only the prefix changed: pwm_start reads info[0].duty in the CONFIG_PWM_NCHANNELS != 2 branch (lines 362-364), setup_period computes top = 0xffff / (frequency / max_freq) and divisor = 16 * max_freq / frequency with no range clamp (lines 471-503), and setup_pulse computes 0xffff * duty / top (lines 535-538), while arch/arm/src/rp23xx/rp23xx_pwm.c and the rp23xx-rv driver now use info->channels[0].duty, a clamped div16 and duty * (top + 1) / 65535. Everything the fix relies on exists for rp2040: struct pwm_info_s now only has channels[CONFIG_PWM_NCHANNELS] (include/nuttx/timers/pwm.h line 218) and PWM_NCHANNELS defaults to 1 (drivers/timers/Kconfig lines 90-92), so the single-channel rp2040 build fails, and hardware/rp2040_pwm.h defines the same 8-bit INT and 4-bit FRAC divider fields (lines 90-93) that the 0x10..0xFFF clamp targets. From the code itself, whenever top is reduced below 0xffff the old compare 0xffff * duty / top is scaled up instead of down, so it no longer matches the requested duty and for most duty values exceeds top (in the two-channel sum it then spills into the B field), and the old divisor can fall below 0x10 (e.g. 3000 Hz at 125 MHz gives 16 * 1907 / 3000 = 10) or exceed 0xFFF (1 Hz gives 30512); rp2040 has no other code that handles this.
claude.title: The rp2040 PWM driver still has the old divider and duty-cycle formulas and the removed info[0].duty field access that were fixed in both rp23xx PWM drivers.
claude.summary: The ARM rp23xx PWM driver was fixed on 2026-05-25 (commit 53ef7c063) and the RISC-V rp23xx-rv copy on 2026-06-24 (commit 970f2f22): the clock divider is now a clamped 8.4 fixed-point value, the compare value is duty * (top + 1) / 65535 clamped to top, and pwm_start reads info->channels[0].duty. arch/arm/src/rp2040/rp2040_pwm.c still has the identical old code in pwm_start, setup_period and setup_pulse. If it is not fixed, a single-channel build (PWM_NCHANNELS=1, the Kconfig default) does not compile because struct pwm_info_s has no duty member, and at run time any frequency that forces top below 0xffff gives a wrongly scaled compare value (wrong duty cycle, for most duties above top, and in two-channel mode corrupting channel B), while the divider can be written outside the 0x10..0xFFF range. The patch can be carried over by renaming the rp23xx identifiers to rp2040 ones; this is based on reading the code only, not on hardware tests.
claude.same_problem_note: Same three pre-fix places in rp2040_pwm.c as nuttx-143: the same PWM fix was made in the rp23xx driver on 2026-05-25 and in its RISC-V copy on 2026-06-24.

claude.evidence: The commit is the squashed "Base IMXRT1170 port", and the four listed imxrt_enet.c hunks come from its 1170 rework rather than from a fix for existing chips: union enet_desc_u was dropped together with changing ENET_ALIGN to 64 ("imxrt: enet align buffers 64-byte for optimal performance"), the GPR1 access was abstracted into IMXRT_ENET_IOMUXC_GPR so the 1170 can use GPR4/GPR5 ("imxrt:enet Support ENET_1G"), the DSB replaces the cache clean only under CONFIG_ARMV7M_DCACHE_WRITETHROUGH ("Add DSC barriers for write-through cache support"), and swap32 was replaced by __builtin_bswap32. In s32k1xx_enet.c the swap32 branch (line 306) is only compiled when S32K1XX_BUFFERS_SWAP is defined (line 298), which never happens because s32k1xx_config.h defines S32K1XX_ENET_HAS_DBSWAP (line 108) so the hardware byte swap is used, and swap32 is in any case a valid macro (include/sys/endian.h line 140). The s32k1xx receive path has no cache clean after setting RXDESC_E (line 793) to replace, and the write-through option only exists with an ARMv7-M D-cache (armv7-m/Kconfig lines 64 and 70), which s32k1xx never selects. s32k1xx_lpspi_set_delays gets its clock from s32k1xx_lpspi_pckfreq (s32k1xx_lpspi.c line 747) and has no PLL locals, so the 1170-specific lpspi hunks have nothing to apply to.

claude.evidence: All listed hunks come from the squashed "Base IMXRT1170 port" and add support for the new chip rather than correct a behavioural error: the lowputc and serial hunks add console and buffer definitions for the new LPUART9-12 ("IMXRT7 Add LPUART 9/10/11/12 support"), the two lpspi hunks only add CONFIG_ARCH_FAMILY_IMXRT117x code (1170 root-clock lookup) and hide the pll3_div/pll_freq locals on that family ("imxrt:lpspi Fix unused var warnings"), and the flexspi hunk applies a new rx_sample_clock field that the same commit added to struct flexspi_device_config_s in imxrt_flexspi.h. arch/arm64/src/imx9 has none of the prerequisites for the UART and SPI parts: its Kconfig stops at IMX9_LPUART8 (line 317) and its console/buffer tables stop at LPUART8 (imx9_lowputc.c line 102, imx9_lpuart.c line 592), and imx9_lpspi_master_set_delays takes the source clock from imx9_get_rootclock (imx9_lpspi.c line 733) without any PLL locals. claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit message is "samv7: fix compile warnings for sam_wdt.c" and "Incorrect types in wdinfo and wderr functions were fixed to PRIu32 and PRIx32", and all five listed hunks only change format strings of wdinfo/wderr debug messages from %d/%08x to PRIu32/PRIx32. sama5 sam_wdt.c still has the old strings in sam_getstatus (lines 415-417), sam_settimeout (lines 445, 451, 484, 530) and sam_wdt_initialize (line 656), printing uint32_t values (struct watchdog_status_s fields in include/nuttx/timers/watchdog.h lines 182-184, the uint32_t timeout parameter at line 438), so it would give the same -Wformat warnings. On ARM uint32_t is the compiler's 32-bit __UINT32_TYPE__ (arch/arm/include/types.h line 64), the same width as int, so the printed values do not change and nothing outside the debug output is affected. Per the guide this is a warning-only change, not a behavioural fix.

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The picked hunks only change the parameter type of imx9_dmach_xfrsetup() and imx9_dmach_getcount() from 'DMACH_HANDLE *handle' to 'DMACH_HANDLE handle'; the commit message only says 'The DMACH_HANDLE is already defined as "void *"' and reports no failure. kinetis_edma.c keeps the old signatures (lines 951 and 1224), but kinetis_edma.h declares them the same way (lines 313 and 405), so there is no prototype conflict, and every caller passes a DMACH_HANDLE value (e.g. kinetis_spi.c line 1251 passes priv->rxdma, declared as DMACH_HANDLE at line 112), which C converts implicitly from void * to void **. Inside both functions the parameter is used exactly once, cast straight to 'struct kinetis_dmach_s *' (lines 954 and 1226), so the pointer value and the run-time behaviour are identical with either type. The change is a type cleanup with no run-time effect, so it is not a behavioural fix that kinetis is missing.

fix.subject: stm32/adc: add support for differential mode (DIFSEL) and calibration
fix.message:
stm32/adc: add support for differential mode (DIFSEL) and calibration

Add board-level configuration and driver support for differential input
channels and auto-calibration on STM32 ADC IPv2 and IPv2G4 (STM32F3,
STM32G4), following the STM32H5 architecture pattern requested in review:

- In hardware headers (stm32_adc_v2.h and stm32_adc_v2g4.h), fix register
  comments and define ADC_DIFSEL register shift and masks.
- In stm32_adc_m3m4_v1v2.c:
  - Add difsel field to struct stm32_dev_s initialized from
    BOARD_ADCx_DIFSEL if defined, falling back to ADC_DIFSEL_DEFAULT (0).
  - Configure DIFSEL before enabling the ADC in adc_configure().
  - Fix and enable adc_calibrate() for HAVE_IP_ADC_V2, supporting both
    single-ended calibration (ADCALDIF=0) and differential calibration
    (ADCALDIF=1) based on the channel selection.

Verified on Nucleo-G431KB (single-ended and differential channel 1).

fix.subject: !nuttx: drop redundant casts on tv_sec/tv_nsec and fix printf formats
fix.message:
!nuttx: drop redundant casts on tv_sec/tv_nsec and fix printf formats

Now that time_t is unconditionally 64-bit (signed int64_t) and the
struct timespec fields tv_sec / tv_nsec are wide enough on their own,
the explicit (uint64_t)/(int64_t)/(int) casts that used to guard the
multiplications and subtractions in *_us / *_ms / *_ns helpers are no
longer needed.  Drop them to keep the timekeeping math readable and
consistent with the previous sclock_t/time_t cleanup.

In the same spirit, this commit also:

* Normalises the printf-style format specifiers and casts used to
  print tv_sec / tv_nsec / tv_usec values across arch/, drivers/,
  fs/, sched/ and libs/.  The prior code was a mix of
  "%d"/"%u"/"%ld"/"%lu"/"%lld"/PRIu32/PRIu64 with matching
  (int)/(unsigned long)/(long long)/PRIu* casts; some formats
  truncated time_t on 32-bit hosts, others mismatched signedness or
  width.  Replace all such cases with the portable POSIX-recommended
  forms:

    - tv_sec  (time_t,       signed, impl-defined width) -> %jd  + (intmax_t)
    - tv_nsec (long,         signed)                     -> %ld  (no cast)
    - tv_usec (suseconds_t / long)                       -> %ld  (no cast)

  Add #include <stdint.h> where required.

* Drops a few stale `(FAR const time_t *)&ts.tv_sec` casts and
  related `(FAR struct tm *)` / `(const time_t *)` casts in
  gmtime_r() / localtime_r() / gmtime() callers; ts.tv_sec is plain
  time_t now and the casts only obscured the type.

* Fixes one overflow in fs/procfs/fs_procfscritmon.c where
  all_time.tv_sec * 1000000 could overflow on 32-bit time_t before
  being multiplied again; cast to uint64_t at the start.

No behavioural change.

fix.subject: arch/rp23xx: add bounded timeout to SPI DMA completion wait
fix.message:
arch/rp23xx: add bounded timeout to SPI DMA completion wait

The SPI DMA exchange path previously waited for completion with two untimed, uninterruptible semaphore waits (nxsem_wait_uninterruptible). If a DMA transfer never completes (e.g. stalled slave or bus glitch), the calling thread sleeps indefinitely.

In network drivers like W5500 on SPI0 running from the LP work queue while holding net_lock, this causes the worker to hang permanently, wedging the whole network stack and blocking recovery handlers.

This patch updates both ARM and RISC-V ports of rp23xx:

- Switches to nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() with a transfer-size-derived timeout plus a safety margin.

- On timeout, forcibly stops both DMA channels with rp23xx_dmastop(), disables SPI DMA in the control register, resets the semaphore count, drains leftover RX FIFO bytes, and logs an error to degrade gracefully instead of deadlocking.

Fixes #19305

Signed-off-by: Sarthak Pandey <sarthak@email.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The rp23xx commit replaces the two untimed nxsem_wait_uninterruptible() calls in spi_dmatrxwait() with nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() bounded by a transfer-size-derived timeout, and on timeout stops both DMA channels, resets the semaphore and drains the RX FIFO; its message says "If a DMA transfer never completes (e.g. stalled slave or bus glitch), the calling thread sleeps indefinitely." cxd56_spi.c has the same spi_dmatrxwait() as the pre-fix rp23xx code: two untimed uninterruptible waits on priv->dmasem, which only spi_dmatxcallback()/spi_dmarxcallback() post, followed by cxd56_dmastop() on both channels and clearing DMACR; it is called from spi_dmaexchange() after up_pm_acquire_freqlock(), so a stuck wait also keeps the frequency lock (the flagged lines 1547/1569 are only the similar-looking spierr calls inside the DMA callbacks). Nothing in this driver bounds the wait, and everything the fix uses exists here: the frequency, actual and nbits fields, cxd56_dmastop(), the SR/RNE and DR registers for draining the RX FIFO, and the OS calls nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() and nxsem_reset(). The only basis for a DMA transfer that never completes is the rp23xx commit message, and the CXD56 DMA controller is different hardware, so confidence is medium.

claude.title: The cxd56 SPI driver waits for DMA completion with no timeout, so a DMA transfer that never finishes hangs the caller forever.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-13 the rp23xx SPI driver (ARM and RISC-V ports) changed spi_dmatrxwait() to wait for the TX and RX DMA completions with nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() and a timeout derived from the transfer size and SPI clock, and on timeout to stop both DMA channels, reset the semaphore and drain the RX FIFO. The cxd56xx SPI driver still has the pre-fix version: two untimed uninterruptible waits on dmasem that only the DMA completion callbacks post. If a DMA transfer never finishes, the calling thread blocks forever while it holds the SPI bus lock and the PM frequency lock taken in spi_dmaexchange(), so other users of that bus stall too. The repository does not show that a DMA transfer can actually stall on the CXD56 DMA controller; that scenario comes only from the rp23xx commit message.

fix.subject: arch/rp23xx: add bounded timeout to SPI DMA completion wait
fix.message:
arch/rp23xx: add bounded timeout to SPI DMA completion wait

The SPI DMA exchange path previously waited for completion with two untimed, uninterruptible semaphore waits (nxsem_wait_uninterruptible). If a DMA transfer never completes (e.g. stalled slave or bus glitch), the calling thread sleeps indefinitely.

In network drivers like W5500 on SPI0 running from the LP work queue while holding net_lock, this causes the worker to hang permanently, wedging the whole network stack and blocking recovery handlers.

This patch updates both ARM and RISC-V ports of rp23xx:

- Switches to nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() with a transfer-size-derived timeout plus a safety margin.

- On timeout, forcibly stops both DMA channels with rp23xx_dmastop(), disables SPI DMA in the control register, resets the semaphore count, drains leftover RX FIFO bytes, and logs an error to degrade gracefully instead of deadlocking.

Fixes #19305

Signed-off-by: Sarthak Pandey <sarthak@email.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The rp23xx commit replaces the two untimed nxsem_wait_uninterruptible() calls in spi_dmatrxwait() with nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() bounded by a transfer-size-derived timeout, and on timeout stops both DMA channels, resets the semaphore and drains the RX FIFO; its message says "If a DMA transfer never completes (e.g. stalled slave or bus glitch), the calling thread sleeps indefinitely." Apart from the chip prefix, rp2040_spi.c has the same DMA path as the pre-fix rp23xx file: spi_dmatrxwait() (line 1128) does two untimed uninterruptible waits on priv->dmasem, which only the DMA callbacks post, and it is called from spi_dmaexchange() at line 962; rp2040_dmac.c calls the callback only from its channel interrupt, as rp23xx_dmac.c does. Of the three hunks, the prototype change at line 118 is part of the fix and the spi_dmatrxwait body (lines 1132/1137) is the fix itself, while the spi_flush hunk at line 915 only turns an empty ';' loop body into braces and is style-only; the flagged spierr lines 1012/1034 sit in the DMA callbacks and are not part of the fix. Everything the fix uses exists here (frequency, actual and nbits fields, rp2040_dmastop(), SSPSR RNE and SSPDR for draining, nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible() and nxsem_reset()) and nothing else bounds the wait; confidence is medium only because the stall scenario is stated by the commit message rather than shown in code.

fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32h7: Fix UART TX DMA getting stuck
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32h7: Fix UART TX DMA getting stuck

When closing a serial port an ongoing TX DMA transfer will be stopped. This can cause
one (or multiple) the following:

- dev->dmatx.length != 0
- dev->dmatx.nlength != 0
- stm32_dmaresidual returning a non-zero residual

This is caused by length/nlength not being set to 0 at startup or during closing.
In addition the DMA_SxNDTR register is not set to 0 at startup or during closing.

This commit solves the issue by setting the variables and register to 0 during closing.

Signed-off-by: Alexander Lerach <alexander@auterion.com>

arch/arm/stm32h7: Add review feedback regarding style

Removed non-needed spaces.
Aligned style of documentation.

Signed-off-by: Alexander Lerach <alexander@auterion.com>

lines: *   Configure the USART to operation in interrupt driven mode.  This method
*   Configure the USART to operation in interrupt driven mode.  This method

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The judged hunk only clears dev->dmatx.length and dev->dmatx.nlength after the TX DMA channel is freed in up_dma_shutdown(); in stm32h7 this matters because its up_dma_txavailable() starts a new transfer only when dmatx.length == 0, dmatx.nlength == 0 and the residual is 0, and a transfer stopped at close never reaches uart_xmitchars_done(), which is what zeroes them. at32_serial.c has the same shutdown code, but its up_dma_txavailable() gates only on at32_dmaresidual(priv->txdma) == 0 and never reads length/nlength; the upper half's uart_xmitchars_dma() rewrites both fields before every new transfer, and the TX callback runs only after a transfer has been started, so stale values cannot block transmission. The difference is purely in how the TX-idle check is written, so this hunk is not needed there. Separately, the same commit also clears the DMA count register on free in stm32h7 stm32_dma.c (not part of this candidate), which targets the residual that the at32 check does rely on; at32_dmafree() only marks the channel unused and does not clear CNDTR, which would need its own review.

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The listed hunks only declare and wire into g_dma_ops the new per-controller dma_free op that the commit ('Fix UART TX DMA getting stuck') adds so that stm32_dmafree writes 0 to the stream count register (stm32_sdma_free does 'dmachan_putreg(dmachan, STM32_DMA_SNDTR_OFFSET, 0)'), because the stm32h7 serial driver only starts a new TX DMA when 'stm32_dmaresidual(priv->txdma) == 0' and the message says a stopped transfer left 'stm32_dmaresidual returning a non-zero residual'. The n32h7 DMA driver drives a different controller: hardware/n32h7_dma.h defines per-channel SA/DA/LLP/CTRL/CFG/SG/DS registers plus a global CHEN enable register and no SxNDTR-style count register, n32_sdma_setup writes the transfer size into the CTRL BTS field, and the n32h7 MDMA ops are unimplemented stubs ('#warning n32_mdma_setup not implemented'). More importantly nothing in n32h7 consumes a DMA residual: n32_dma.h exports no n32_dmaresidual, g_dma_ops[].dma_residual is never called, and n32_serial.c's up_dma_txavailable gates only on 'priv->dev.dmatx.length == 0 && priv->dev.dmatx.nlength == 0', so a dma_free op that clears a count register on free would change nothing here. Side note outside this pair: n32_serial.c's up_dma_shutdown calls n32_dmastop/n32_dmafree on the TX channel without resetting dev->dmatx.length/nlength, which corresponds to the serial-side half of the same commit and may deserve its own check.

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The listed hunk adds 'dev->dmatx.length = 0; dev->dmatx.nlength = 0;' after stm32_dmafree in up_dma_shutdown; per the commit message ('Fix UART TX DMA getting stuck'), closing a port mid-transfer left 'dev->dmatx.length != 0' or 'dev->dmatx.nlength != 0', and the stm32h7 up_dma_txavailable only calls uart_xmitchars_dma when 'priv->dev.dmatx.length == 0 && priv->dev.dmatx.nlength == 0 && stm32_dmaresidual(priv->txdma) == 0', so stale lengths blocked TX after the port was reopened. stm32f7's up_dma_shutdown (lines 2208-2213) has the same pre-fix lines, but its up_dma_txavailable gates only on 'stm32_dmaresidual(priv->txdma) == 0' and never reads dmatx.length/nlength; the only other readers are up_dma_txcallback and up_dma_send, which act on a transfer started by uart_xmitchars_dma, and that function in drivers/serial/serial_dma.c rewrites length and nlength before every send. So stale lengths cannot block the f7 driver and adding this hunk would not change its behaviour; the difference is purely in how the idle check is written. Caveat outside this hunk: the f7 DMA driver does not clear SNDTR on stop or free (stm32_dmastop only calls stm32_dmastreamdisable, stm32_dmafree only posts the semaphore) while f7's up_dma_txavailable depends on stm32_dmaresidual, so the residual half of the commit (done in stm32h7/stm32_dma.c) may still matter for stm32f7/stm32_dma.c and should be checked separately.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/*/stm32_fdcan_sock.c: prevent interrupt flood on errors.
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/*/stm32_fdcan_sock.c: prevent interrupt flood on errors.

Previous code was failing to disable error interrupts which
due to standard CAN retransmissions might trigger continusouly
(for example, with a disconnected CAN interface) flooding the
system and preventing other operations to continue.

Fixes: https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/16668
Signed-off-by: Carlos Sanchez <carlossanchez@geotab.com>

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The commit ('prevent interrupt flood on errors', 'Previous code was failing to disable error interrupts') fixes the SocketCAN FDCAN drivers, whose ISR first masks every error interrupt with 'fdcan_errint(priv, false)' and defers to fdcan_error_work; that work used to clear PEA/PED or the RX-error enables and then call fdcan_errint(priv, true), re-enabling everything at once, so the listed hunk 'ie |= FDCAN_ANYERR_INTS;' rebuilds the full mask locally so the selective clears survive the single final IE write. stm32h5/stm32_fdcan.c is the character-device FDCAN driver and has no fdcan_errint or error work at all: its fdcan_interrupt reads IR/IE (lines 3003-3006), clears PEA/PED when PSR.LEC is set and the pending RX-error enables, and writes IE immediately ('fdcan_putreg(priv, STM32_FDCAN_IE_OFFSET, ie);' at 3046 and 3095). Those interrupts are turned back on only after a successful transmission (line 3132) or reception (line 3198), and nothing re-enables all error interrupts at the end, which is exactly the behaviour the fix restores in the socket drivers; the in-code comment states the same intent ('These errors have a tendency to flood the system with'). Line 2066 is an unrelated match in the CANIOC bit-timing ioctl that saves IE across fdcan_reset. Adding 'ie |= FDCAN_ANYERR_INTS' to the h5 ISR would instead re-enable deliberately masked error interrupts at the next IE write, so the h5 driver already handles this problem in its own way.

fix.subject: Enable LPUART functionality for the STM32G4 series.
fix.message:
Enable LPUART functionality for the STM32G4 series.

1. Kconfig - Removed USART1 config option from STM32_STM32G47XX. Not necessary to adding LPUART functionality. 2. stm32_lowput.c - Added extra check from STM32G4 board because that is the only with LPUART functionality. 2. stm32_serial.c - Removed unneeded function (stm32_serial_get_lpuart). Fixed up_putc return bug. Added configuration for DMAMAP_LPUART RX and TX for STM32G4XXX only. The G4 is the only in this family with LPUART and uses a DMAMUX unlike the others.

1. Removed 1WIRE LPUART refereences in Kconfig and stm32_uart.h. There is no support for LPUART currently in stm32_1wire.c. 2. Removed references to LPUART under DMA_V2 ifdefs. STM32G4 uses DMA_V1, and I saw that none of the chips DMA_V2 (F20, F4) have LPUARTs. AFAIK the only chip in the stm32 folder that has LPUART peripherals is the STM32G4.

Removed unnecessary brackets and empty lines

Added lpuartnsh (LPUART NuttShell) config to the nucleo-g474re board configurations. nsh uses USART3 by default. lpuartnsh uses nsh as a template, changes the serial console to LPUART1, and adds the DMA configs to enable DMA for the LPUART.

Added support for using the lpuart prescaler register. Without prescaling the apbclock, 9600 baud is not supported on the G474RE. By utilizing the prescaler, when necessary, we can support nearly any baud rate (300 baud to 30M Mbaud). lowputc defaults to a prescaler of 16 for the lpuart so standard baud rates (9600 to 115200) are supported early in the boot process. Later in stm32_serial.c the ideal prescaler and BRR values are determined.

Added ifdef statements for LPUART code sections not compatible with other chips.

Changed LPUART BRR calcuation to use 64-bit integers.

Feedback from nuttx pull request. Added brackets around single line if/else statements. Reordered lpuartnsh defconfig file.

Fix lpuart brr calculation after attempting to break the calculation into 2 lines.

Removed TAB

claude.evidence: The commit is a feature commit ('Enable LPUART functionality for the STM32G4 series'), and the three hunks listed for this pair are LPUART plumbing only: a new 'islpuart' member in struct up_dev_s, and '#elif CONSOLE_LPUART > 0' branches in arm_serialinit and up_putc that take the console from the new g_lpuart_devs table. For a U[S]ART console nothing changes: the UART branch still registers &g_uart_devs[CONSOLE_UART - 1]->dev, and up_putc ends with 'return ch;' both before and after the commit, so the 'Fixed up_putc return bug' in the message is not visible in these hunks or anywhere in the final stm32_serial.c diff. The at32 port has no LPUART at all: no file under arch/arm/src/at32 mentions LPUART, at32_uart.h only selects CONSOLE_UART values, and the driver iterates g_uart_devs[AT32_NUSART]. fix.subject: Fix Serial APB Clock Sources
fix.message:
Fix Serial APB Clock Sources

The apbclock sources for lpuart1, usart6, usart10, and usart11 were set to the wrong PCLK (default).

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk changes the STM32H5 LPUART1 .apbclock from STM32_PCLK2_FREQUENCY to the clock of the bus LPUART1 really sits on (PCLK3 there); the commit message says these apbclock sources 'were set to the wrong PCLK (default)'. In stm32wl5_serial.c the g_lpuart1priv initializer still uses STM32_PCLK2_FREQUENCY (line 426) and the LPUART divisor is computed from priv->apbclock (line 795), yet the same driver enables LPUART1 through RCC_APB1ENR2 (line 1122), the WL5 RCC header puts LPUART1EN in APB1ENR2 and names LPUART1SEL value 0 as PCLK1 (lines 420, 517; stm32wl5_rcc.c never changes LPUART1SEL), and stm32wl5_lowputc.c uses STM32_PCLK1_FREQUENCY for an LPUART1 console (line 51), as does the STM32L4 serial driver for LPUART1. So the WL5 copy has the same wrong-PCLK default for LPUART1, but the right value there is PCLK1, not PCLK3 (no STM32_PCLK3_FREQUENCY exists for stm32wl5), so the patch must be adapted; the other listed line (486, USART1 with PCLK2) is correct because USART1 is enabled in APB2ENR (line 1128). The only in-tree board, nucleo-wl55jc, sets PCLK1 and PCLK2 both to HCLK/1 (board.h lines 87 and 99), so the error has no visible effect there today.
claude.title: The STM32WL5 serial driver computes the LPUART1 baud divisor from PCLK2, although LPUART1 is clocked from APB1 (PCLK1).
claude.summary: On 2024-11-07 the STM32H5 serial driver fixed LPUART1 (and three USARTs) whose apbclock had been left at the default PCLK2 instead of the clock of the bus the port is on. The STM32WL5 serial driver still sets LPUART1's apbclock to STM32_PCLK2_FREQUENCY and uses it for the baud divisor, while its own clock-enable code, RCC header and early console code all treat LPUART1 as an APB1/PCLK1 peripheral. On a board whose APB1 and APB2 prescalers differ, the serial driver would program a wrong LPUART1 baud rate that also disagrees with what the early console set up. The change has to be adapted: on WL5 the value should be STM32_PCLK1_FREQUENCY, not PCLK3. The only in-tree board runs PCLK1 and PCLK2 at the same 48 MHz, so no in-tree configuration shows the error today.
claude.impact_note: The only in-tree STM32WL5 board (nucleo-wl55jc) sets PCLK1 and PCLK2 both to HCLK/1, so the divisor comes out the same today; only a board with different APB1 and APB2 prescalers would get a wrong LPUART1 baud rate.

claude.evidence: The picked hunk only swaps nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock) for enter_critical_section() around the reference-count check in imxrt_i2cbus_initialize and adds a (volatile int) cast to the post-increment result, which does not change the value tested; both forms serialize the refs++ test and the one-time hardware init. None of the commit message lines ('imxrt:lpi2c fix status handeling & race', 'Simplify DMA and Non DMA usage', 'dma invalidate cache after exchange', 'fix timeout not stopping dma') describes a problem with this locking, and the race the commit does fix is elsewhere: it now sets priv->intstate = INTSTATE_WAITING before the DMA is started in imxrt_lpi2c_transfer (imxrt_lpi2c.c line 2187). In am335x_i2cbus_initialize (lines 1610-1616) and am335x_i2cbus_uninitialize (lines 1641-1651) refs is only tested and changed while holding priv->lock, the same mutex that am335x_i2c_transfer and am335x_i2c_reset take (lines 1314, 1467), so the am335x copy has no unprotected access for this hunk to fix. Most other NuttX I2C drivers in this tree, for example stm32h7 and stm32l4, use the same nxmutex_lock pattern in their initialize functions.

fix.subject: arch/arm64/src/imx9/imx9_lowputc.c: Fix an arithmetic sign error in divisor calculation
fix.message:
arch/arm64/src/imx9/imx9_lowputc.c: Fix an arithmetic sign error in divisor calculation

In the algorithm there is a subtraction (int - unsigned), which results (potentially overflowed)
unsigned.

Passing this to macro ABS and the assigning to int doesn't work ( unsigned is always >= 0 ).

Fix this by replacing (dangerous) ABS macro with stdlib's standard "int abs(int)"

Signed-off-by: Jukka Laitinen <jukkax@ssrc.tii.ae>

fix.subject: esp32: fix esp32 wifi bug caused scan failed
fix.message:
esp32: fix esp32 wifi bug caused scan failed

tools/configure.sh esp32c3-generic:wifi
wapi scan wlan0
has no return result after couple times

rootcause:
mq_timedsend() return failed because the time valid check error.
the ts_nsec is bigger than 1000000000.
esp_update_time() hasn't consider of the ns > 1s after the adding
calculation

Signed-off-by: ligd <liguiding1@xiaomi.com>

lines: static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)
*   Wait semaphore within a certain period of time
static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)
static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)
*  arg - number of the bit as void pointer
static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)
static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)
static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The fix replaced the hand-written body of esp_update_time() with clock_ticks2time() plus clock_timespec_add(), because, in the commit's words, "mq_timedsend() return failed because the time valid check error. the ts_nsec is bigger than 1000000000. esp_update_time() hasn't consider of the ns > 1s after the adding calculation". In arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_ble_adapter.c, esp_update_time() (lines 2198-2209) is still the exact pre-fix body: it adds TICK2NSEC() of the leftover ticks to timespec->tv_nsec with no carry into tv_sec. It is used the same way as on the fixed side: queue_recv_wrapper() and esp_queue_send_generic() take clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME), call esp_update_time() and pass the result to file_mq_timedreceive()/file_mq_timedsend(), which at the pinned commit return -EINVAL when abstime->tv_nsec >= 1000000000 (sched/mqueue/mq_send.c line 305, sched/mqueue/mq_receive.c line 163). Nothing chip- or config-specific stands in the way: the sibling arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_wifi_adapter.c in the same directory already has the fixed esp_update_time() using clock_ticks2time()/clock_timespec_add(), and the BLE adapter is built whenever CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_BLE is set.

refs.quote: static void esp_update_time(struct timespec *timespec, uint32_t ticks)

claude.title: The ESP32-C3 BLE adapter's esp_update_time() can leave tv_nsec at one second or more, so timed BLE message-queue sends and receives fail with EINVAL.
claude.summary: On 2024-10-07, commit b3727f67bee3 rewrote esp_update_time() in the ESP32, ESP32-S3 and legacy ESP32-C3 BLE and Wi-Fi adapters to use clock_ticks2time() and clock_timespec_add(), which carry nanoseconds above one second into tv_sec. The newer ESP32-C3 BLE adapter (arch/risc-v/src/esp32c3/esp_ble_adapter.c) still has the old body, even though esp_wifi_adapter.c in the same directory has the fixed one. Whenever the current time's nanoseconds plus the timeout's fraction of a second reach one second, file_mq_timedsend() and file_mq_timedreceive() reject the deadline with -EINVAL, so a timed BLE queue send fails and a timed receive returns at once instead of waiting. This is the same failure the commit reports for Wi-Fi scanning, and the two-line fix can be copied as is.

fix.subject: arch/arm/rp23xx: Add the PM standby and dormant states.
fix.message:
arch/arm/rp23xx: Add the PM standby and dormant states.

Map the NuttX PM states onto the RP2350 low-power modes:

- PM_STANDBY is the RP2350 SLEEP state: a WFI with the clocks of the
  blocks that have no driver in the configuration gated (SLEEP_EN0/1).
- PM_SLEEP is the DORMANT state: clk_sys moves to the crystal
  oscillator, the PLLs and then the oscillator stop, and the clock tree
  is restored after the wake, as pico-extras does.  Only the GPIO
  dormant-wake detector can wake the chip, so PM_SLEEP gives the
  standby state when no wake GPIO is configured.  The wake GPIO also
  raises a one-shot interrupt, so that the core leaves its WFI and
  restores the PLLs at once.  The time of day is taken back from the
  always-on timer after the wake.

The dormant state stops the UARTs.  A PM_STANDBY wakelock
(pm_staytimeout()) is held for RP23XX_PM_WAKE_HOLD_MS after a dormant
wake and after each character a UART receives.  The serial driver
refuses PM_SLEEP in its prepare callback while a UART transmits.  A
dormant chip does not answer SWD, so the pm configurations use
PM_GOVERNOR_EXPLICIT_RELAX to stay out of it for a time after boot.

With RP23XX_PM_QUIESCE_PADS, arm_pminitialize() also isolates the
unused pads and holds the blocks with no driver in reset.  A floating
bank 0 input settles near 2.2V (erratum RP2350-E9) and its input
buffer then draws a static current in every state.

Also select ARCH_HAVE_PM, and fix the LED PM callbacks of three boards,
which used BOARD_LED where the boards define BOARD_LED1.  They did not
build with CONFIG_PM.

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
Signed-off-by: Marco Casaroli <marco.casaroli@gmail.com>

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit is a feature addition, "arch/arm/rp23xx: Add the PM standby and dormant states.", and the only hunk picked out adds a forward declaration of up_pm_prepare() under '#ifdef CONFIG_RP23XX_PM', the new prepare callback that, in the commit's words, makes the serial driver refuse PM_SLEEP "while a UART transmits" because the RP2350 dormant state stops the UART clock. CONFIG_RP23XX_PM is a new rp23xx-only Kconfig menu (arch/arm/src/rp23xx/Kconfig line 917), and the declaration has no behaviour by itself. The lines matched in arch/arm/src/a1x/a1x_serial.c (103-105) are just the standard up_txint/up_txready/up_txempty prototypes of the serial upper-half operations that a1x declares for its own g_uart_ops table (line 111); they are shared context, not pre-fix code, and a1x_serial.c has no PM callback or any PM code at all. The one real fix in the commit (the board LED PM callbacks using BOARD_LED instead of BOARD_LED1) is in boards/arm/rp23xx files, not in this hunk.

  dormant-wake detector can wake the chip, so PM_SLEEP gives the
  standby state when no wake GPIO is configured.  The wake GPIO also
  raises a one-shot interrupt, so that the core leaves its WFI and
  restores the PLLs at once.  The time of day is taken back from the
  always-on timer after the wake.

The dormant state stops the UARTs.  A PM_STANDBY wakelock
(pm_staytimeout()) is held for RP23XX_PM_WAKE_HOLD_MS after a dormant
wake and after each character a UART receives.  The serial driver
refuses PM_SLEEP in its prepare callback while a UART transmits.  A
dormant chip does not answer SWD, so the pm configurations use
PM_GOVERNOR_EXPLICIT_RELAX to stay out of it for a time after boot.

With RP23XX_PM_QUIESCE_PADS, arm_pminitialize() also isolates the
unused pads and holds the blocks with no driver in reset.  A floating
bank 0 input settles near 2.2V (erratum RP2350-E9) and its input
buffer then draws a static current in every state.

Also select ARCH_HAVE_PM, and fix the LED PM callbacks of three boards,
which used BOARD_LED where the boards define BOARD_LED1.  They did not
build with CONFIG_PM.

fix.subject: arm: sama5: sam_ehci: fix transfer cancellation process.
fix.message:
arm: sama5: sam_ehci: fix transfer cancellation process.

The logic of the conditional expression that determines whether
the QH is a target QH or not is reversed in the process of canceling
a transfer in INPROGRESS state.

Therefore, the QH in INPROGRESS state is not released and subsequent
communication is not successful.

Checked with CDC-ACM driver and cu command.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The sama5 commit 'arm: sama5: sam_ehci: fix transfer cancellation process.' says 'The logic of the conditional expression that determines whether the QH is a target QH or not is reversed in the process of canceling a transfer in INPROGRESS state' and that therefore 'the QH in INPROGRESS state is not released and subsequent communication is not successful'; the listed hunk flips sam_qh_cancel()'s test to 'if (qh->epinfo != epinfo)' (sam_ehci.c line 2724). imxrt_ehci.c line 3149 is in imxrt_qh_cancel(), the same imxrt_qh_foreach() callback that imxrt_cancel() passes at line 4900, and it still returns OK under the comment 'No... keep looking' when qh->epinfo == epinfo, so it skips the QH being cancelled and would unlink and free a non-matching one instead. The companion test that the same commit flipped in sam_cancel() (sam_ehci.c line 4446) is also still pre-fix here, written with the per-controller head: 'if (qh && qh != priv->asynchead)' at line 4846 claims success without searching whenever the asynchronous queue is not empty. Nothing the fix relies on is missing: QHs record their epinfo (line 1894), imxrt_qh_cancel() is built under CONFIG_USBHOST_ASYNCH (line 3131), which IMXRT_USBOTG1 selects (arch/arm/src/imxrt/Kconfig line 571), and the change is plain C logic with no register dependence.
claude.title: imxrt EHCI transfer cancellation tests for the target QH the wrong way round, so a cancelled in-progress transfer is never removed from the schedule.
claude.summary: On 2024-01-20 commit bca8df7d fixed two reversed tests in sama5's EHCI transfer cancellation: sam_qh_cancel() now skips QHs that belong to other endpoints, and sam_cancel() skips the search only when the asynchronous queue is empty. imxrt_ehci.c has the same cancellation code and still has both pre-fix tests: imxrt_qh_cancel() treats the matching QH as 'keep looking' (line 3149), and imxrt_cancel() reports success without searching whenever the queue holds any QH (line 4846). As the sama5 commit message describes, cancelling a bulk or control transfer that is still in progress then leaves its QH linked in the schedule, and later communication with the device fails (the sama5 fix was checked with the CDC-ACM driver and the cu command). The listed hunk is a one-operator change, but the companion test at line 4846 must be flipped as well (with priv->asynchead in place of &g_asynchead) for the search to run at all.

fix.subject: risc-v/bl808, sg2000: Configure MMU to cache Kernel Text, Data and Heap (T-Head C906)
fix.message:
risc-v/bl808, sg2000: Configure MMU to cache Kernel Text, Data and Heap (T-Head C906)

This PR configures the BL808 and SG2000 MMU (inside T-Head C906) to cache the the Kernel Text, Data and Heap.  We set the MMU Flags (Shareable, Bufferable and Cacheable) as explained in this article: https://lupyuen.github.io/articles/plic3#appendix-mmu-caching-for-t-head-c906

This PR fixes the Slow Memory Access for NuttX Kernel in BL808 and SG2000: https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/12696

In the next PR, we will fix the Slow Memory Access for NuttX Apps, by caching the User Text and Data.

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The hunks OR MMU_THEAD_PMA_FLAGS into the kernel text, data and page-pool mappings of bl808_kernel_mappings() and sg2000_kernel_mappings(); the commit message says it configures 'the BL808 and SG2000 MMU (inside T-Head C906) to cache the the Kernel Text, Data and Heap', and the flag is built from PTE bits 60-62 that those files define under '/* T-Head C906 MMU Extensions */' (bl808_mm_init.c lines 45-61). In arch/risc-v/Kconfig, ARCH_CHIP_BL808 and ARCH_CHIP_SG2000 select ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD (lines 472 and 518), and the shared riscv_mmu.h defines the T-Head 'Shareable, Bufferable, Cacheable' PTE bits only under '#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD' (lines 51-53). ARCH_CHIP_JH7110 (line 440) does not select ARCH_MMU_EXT_THEAD, and jh7110_mm_init.c defines no T-Head bits at all: it even maps its I/O region with the plain MMU_IO_FLAGS (line 240), where bl808 and sg2000 need a T-Head strong-order variant. The jh7110 lines 245, 248 and 258 are textually the pre-fix code, but the vendor-specific PTE attributes the fix adds belong to the T-Head MMU extension, which this chip is not configured with.

fix.subject: arch/nrf91: fix compilation for SPI
fix.message:
arch/nrf91: fix compilation for SPI

remove references to unsupported SPI freq and SPI4 which is not supported

lines: /* We are already at this frequency */
/* We are already at this frequency */

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The nrf91 commit "fix compilation for SPI" ("remove references to unsupported SPI freq and SPI4 which is not supported") drops the SPIM4 exception from the >8 MHz limit in setfrequency because NRF91_SPIM4_BASE does not exist on that chip. nrf53_spi_setfrequency() line 787 has the same pre-fix check; on the nRF5340 application core it is correct and needed (NRF53_SPIM4_BASE is defined in nrf53_memorymap_cpuapp.h, the driver has a g_spi4dev instance, SPIM_FREQUENCY_16MBPS/32MBPS exist), so the nrf91 deletion itself must not be copied. But the same driver also builds for the network core: Kconfig offers NRF53_SPI0_MASTER outside "if NRF53_HAVE_SPI1234" (selected only by NRF53_APPCORE), nrf53_memorymap.h then includes nrf53_memorymap_cpunet.h, which defines only NRF53_SPIM0_BASE, and line 787 is under no #ifdef (the only other SPIM4 use, line 394, is inside CONFIG_NRF53_SPI4_MASTER). A net-core build with SPI0 enabled would therefore hit the same undefined SPIM4-base compile error the nrf91 commit fixed; no in-tree *_cpunet defconfig enables SPI, so it is latent, and the adapted fix is a guard (for example on CONFIG_NRF53_SPI4_MASTER) rather than deleting the check.
claude.title: The nRF53 SPI driver uses NRF53_SPIM4_BASE unconditionally, so a network-core build with SPI0 enabled fails to compile.
claude.summary: In March 2024 the nrf91 SPI driver was fixed to build by removing the SPIM4 exception from the >8 MHz frequency limit, because nRF91 has no SPIM4. The nrf53 copy still has the same check at line 787 in nrf53_spi_setfrequency(); it is correct on the nRF5340 application core, which has SPIM4, but the network-core memory map defines only SPIM0 while Kconfig still lets SPI0 be enabled there. In that configuration the driver would fail to compile on an undefined NRF53_SPIM4_BASE, the same error nrf91 had. No in-tree network-core board config enables SPI, so the problem is latent, and the fix has to be a conditional guard rather than the nrf91 deletion. This comes from reading Kconfig and headers only; no network-core build was tried.
claude.impact_note: It is only a compile failure, and only for a network-core configuration with SPI0 enabled, which no in-tree board config uses; application-core builds compile and run unchanged.

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The commit message calls it a "Small fix to compile imxrt_edma_ver2.c correctly also for M33": imxrt/chip.h defines ARMV8M_DCACHE_LINESIZE under CONFIG_ARCH_CORTEXM33 and ARMV7M_DCACHE_LINESIZE only in the #else branch, so the old "EDMA_ALIGN ARMV7M_DCACHE_LINESIZE" did not build for an i.MX RT M33. imx9_edma.c line 89 has the same pre-fix define, and the arm imx9 port can also target a Cortex-M33 (ARCH_CHIP_IMX93_M33 selects ARCH_CORTEXM33), but imx9/chip.h, which imx9_edma.c includes, defines ARMV7M_DCACHE_LINESIZE as 32 with no core condition. So on both imx9 cores EDMA_ALIGN resolves to 32 bytes, the same value the imxrt fix yields on M33, and the build error does not occur; nothing under imx9 defines ARMV8M_DCACHE_LINESIZE, so copying the imxrt change verbatim would instead break the i.MX93 M33 build. The difference lies only in how the chip header is written, so imx9 already avoids the problem another way.

fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32{|f7}/socketcan: fix debugassert for extid frames
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32{|f7}/socketcan: fix debugassert for extid frames

fix debugassert for extid frames, we have to remove
CAN_EFF_FLAG bit from the expression

lines: /* Set up the ID, standard 11-bit or extended 29-bit. */
/* Set up the ID, standard 11-bit or extended 29-bit. */
/* Set up the ID, standard 11-bit or extended 29-bit. */
/* Set up the ID, standard 11-bit or extended 29-bit. */

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The stm32/stm32f7 commit says "fix debugassert for extid frames, we have to remove CAN_EFF_FLAG bit from the expression": inside "if (frame->can_id & CAN_EFF_FLAG)" the ID always carries CAN_EFF_FLAG (0x80000000 in include/nuttx/can.h), so "frame->can_id < (1 << 29)" can never hold and the assertion fires on every extended-ID frame when debug assertions are enabled. at32can_transmit() in at32_can_sock.c has exactly the same branch and assertion at line 892, followed by the same bxCAN-style ID write (ID shifted by CAN_TMI_TMEID_SHIFT plus the ID-type bit), and nothing chip-specific is involved: CAN_EFF_FLAG is already used on line 890 and the corrected expression needs nothing else. Separately, the same CONFIG_NET_CAN_EXTID block uses CAN_TIR_EXID_MASK on line 889, which no header reachable from at32 defines (only STM32 hardware headers do), and the only in-tree at32 socket config (at32f437-mini can_socket) does not enable NET_CAN_EXTID, so this path does not build today and the bug is masked. Once extended-ID support is made to build on at32, the wrong assertion would trip on the first extended frame; the STM32 one-line change can be copied unchanged.
claude.title: The at32 SocketCAN transmit path asserts that an extended CAN ID, still carrying the EFF flag, is below 2^29, which always fails for extended frames.
claude.summary: In October 2024 the stm32 and stm32f7 SocketCAN drivers changed the extended-ID assertion to drop CAN_EFF_FLAG before comparing against 2^29. The at32 copy still asserts frame->can_id < (1 << 29) inside the branch that requires CAN_EFF_FLAG, so with debug assertions on, sending any extended-ID frame would stop the system. Right now this is masked because the same CONFIG_NET_CAN_EXTID block also uses CAN_TIR_EXID_MASK, which at32 does not define, so extended-ID support does not build on at32; whoever fixes that build error will hit the assertion next. The STM32 one-line change applies unchanged.
claude.impact_note: DEBUGASSERT is only active in debug-assertion builds, and on at32 the extended-ID block currently does not compile (line 889 uses an STM32-only macro), so no working build reaches this line today.

fix.subject: arch/arm/src/samv7/sam_mcan.c: fix potential false debug assertions
fix.message:
arch/arm/src/samv7/sam_mcan.c: fix potential false debug assertions

MCAN controller keeps track of empty TX HW FIFO slots in priv->txfsem
semaphore. The semaphore is incremented from TX complete interrupt
and taken before new frame is inserted to the HW FIFO.

There may be a situation when TX HW FIFO is not full but the
semaphore is not yet incremented because the driver didn't handle the
interrupt. I managed to reproduce this issue when sending large
data chunks over CAN bus and keeping the buffers full for most of
the transmission process. This situation leads to the debug assertion
although technically it's not a big issue -> the sending function
waits on the semaphore until it's posted by the interrupt handler.

Moreover, the sanity checks should not be necessary because
mcan_buffer_reserve function will take care of fixing the semaphore
value if it doesn't match with the FIFO.

The entire semaphore logic is a bit weird and probably not
necessary. All we need to do is to check SAM_MCAN_TXFQS register
if there is at least one free slot in the queue. But this would
require a bigger SAMv7 MCAN rewrite, this is rather a hot fix.

Signed-off-by: Michal Lenc <michallenc@seznam.cz>

lines: * REVISIT: Dedicated TX buffers are not supported.
/* As a sanity check, the txfsem should also track the number of elements
* the TX FIFO/queue.  Make sure that they are consistent.
* the TX FIFO/queue. Check only if the value doesn't exceed number of
* FIFO queue members. Sanity check comparing semaphore value with notfull
* flag may not always work, because SAM_MCAN_TXFQS register may signalize
* not full queue before we process the interrupt and increment the
* semaphore. The sanity checks should not be necessary because
* mcan_buffer_reserve function will take care of fixing the semaphore
* value if it doesn't match with the FIFO.
* REVISIT: The entire semaphore logic is a bit weird and probably not
* necessary. All we need to do is to check SAM_MCAN_TXFQS register
* if there is at least one free slot in the queue.
/* As a sanity check, the txfsem should also track the number of elements
* the TX FIFO/queue.  Make sure that they are consistent.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The samv7 commit explains that the TX FIFO can be "not full but the semaphore is not yet incremented because the driver didn't handle the interrupt", which "leads to the debug assertion", and that "mcan_buffer_reserve function will take care of fixing the semaphore value if it doesn't match with the FIFO"; it therefore drops the notfull/sval consistency part of the DEBUGASSERT in mcan_txready(). sama5's mcan_txready() (line 3162) has the identical pre-fix block: it reads SAM_MCAN_TXFQS, derives notfull from MCAN_TXFQS_TFQF, and asserts ((notfull && sval > 0) || (!notfull && sval <= 0)) at lines 3195-3196 under CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES. The same race exists there: txfsem is posted only by mcan_buffer_release(), which mcan_interrupt() calls on TX completion (line 3838), and sama5's mcan_buffer_reserve() has the same resynchronisation (nxsem_reset to 0 or to the FIFO free level) that the commit relies on. Nothing in the change is SAMv7-specific (same register, same bit, same semaphore and config field), so the false assertion can also trigger on sama5 under sustained CAN TX load in debug builds.
claude.title: The SAMA5 MCAN debug check in mcan_txready() can fire falsely when the TX FIFO frees a slot before the TX-complete interrupt has posted the semaphore.
claude.summary: In September 2026 the samv7 MCAN driver relaxed the debug assertion in mcan_txready() so that it only checks that the semaphore count does not exceed the FIFO size, because the hardware can report a free TX FIFO slot before the interrupt handler has incremented txfsem. The sama5 MCAN driver has the same code and still asserts that the FIFO-not-full flag and the semaphore count agree. With CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES and debug assertions enabled, keeping the CAN TX queue full (for example when sending large data) can make the assertion fire and halt the system although nothing is wrong. Release builds are not affected, and the samv7 change can be copied as is.
claude.impact_note: The check is compiled only with CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES and halts only builds with debug assertions enabled; release builds behave the same, and the commit itself says "technically it's not a big issue".

fix.message:

chromakey is a uint32_t, so printing it with %d warns.  The line is only
compiled when CONFIG_STM32_FB_CMAP is enabled, which is why it has gone
unnoticed.

Signed-off-by: Jorge Guzman <jorge.gzm@gmail.com>

lines: lcderr("ERROR: Clut index %d is out of range\n", oinfo->chromakey);
lcderr("ERROR: Clut index %" PRIu32 " is out of range\n",
lcderr("ERROR: Clut index %d is out of range\n", oinfo->chromakey);

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The stm32h7 commit only changes the printf format in an error message; its message says "chromakey is a uint32_t, so printing it with %d warns", and the line is only compiled with CONFIG_STM32_FB_CMAP. The stm32f7 copy at line 2657 has the same lcderr() call with %d, and chromakey is declared uint32_t in include/nuttx/video/fb.h, but the surrounding logic (the range check on line 2655 and ret = -EINVAL on line 2658) is unaffected by the format string. No -Werror is set in the arm toolchain files or tools/Config.mk, so the mismatch is a compiler warning, not a build failure, and at run time at most the logged index text would differ for values above INT_MAX. Per the guide, a change that only silences a warning or changes printing without altering runtime behaviour is not a bug fix.

refs.quote: lcderr("ERROR: Clut index %d is out of range\n", oinfo->chromakey);

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The commit message is only "Fix #11005"; its two hunks replace the undeclared local "privep" in stm32_ep_allocbuffer()/stm32_ep_freebuffer() with "((struct stm32_ep_s *)ep)->epphy", which is a build fix: neither function declares privep. efm32_ep_allocbuffer() (line 4387) and efm32_ep_freebuffer() (line 4408) are the same CONFIG_USBDEV_DMA functions and still use privep->epphy at lines 4389 and 4410 with no privep declared (privep appears only as a parameter name of other functions); the neighbouring efm32_ep_freereq() already uses the correct cast form at line 4374. The error appears whenever usbtrace() is a real function, i.e. with CONFIG_USBDEV_TRACE or CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES plus CONFIG_DEBUG_USB (include/nuttx/usb/usbdev_trace.h); otherwise the macro discards its arguments. Nothing makes this inapplicable to efm32: USBDEV_DMA in drivers/usbdev/Kconfig depends only on USBDEV, efm32_usbdev.c wires both functions into its ops table under CONFIG_USBDEV_DMA, and struct efm32_ep_s has the epphy field.
claude.title: The EFM32 USB device driver uses an undeclared variable privep in its DMA buffer alloc/free functions, so it fails to build with USB DMA and USB tracing enabled.
claude.summary: In October 2023 the stm32 OTG HS device driver fixed its allocbuffer/freebuffer functions, which referred to a local variable privep that is never declared, by casting the ep argument instead. The efm32 USB device driver has the same two functions with the same undeclared privep at lines 4389 and 4410. With CONFIG_USBDEV_DMA and either USB tracing or USB debug output enabled, usbtrace() is a real call and efm32_usbdev.c stops compiling; without tracing the bad expression is dropped by the macro. The stm32 change can be copied with only the struct name changed to efm32_ep_s.
claude.impact_note: It only breaks compilation when CONFIG_USBDEV_DMA is combined with USB tracing or USB debug output; it does not change how a working build behaves.

fix.subject: arch/mips/pic32mz: convert the Ethernet driver to netdev_lowerhalf.
fix.message:
arch/mips/pic32mz: convert the Ethernet driver to netdev_lowerhalf.

Convert the PIC32MZ Ethernet MAC driver from the legacy net_driver_s
model to the netdev_lowerhalf_s model, registered with
netdev_lower_register().

Each descriptor owns a DMA buffer of its own.  A received frame is copied
to a netpkt in the receive() operation, which takes the descriptors in
ring order, and the descriptor is given back to the hardware at once; the
interrupt only notifies the upper half.  A packet to send is copied to the
buffer of the next TX descriptor and held until the descriptor is
reclaimed, so the TX quota is the number of TX descriptors and the upper
half never queues more than the ring can take.  The reclaim operation
and the TX done interrupt release the descriptors that were sent.

The RX descriptor ring handling and the TX done fixes already in the
driver are kept.  The TX timeout still resets the interface; the packets
held for the TX descriptors are released when the interface is reset or
taken down.

The packet buffer list, the poll, the response and the txavail logic are
no longer needed and are removed.

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-sonnet-5-5
Signed-off-by: Daniel P. Carvalho <danieloak@gmail.com>

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit "arch/mips/pic32mz: convert the Ethernet driver to netdev_lowerhalf." says it converts the driver "from the legacy net_driver_s model to the netdev_lowerhalf_s model", that "The RX descriptor ring handling and the TX done fixes already in the driver are kept", and that the buffer list, poll, response and txavail logic "are no longer needed and are removed". The selected hunks are mechanical parts of that conversion: the driver struct swaps pd_pollwork, pd_freebuffers and the net_driver_s for a mutex, a per-descriptor TX packet array and a netdev_lowerhalf_s; the prototypes change to the lower-half operations; and NETDEV_RXERRORS/NETDEV_TXERRORS(&priv->pd_dev) become (&priv->pd_dev.netdev) only because pd_dev changed type. pic32mx_ethernet.c still consistently uses the legacy model (struct net_driver_s pd_dev at line 312, devif_poll() at line 1187, d_txavail at line 3195, netdev_register() at line 3232), so there &priv->pd_dev is already the correct argument to the statistics macros. Carrying this over would be a driver-model conversion (refactor/new feature), not a missed bug fix.

fix.subject: rp2040/rp23xx: implement stall queueing and GET STATUS responses
fix.message:
rp2040/rp23xx: implement stall queueing and GET STATUS responses

Two device-controller defects that break standard host error recovery,
found while root-causing why macOS never mounts a NuttX mass-storage
function (full analysis and host traces in apache/nuttx#19435):

1. epsubmit() aborted (-EBUSY) any IN request submitted while the
   endpoint was halted.  The mass storage class halts bulk-IN for a
   failed device-to-host command (BOT-legal) and then submits the CSW;
   the CSW was dropped on the floor, so after the host's Clear-Halt the
   endpoint NAKed forever and the host timed out (macOS: 30 s, then a
   Bulk-Only-reset/device-reset spiral until it disables the port).
   This is exactly the race documented for years in the usbmsc_scsi.c
   header (David Hewson's analysis); the USBMSC_STALL_RACEWAR sleep
   workaround only survives hosts that clear the halt within 100 ms --
   Linux does, macOS does not, which is why Linux testing never saw it.

   Implement the stall-queueing contract instead: requests submitted
   while an endpoint is halted are queued without arming the hardware
   (arming rewrites the buffer control word and would silently clear
   the STALL bit); a halt terminates any in-flight IN transfer (its
   hardware buffer is disarmed by the STALL write and would never
   complete); clearing the halt resets the data toggle and re-arms the
   head of the queue; stale buffer completions latched for transfers
   aborted by a halt are ignored.  RP2040/RP23XX now select
   ARCH_USBDEV_STALLQUEUE, which also retires the RACEWAR's two 100 ms
   sleeps per failed command.

2. The USB_REQ_GETSTATUS handler in ep0setup() validated the request
   but never queued the two-byte response, for all three recipients
   (device/interface/endpoint), so EP0 NAKed the host's data stage
   forever and every GET STATUS timed out.  macOS issues GetPipeStatus
   = GET STATUS(endpoint) on a halted pipe before running Bulk-Only
   reset recovery and hit this on every probe; lsusb -v's device-status
   query hangs on it as well.  Send the response: endpoint recipient
   reports the halt bit, device recipient reports self-powered,
   interface reports zeros; the status stage is armed by handle_zlp()
   exactly as for class-dispatched IN transfers.

Validated on RP2350 silicon (Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, composite
CDC-ACM + CDC-NCM + USBMSC): pre-fix, a raw-usbfs replay of macOS's
sequence and timing reproduced both defects deterministically (CSW read
ETIMEDOUT after a delayed clear-halt; all GET STATUS variants
ETIMEDOUT).  Post-fix: the CSW survives the halt and is delivered after
Clear-Halt with correct tag/status/residue across a post-stall delay
sweep of 0-1000 ms; all GET STATUS variants answer immediately with
correct halt reporting; no regressions in the exact-length SCSI suite,
Bulk-Only reset, FAT mount and full reads, CDC-NCM/ACM, or warm
reboots; and macOS now mounts the volume (together with the companion
usbmsc fixes).  The rp2040 driver shares the code and receives the
identical fix (build-tested).

Assisted-by: Claude (Anthropic Claude Code)
Signed-off-by: Ricard Rosson <ricard@groundbits.com>

claude.title: The cxd56 USB device driver still throws away IN requests submitted while the endpoint is halted, so a mass-storage status reply can be lost.
claude.summary: On 2026-07-28 the rp2040 and rp23xx USB device drivers stopped rejecting IN requests that arrive while an endpoint is halted: they now keep them queued and send them once the host clears the halt, because the mass storage class submits its status reply (CSW) while bulk-IN is still halted. The cxd56 driver still rejects such requests with -EBUSY in cxd56_epsubmit(), and its resume path only clears the STALL bit. The CXD56 does not declare stall queueing, so the mass storage class falls back to a 100 ms sleep workaround; if the host clears the halt later than that, the status reply is dropped and the host waits, times out and resets the device (the commit reports this with macOS). The fix has to be rewritten for this different controller, which starts IN transfers from an IN-token interrupt and can also clear the halt in hardware; how this controller treats a STALL while NAK is cleared cannot be checked from the repository.

claude.title: The RISC-V RP23xx USB device driver still throws away IN requests submitted while the endpoint is halted, so a mass-storage status reply can be lost.
claude.summary: On 2026-07-28 the arm rp2040 and rp23xx USB device drivers were changed to keep IN requests that arrive while an endpoint is halted and send them once the host clears the halt, because the mass storage class submits its status reply (CSW) while bulk-IN is still halted. The RISC-V build of the same RP23xx chip uses its own copy of the driver, which still rejects those requests with -EBUSY in rp23xx_epsubmit() and does not restart anything when the halt clears; its chip option also does not declare stall queueing. With a host that clears the halt later than the mass storage class's 100 ms workaround allows (the commit reports macOS), the status reply is lost, the host times out and resets the device, and the volume never mounts. The port needs the epsubmit change plus the matching re-arm on halt clear (and preferably the related halt-time cancel), written for this copy's spinlock-based locking rather than copied line for line.

fix.subject: esp32s3: add simple boot support
fix.message:
esp32s3: add simple boot support

The Simple Boot feature for Espressif chips is a method of booting
that doesn't depend on a 2nd stage bootloader. Its not the
intention to replace a 2nd stage bootloader such as MCUboot and
ESP-IDF bootloader, but to have a minimal and straight-forward way
of booting, and also simplify the building.

This commit also removes deprecated code and makes this bootloader
configuration as default for esp32s3 targets and removes the need
for running 'make bootloader' command for it.

Other related fix, but not directly to Simple Boot:
- Instrumentation is required to run from IRAM to support it during
initialization. `is_eco0` function also needs to run from IRAM.
- `rtc.data` section placement was fixed.
- Provide arch-defined interfaces for efuses, in order to decouple
board config level from arch-defined values.

Signed-off-by: Almir Okato <almir.okato@espressif.com>

The listed hunk only renames the type of the local chip pointer in esp32s3_spiflash_alloc_mtdpart() to esp_rom_spiflash_chip_t to follow that header change; the struct is used the same way and no behaviour changes. In esp32c3-legacy, the matching line 654 uses esp32c3_spiflash_chip_t, which is still defined in its own rom/esp32c3_spiflash.h (line 136) and is the type of the chip member of struct spiflash_legacy_data_s (line 152) that line 669 points at, so the code is consistent and builds. A type rename that follows a header migration is a refactor, not a bug fix.

fix.subject: arch/xtensa/esp32s3: fix USB OTG request lifecycle on SMP
fix.message:
arch/xtensa/esp32s3: fix USB OTG request lifecycle on SMP

The IN endpoint completed a request as soon as all bytes had been
written to the TxFIFO, before the corresponding XFRC interrupt.  The
class driver could then release or reuse the request while the
controller was still transmitting it.  On SMP, the request queue and
active state could also be changed concurrently from the interrupt and
task contexts.

Keep IN requests in flight until XFRC, account the bytes completed by
the controller, and complete the request only when all bytes have been
transmitted.  Clear active/in-flight state when requests are cancelled,
including the path where the hardware has already disabled the IN
endpoint, so the next submit can re-arm the endpoint.  Return cancelled
requests through esp32s3_req_complete() to preserve EP0 stall
semantics, and protect the request queues with a controller lock.

Without this, an SMP build can hang when a host opens the CDC ACM port
while the target is continuously sending IN data.

Fixes: #18541

Assisted-by: DeepSeek (deepseek-flash)
Signed-off-by: liu <liu334275@gmail.com>

claude.evidence: The commit is "arch/xtensa/esp32s3: fix USB OTG request lifecycle on SMP" and says "Without this, an SMP build can hang when a host opens the CDC ACM port while the target is continuously sending IN data"; ESP32-S3 selects ARCH_HAVE_MULTICPU (arch/xtensa/Kconfig line 113) and SMP depends on it (sched/Kconfig line 416), but ARCH_CHIP_AT32 (arch/arm/Kconfig lines 1009-1021, one Cortex-M4) does not, and at32_otgfsdev.c has no spinlock at all. fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32: fix PTP multicast filter and RX/TX frame routing

- Under CONFIG_NET_PROMISCUOUS, forward all control frames
  (ETH_MACFFR_PCF_ALL) instead of only non-PAUSE ones, so link-local
  PTP multicast reaches the DMA.

claude.label: missing

The fix needs nothing the AT32 side lacks: at32_eth.h defines the same PCF field including ETH_MACFFR_PCF_ALL ('Forwards all control frames'), and every received frame is handed to packet sockets through pkt_input(), the path the fixed driver uses for PTP (Ethertype 0x88f7) frames. claude.title: AT32 Ethernet promiscuous mode still blocks non-PAUSE control frames, so link-local multicast such as PTP may never reach the host.
claude.summary: On 2026-09-21 the shared STM32 F1/F2/F4 Ethernet driver (stm32_eth_m3m4_v1.c, commit d357c5454) changed its promiscuous-mode frame filter to ETH_MACFFR_PCF_ALL so that all control frames are forwarded and link-local PTP multicast reaches the DMA. at32_eth.c still uses (ETH_MACFFR_PCF_PAUSE | ETH_MACFFR_PM) under CONFIG_NET_PROMISCUOUS and programs MACFFR the same way, with identical PCF definitions in its header. With promiscuous mode enabled, frames the MAC treats as control frames (per the commit, including link-local PTP multicast) are dropped before they reach the network stack or packet sockets, so L2 PTP or similar link-local protocols run over packet sockets would not receive them. Confidence is limited because AT32 has no hardware PTP support in this driver, the problem only exists with CONFIG_NET_PROMISCUOUS, and the effect on PTP frames is stated only by the commit message and the header comments, not by anything visible for this chip.

fix.subject: arch/arm/imxrt: fix eDMA NCE error caused by zero-length split transfer
fix.message:
arch/arm/imxrt: fix eDMA NCE error caused by zero-length split transfer

- In imxrt_dma_send(), verify dev->dmatx.nlength > 0 before setting up
  a chained TCD. Chaining a TCD with iter == 0 causes eDMA NCE errors
  and halts the eDMA engine when HOE is enabled.
- In imxrt_dmaterminate(), clear CITER and BITER registers so residual
  zero-iteration states do not trigger repeated NCE errors on channel
  re-activation.
- In imxrt_dmach_xfrsetup(), return -EINVAL if config->iter is 0.

Fixes #20881

Signed-off-by: Sarthak Pandey <sarthakpandey5667@gmail.com>

lines: /* Allocate a TCD, waiting if necessary */
/* Get the eDMA Error Status register value. */
/* Allocate a TCD, waiting if necessary */
*   This function checks the TCD (Task Control Descriptor) status for a
*   specified eDMA channel and returns the number of major loop counts

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The selected hunk adds 'if (config->iter == 0) return -EINVAL;' to imxrt_dmach_xfrsetup(); the commit message lists it among the fixes for eDMA NCE errors, explaining that a TCD 'with iter == 0 causes eDMA NCE errors and halts the eDMA engine when HOE is enabled'. imx9_dmach_xfrsetup() in imx9_edma.c is the same function (same DEBUGASSERT/dmainfo prologue, then flags, TCD allocation and imx9_tcd_configure()), and imx9_tcd_configure() copies config->iter unchecked into tcd->citer and tcd->biter; there is no other iteration-count check in imx9_edma.c. What the fix guards against exists on i.MX9: the included imx95_edma.h defines EDMA_CH_ES_NCE ('NBYTES/CITER Configuration Error (NCE)') and EDMA_CSR_HAE ('Halt After Error'), which imx9_edma.c sets under CONFIG_IMX9_EDMA_HOE (default y). A zero count can reach the function on i.MX9: imx9_lpi2c_dma_data_configure() sets config.iter = msg->length and is called for every message that has a START command, including zero-length ones, while the LPUART split-transfer trigger named in the commit is already guarded there with nlength > 0, so only this API check is missing.
claude.title: imx9_dmach_xfrsetup() accepts a zero iteration count and programs an eDMA transfer descriptor with CITER/BITER = 0.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-23 the i.MX RT eDMA driver (commit d9a2e4225) made imxrt_dmach_xfrsetup() return -EINVAL when config->iter is 0, because a transfer descriptor with a zero iteration count raises the eDMA NCE error and, with Halt On Error, stops the eDMA engine. The i.MX9 copy imx9_dmach_xfrsetup() has no such check, and imx9_tcd_configure() writes config->iter straight into CITER/BITER; the i.MX95 eDMA header defines the same NCE error, and the Halt After Error option IMX9_EDMA_HOE defaults to on. On i.MX9 a zero count can arrive from the LPI2C DMA path, which uses msg->length as the count for every message including zero-length ones (the LPUART case from the original report is already guarded). Such a transfer would put the channel into an NCE error and, with the default halt-on-error setting, could make the eDMA ignore all service requests until the halt is cleared, affecting every DMA user; the exact hardware reaction is taken from the commit message and the header descriptions, and how often zero-length I2C messages are sent with DMA enabled is not visible in the repository.

claude.summary: On 2026-10-23 commit d9a2e4225 made imxrt_dmach_xfrsetup() return -EINVAL when config->iter is 0, because a TCD with a zero iteration count raises the eDMA NBYTES/CITER configuration error and, with halt on error, stops the eDMA engine. On 2026-10-26 the serial part of that fix was ported to imx9_lpuart.c, but imx9_dmach_xfrsetup() is still the unguarded copy that writes config->iter into CITER and BITER, on an eDMA that defines the same NCE error and a Halt After Error bit the driver sets by default. With LPI2C DMA enabled, a zero-length I2C message becomes a data TCD with iter 0; this would raise the configuration error, end that transfer with -EIO, and with HAE stop servicing all eDMA channels, since the driver has no code that clears HALT. Whether applications actually send zero-length I2C messages is not visible in this repository, and nothing was run on hardware.

fix.subject: arch/arm/stm32h7: add the PTP hardware clock of the Ethernet MAC.
fix.message:
arch/arm/stm32h7: add the PTP hardware clock of the Ethernet MAC.

The MAC has a system time that is the base of the PTP hardware
timestamps, but the driver never started it, and STM32_ETH_PTP only
printed a warning.

Add the registers of the timestamp unit and start the system time with
the fine update method and the digital rollover, so that the nanoseconds
count up to 10^9. The increment is 2 * 10^9 / HCLK ns, and the addend
makes the update rate half of HCLK, which leaves room to trim the
frequency in both directions. The time starts at zero right after the MAC
reset, not with the MAC configuration, so it does not depend on the PHY
having a link. The reset clears it, so it starts again each time the
interface goes up.

With STM32_ETH_PTP_GPIO, start the pulse-per-second output as a pulse
train with a period of one second and a width of half of it, at the whole
seconds of the system time. The fixed frequency mode of the MAC gives a
pulse too short to be seen, so the flexible mode is used. The interrupt
of the timestamp unit is not enabled in the MAC: it is set each time the
target time of the PPS output is reached and is cleared by reading
MACTSSR, which the interrupt handler does not do, so it would stay
pending and keep the handler running until the network stops.

Register /dev/ptp0 when CONFIG_PTP_CLOCK is set, so that a PTP daemon can
read and set the system time and correct its frequency and its phase.
The frequency is corrected by changing the addend, by up to 50% each way.
A step of the time is added or subtracted with the update register; with
the digital rollover a subtraction is programmed with the negated seconds
and with 10^9 minus the nanoseconds. The pulse train counts by itself, so
it does not follow a step of the system time and would be displaced by the
same amount: after the time is set or stepped, it is started again at the
next whole second.

With HCLK at 200 MHz the system time advanced 10.0018 s while a host
clock advanced 10.002 s, and the pulse train was seen on the pin. Reading,
setting, steps of +0.5 s and -1.25 s and a change of 100 ppm were done
through /dev/ptp0 on hardware, and the edges of the PPS output stayed at
the whole seconds of the system time.

Signed-off-by: Daniel P. Carvalho <danieloak@gmail.com>
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-sonnet-5

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: Commit e2d5b8f29 is titled "add the PTP hardware clock of the Ethernet MAC" and says that before it "the driver never started it, and STM32_ETH_PTP only printed a warning"; it adds a new feature (starting the MAC system time, a PPS pulse train and a /dev/ptp0 clock), not a correction of existing behaviour. The picked hunk only adds the forward declaration `static int  stm32_eth_ptp_init(void);` under #ifdef CONFIG_STM32_ETH_PTP for a function that the same commit introduces. The lines matched in lpc43_ethernet.c are merely the neighbouring unchanged prototypes of lpc43_ethgpioconfig() and lpc43_ethreset(), so there is no shared pre-fix logic and nothing to carry over as a fix. For context, lpc43_ethernet.c still has the warning that CONFIG_LPC43_ETH_PTP is not yet supported, so PTP is simply an unimplemented feature there as well.

fix.subject: arch/arm/imxrt: a fixed link when no PHY answers
fix.message:
arch/arm/imxrt: a fixed link when no PHY answers

A carrier with a switch port wired MAC to MAC has no PHY on MDIO, and
ifup failed. With IMXRT_ENET_FIXED_LINK the configured PHY, or the
board's PHY list, is tried first; if none answers the MAC runs at
100 Mbps full duplex and SIOCGMIIREG reports the link up, so the
network monitor keeps the interface up.

Signed-off-by: Royyan Zahir <royzah@gmail.com>

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit adds an opt-in feature rather than correcting wrong behaviour: its message says that with IMXRT_ENET_FIXED_LINK, 'if none answers the MAC runs at 100 Mbps full duplex and SIOCGMIIREG reports the link up', and the new Kconfig option IMXRT_ENET_FIXED_LINK is 'default n' (imxrt Kconfig lines 2739 and 2741). All three picked hunks only change behaviour when that option is set: the SIOCGMIIREG branch sits inside '#ifdef CONFIG_IMXRT_ENET_FIXED_LINK', and in imxrt_initphy 'bool fixed = false;' is only changed under that option, so 'fixed || BOARD_PHY_ISDUPLEX(phydata)' and '!fixed && BOARD_PHY_10BASET(phydata)' reduce to the old conditions by default. The imx6 driver matches the default behaviour that imxrt keeps: SIOCGMIIREG reads the real PHY (line 1787), duplex and speed come from the PHY status (lines 2321, 2336, 2343), and imx_initphy returns -ENOENT when the PHY does not answer (line 2071). imx6 has no fixed-link option in its driver or Kconfig, so carrying this over would mean adding support for a PHY-less MAC-to-MAC wiring, not fixing a missed bug.
