fix.subject: samv7: ensure the correct location of message RAM
fix.message:
samv7: ensure the correct location of message RAM

The message RAM does not behave correctly if lower 16 bits of
buffer address overflow (upper 16 bits are set once in matrix driver
for the entire CAN driver). For example message RAM starting at
0x2040fc20 would not work for buffers that go beyond 0x20410000 and
MCAN would sent data located at 0x20400000 to the network. The same
issue would occur even if TX buffers would start directly at 0x20410000.
The upper 16 bits would still have 0x2040 value because of RX buffers
located in 0x2040ffff range.

This commit ensures the RAM is always located at the beginning of
the data section and thus the overflow mentioned above should never occur.
The alternative would be to use larger alignment, but the message RAM
can have up to 4352 words and this would cause a significant padding.

The RAM is also initialized to zero to ensure valid parity/ECC checksums.
The address issue is not described anywhere in the manual, so it is
possible this is caused by some incorrect configuration, but the context
of the registers looks valid.

This commit also fixes the compilation errors when the driver is run
without data cache.

Signed-off-by: Michal Lenc <michallenc@seznam.cz>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunks are the driver half of a real fix: SAMv7 put g_mcan0_msgram/g_mcan1_msgram into a '.mcan' section that its board linker scripts place at the start of .data (the start of SRAM, after an optional RAM vector table), because each buffer start is programmed as a 16-bit offset under one shared upper-16-bit base, and with a message RAM crossing a 64 KB boundary 'MCAN would sent data located at 0x20400000 to the network' (commit message). The SAMA5 copy uses the same addressing: MAILBOX_ADDRESS keeps only the low 16 bits (line 700), and sam_mcan_initialize() writes a single MSB taken from msgram.stdfilters into SFR_CAN (lines 4342 and 4366; hardware/sam_sfr.h line 249 'Bits 0-15: MSB CAN0 Base Address'), exactly like the SAMv7 MATRIX CAN0DMABA write. Its message RAM arrays (lines 998-1003 and 1089-1094) are still plain .bss arrays with only cache-line alignment, and nothing in the driver checks that they stay inside one 64 KB window, so the same failure can occur when the link places an array across a boundary. The fix must be adapted: no SAMA5 board linker script has a .mcan section, and e.g. sama5d2-xult uboot.ld puts .data right after .text in SDRAM, so 'start of .data' is not 64 KB aligned as SRAM start is on SAMv7; the zero-initialization part adds little because the arrays stay in .bss, which arm_data_initialize() already clears. Confidence is medium because the commit itself says the issue 'is not described anywhere in the manual' and whether a given SAMA5 image straddles a boundary depends on its layout.
claude.title: The SAMA5 MCAN message RAM arrays are not kept inside one 64 KB window, although the controller only gets 16-bit buffer offsets under a single upper-16-bit base.
claude.summary: In February 2025 (commit ef469bac) the SAMv7 MCAN driver moved its message RAM arrays into a '.mcan' section at the start of .data and zero-initialized them, because buffers lying past a 64 KB boundary were accessed at the wrong address and wrong data went out on the CAN bus. The SAMA5 copy of the driver programs the same 16-bit offsets and a single upper-16-bit base in SFR_CAN, but its g_mcan0_msgram and g_mcan1_msgram are still ordinary arrays placed wherever the linker puts them. If an array crosses a 64 KB boundary, the filters, receive FIFOs or transmit buffers after the boundary are read and written at the wrong memory address, so frames could be sent with wrong data or received into unrelated memory. The SAMv7 change cannot be copied as is, because SAMA5 linker scripts have no .mcan section and .data does not start on a 64 KB boundary there; a SAMA5-specific placement or alignment is needed. The commit notes the behaviour is not documented in the manual, so a hardware check on SAMA5 would confirm it.

claude.evidence: The picked hunk is the 'Fix compilation' part of the commit: in 'locate_data(".lpram"), aligned(16);' the comma ends the first declarator, so 'aligned(16)' is parsed as a second declarator with a number as its parameter list, which is not valid C; the fix writes 'locate_data(".lpram") aligned_data(16);' instead. For GCC, include/nuttx/compiler.h defines aligned_data(n) as __attribute__((aligned(n))) (line 368) and locate_data(n) as __attribute__((section(n))) (line 372), and there is no macro named 'aligned' that could make the old text valid. samd5e5/sam_dmac.c has the identical declarations of g_base_desc, g_writeback_desc and g_dma_desc (lines 141, 143 and 151), and Make.defs compiles that file whenever CONFIG_SAMD5E5_DMAC is set (lines 72-73), so it fails to build under the same condition. No in-tree samd5e5 defconfig enables SAMD5E5_DMAC, which may be why the error is unnoticed; the CHINTENCLR change in the same commit is not part of this pair.
claude.title: The SAMD5E5 DMA driver declares its LPRAM descriptor tables with invalid syntax and does not compile when DMA is enabled.
claude.summary: In November 2023 (commit f5374e71) the SAMD2L2 DMA driver changed 'locate_data(".lpram"), aligned(16);' to 'locate_data(".lpram") aligned_data(16);' to fix the build. The SAMD5E5 copy still has the old text on all three descriptor tables (g_base_desc, g_writeback_desc and g_dma_desc), where the stray comma turns 'aligned(16)' into an invalid second declarator. As a result any configuration with CONFIG_SAMD5E5_DMAC enabled fails to compile sam_dmac.c, so DMA cannot be used on SAMD5E5 until the same three-line change is made. No in-tree SAMD5E5 board configuration enables DMA, which is likely why this has not been reported.
claude.impact_note: The wrong declaration syntax only breaks compilation of sam_dmac.c when CONFIG_SAMD5E5_DMAC is enabled; it cannot produce wrong runtime behaviour.

claude.evidence: The five candidate hunks of this Espressif RISC-V I2S refactor make i2s_buf_free return int and free heap-allocated lldesc_t DMA descriptors, return the nxsem_post result, replace apb_free(bfcontainer->apb) in the RX worker with kmm_free(bfcontainer->buf) plus a TX/RX channel-stop sequence, and log when i2s_buf_free fails. The return-type and logging parts do not change behaviour, and the descriptor freeing only pairs with the descriptor allocation that the same commit adds to i2s_buf_allocate (the old code embedded the descriptors in the container), so no pre-existing leak is fixed. The rp23xx driver is TX-only (its ops table has only TX methods and no receive), its buffer container has no dma_link or buf field, and its DMA reads straight from apb->samp, so there is no internal buffer or descriptor to free. The matching apb_free/i2s_buf_free lines sit in the TX worker and cleanup paths, where apb_free releases the reference taken by apb_reference in rp23xx_i2s_send, so the text match is not the same logic, and the channel-stop sequence relies on the ESP TX and RX channels sharing WS/BCLK, which this PIO-based TX-only driver does not have.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: Most of the 30 candidate hunks, including the six listed (lldesc_t descriptor pointers, GDMA channel handles, prototypes, non-const config, descriptor allocation and freeing), belong to the RISC-V move from esp_dma_* with embedded esp_dmadesc_s descriptors to the GDMA driver with cache-aligned heap lldesc_t descriptors, or only change return types and logging; the Xtensa driver keeps embedded descriptors with its own chip DMA paths, already takes sclk from clk_hz instead of the clock-source enum, and had its RX path reworked separately for ESP32-S3 (commit 3b1aac55a), so those parts do not apply, and the frame-based TX carry and cache alignment in i2s_txdma_setup are not clearly needed here and are not counted. The hunk near line 2295 of the changed file (i2s_txsamplerate and i2s_rxsamplerate) adds an early 'if (rate == 0) return priv->rate;', documented on the fixed side as 'If rate is 0, the current sample rate is returned.' The I2S character driver implements I2SIOC_GTXSAMPLERATE by calling I2S_TXSAMPLERATE(priv->i2s, 0) (likewise for RX), and the ESP32/S2/S3 boards register i2schar on the device returned by esp_i2sbus_initialize from this Xtensa driver. Here i2s_txsamplerate and i2s_rxsamplerate still have the pre-fix logic: they stop the channel, store 0 in priv->rate and call i2s_check_mclkfrequency, which evaluates priv->mclk_freq % priv->rate, a division by zero. The fix needs only priv->rate, which exists on this side, so this part is judged a missed fix.

claude.title: The ESP32/S2/S3 I2S driver treats a sample-rate query (rate 0) as a set request and then divides by zero.
claude.summary: The Espressif RISC-V I2S driver was refactored in October 2025 (commit fb93a9e4); among many changes, i2s_txsamplerate and i2s_rxsamplerate now return the current rate when called with rate 0, which is how the I2S character driver implements its get-sample-rate ioctls. The Xtensa common driver, which ESP32, ESP32-S2 and ESP32-S3 boards use and expose as /dev/i2scharN, still has the old code: it stops the channel, stores 0 in priv->rate and calls i2s_check_mclkfrequency, which computes priv->mclk_freq % priv->rate. A get-sample-rate ioctl on these boards therefore divides by zero (undefined behaviour, likely a crash) and in any case overwrites the configured rate with 0 after stopping the channel. Only the early return for rate 0 needs to be carried over, adapted to this driver; the matching zero handling for data width and channel count is in other hunks of the same commit, and the rest of the candidate hunks belong to the RISC-V move to the GDMA driver and do not apply. This conclusion comes from reading the code paths only; nothing was built or run.

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The imxrt commit 'Fix correct LPSPI DMA transfer size for 16-bit' changes the word-to-byte conversion from nwords << 2 to nwords << 1 ('Fix byte count calculation for 16-bit SPI words using shift-by-1 instead of shift-by-2') and, in the same commit, sets config.iter to nwords for both DMA channels ('Use word count instead of byte count for DMA iteration config'). s32k1xx_lpspi_exchange (the CONFIG_S32K1XX_LPSPI_DMA variant) has exactly the pre-fix code: nbytes = (priv->nbits > 8) ? nwords << 2 : nwords, used for the DMA threshold and as config.iter of both the RX and TX channels, while each minor loop moves config.nbytes = adjust = 2 bytes with 16-bit transfers. The s32k1xx eDMA header documents iter as the major loop iteration count and nbytes as the bytes per minor loop, so for nbits > 8 the DMA runs 4 * nwords 16-bit transfers, four times the 2 * nwords bytes of the caller's buffers. Words wider than 8 bits are valid here (setbits accepts 2..4096 bits and the exchange comment says such data is packed into uint16_t), the DMA path is a normal Kconfig option (S32K1XX_LPSPI_DMA), and nothing else in the function compensates, so the fix applies unchanged apart from names.

claude.title: S32K1xx LPSPI DMA transfers four times too many words when SPI words are wider than 8 bits.
claude.summary: In February 2026 the i.MX RT LPSPI driver fixed its DMA exchange for words wider than 8 bits: the byte count became nwords << 1 instead of nwords << 2, and the DMA iteration count became nwords instead of that byte count. The S32K1xx LPSPI driver has the same DMA exchange code before that fix: it computes nbytes = nwords << 2 and uses it as the eDMA major loop count for both channels, while each loop moves one 16-bit word. With CONFIG_S32K1XX_LPSPI_DMA enabled and 16-bit words, a transfer above the DMA threshold therefore clocks four times as many words as requested, reads past the end of the transmit buffer and very likely writes past the end of the receive buffer, corrupting memory. The whole imxrt commit (the shift and the two config.iter lines) can be carried over with only the names changed. This is judged from the code only; nothing was built or run on hardware.
claude.same_problem_note: Same DMA word-count code in s32k1xx_lpspi.c as nuttx-194: the same fix was made in the i.MX9 LPSPI driver on 2024-10-23 and in the i.MX RT driver on 2026-02-18.

claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The STM32 commit says 'The maximum timeout was computed as (1 << resolution) - 1, which shifts a 32-bit value by 32 for 32-bit timers (undefined behaviour)', and changes the shift to 64 bits; on the STM32 side the resolution comes from STM32_TIMx_RES, which can be 32. n32_start in the N32H7 capture driver has the same expression, but every one of its 14 lower-half instances (ATIM1-4, GTIMA1-7, GTIMB1-3) is statically initialised with .resolution = 16, and the resolution field is never assigned anywhere else in the file. claude.label_text: Not needed: different chip, device or board
claude.evidence: The listed hunks rewrite imx9_lpi2c_reset: the commit message says the old GPIO recovery 'tried to toggle scl line as GPIO, but the line was not even muxed properly' and replaces it with relaxed mode plus address-0 start/stop sequences, stating '"Relaxed mode" is a new feature on the LPI2C block used in imx93'; the config-table hunks only drop reset_scl_pin/reset_sda_pin, which the rewrite no longer uses. The new code depends on LPI2C_MCFG0_RELAX (MCFGR0 bit 16), which the imx9 header defines, while the imxrt LPI2C header (included unconditionally by imxrt_lpi2c.c for every imxrt family) stops the MCFGR0 bits at RDMO (bit 9) followed by 'Bits 31-10 Reserved', and nothing under arch/arm/src/imxrt defines an LPI2C relax bit, so the fix cannot be carried over. The stated root cause does not appear on imxrt either: imxrt_lpi2c_reset configures the reset pins with imxrt_config_gpio(reset_scl_pin | GPIO_SION_ENABLE), and imxrt_config_gpio muxes the pad itself (imxrt_gpio_configinput writes PADMUX_MUXMODE_ALT5 plus SION into the pad mux register; the RT118x RGPIO variant calls imxrt_iomux_configure(pinset) first), so the pads are switched to GPIO before they are toggled and read back. The remaining part of the hunk (re-initialising the port even when recovery fails) is already present on imxrt, where the out: label now sits before imxrt_lpi2c_init (later commit 70e453c2c 'Improve imxrt_lpi2c_reset').

fix.subject: arch/{nrf52|nrf53}/usbd: various fixes to improve USB stability
fix.message:
arch/{nrf52|nrf53}/usbd: various fixes to improve USB stability

USBD has many limitation that make it hard to work properly:
- only one EasyDMA channel which must be shared for all EPs
- only one DMA transfer can take place at a time
- some registers are unavailable during DMA transfer
- in case of any problems, the peripheral silently blocks,
  or lose the transmitted bytes without information for the user

This commit is trying to fix these problem and makes the USBS stack more reliable.

Tested with high-speed CDCACM data transfers and that's the best I've been able to get in terms of stability.

claude.evidence: The commit (identical hunks in nrf52_usbd.c and nrf53_usbd.c) works around the nRF USBD's EasyDMA, which its message describes as 'only one EasyDMA channel which must be shared for all EPs' and 'only one DMA transfer can take place at a time'; three of the four listed hunks are that arbitration (the NRF52_TRACEERR_DMABUSY trace code, the NRF52_USBD_DMAIRQ mask built from the nRF ENDEPIN/ENDEPOUT/ENDISOIN/ENDISOOUT events, and the dmaepinwait/dmaepoutwait waiting bitsets). fix.message:
arch/risc-v: fix uninitialized HW cmds and bus clock

Initialize i2c_ll_hw_cmd_t in sendstart/startrecv so ack_exp/done are
not left with stack garbage that can NACK or skip the address byte.
Program i2c_hal_set_bus_timing() with the requested bus_freq instead of
the board default so msg frequency is applied.

Affects only Espressif devices.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Signed-off-by: Filipe Cavalcanti <filipe.cavalcanti@espressif.com>

lines: *   priv - Pointer to the internal driver state structure.
*   priv - Pointer to the internal driver state structure.
/* Configure the I2C to trigger a transaction */
*   priv          - Pointer to the internal driver state structure.

claude.label: already_ok
claude.evidence: The fix in esp_i2c.c zero-initialises the i2c_ll_hw_cmd_t bit-field structs in esp_i2c_sendstart/esp_i2c_startrecv (commit message: 'so ack_exp/done are not left with stack garbage that can NACK or skip the address byte') and makes esp_i2c_init_clock pass the requested bus_freq to i2c_hal_set_bus_timing() instead of priv->config->clk_freq ('instead of the board default so msg frequency is applied'). The legacy esp32c3_i2c.c never had either problem because it does not use the HAL command structs: esp32c3_i2c_sendstart and esp32c3_i2c_startrecv write whole command words built by the I2C_BASE_CMD / I2C_SEND_CMD / I2C_RECV_CMD macros, which compute every bit from explicit operands (opcode, ack check or ack value, byte count), so no field can carry stale stack data. Its esp32c3_i2c_init_clock derives all bus timing (clock divider, half cycle, SCL periods) from its bus_freq argument and stores priv->clk_freq = bus_freq, and esp32c3_i2c_transfer calls it with msgs[i].frequency for every message, so the per-message frequency is already applied.

stm32: support querying a previously set RTC alarm In the STM32F1xx series

Impact:
When using the stm32f1xx series MCU, the alarm function can be used, but when we enabled the CONFIG_RTC_ALARM configuration, an error was reported due to the inability to find the specific implementation of rdalarm.

Testing:
In our own projects, we have done alarm verification using the STM32F103RE..

/* Disable pre-emption while we do this so that we don't have to worry
* about being suspended and working on an old time.

claude.label: already_ok
claude.evidence: The listed hunk is an STM32F1 build fix in the lower half shared by several STM32 families: stm32_rdalarm compared the alarm ID with RTC_ALARMA/RTC_ALARMB, which only the F4 and L15 alarm headers provide, while the F1 header stm32_alarm.h had no such IDs and no rdalarm backend (the same commit adds struct alm_rdalarm_s and stm32_rtc_rdalarm there); the commit message says enabling CONFIG_RTC_ALARM on STM32F1 gave 'an error ... due to the inability to find the specific implementation of rdalarm', and the hunk keeps the ALARMA/ALARMB check only for F4/L15 and accepts IDs below CONFIG_RTC_NALARMS otherwise. The esp32c3-legacy counterpart rtc_lh_rdalarm never used family-specific alarm names: it checks the ID against RTC_ALARM0 and RTC_ALARM_LAST from its own enum alm_id_e, which esp32c3_rtc.h defines under the same CONFIG_RTC_ALARM guard as the function, and it reads the alarm through up_rtc_rdalarm, which esp32c3_rtc.h declares and esp32c3_rtc.c implements. So with CONFIG_RTC_ALARM enabled every symbol it uses exists and the accepted IDs match what its backend supports; the way it is written never had this problem. One unrelated difference is that it checks the ID range only with DEBUGASSERT rather than a runtime if, but this commit did not change that aspect (the pre-fix STM32 code already had a runtime check).

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The commit message says 'dma_get_status returned stale pending_length after config/reload because write-back descriptor was not synced with base descriptor. Sync write-back in dma_mchp_config and dmac_desc_reload_block.' In dma_mchp_dmac_g2.c, dma_mchp_config (lines 437-469) builds the channel descriptor with dma_mchp_desc_setup(dev_data, config, base_desc) at line 455 and never copies SRCADDR/DSTADDR/BTCNT into descriptors_wb[channel], exactly like g1 before the fix, while dma_mchp_get_status returns data->descriptors_wb[channel].DMAC_BTCNT whenever the channel is not the active one (line 686), the same logic g1 had. G2 uses the same write-back area (DMAC_WRBADDR at line 135) and already syncs it in dmac_desc_reload_block ('Sync WB registers', line 247), so every field and struct the fix needs exists on this side; only the config path lacks it, and the fixed g1 driver still does this sync in its config at the pinned commit (g1 lines 515-518). Of the three picked hunks, the void* to typed-pointer change is cosmetic and the block_count > 1 check of the first hunk already exists in g2 (line 344); the write-back sync of the third hunk (with the declarations from the second) is the part that is missing.
claude.title: The Microchip DMAC G2 driver does not copy the new descriptor into the write-back descriptor in dma_mchp_config, so dma_get_status can report a stale pending length after configuration.
claude.summary: On 2026-05-11 the G1 driver (dma_mchp_dmac_g1.c) was fixed to copy the source address, destination address and beat count of the freshly built descriptor into the write-back descriptor in dma_mchp_config and in reload, because dma_get_status reads the remaining length from the write-back descriptor whenever the channel is not the active one. The G2 driver already does this copy in dmac_desc_reload_block, but its dma_mchp_config still stops after dma_mchp_desc_setup without touching descriptors_wb[channel]. As a result, a dma_get_status call on G2 after dma_config, while the channel is not the active one, returns the beat count left in the write-back area by an earlier transfer (zero at boot) instead of the newly configured length, which is the 'stale pending_length' the commit message describes and can mislead callers that compute transferred bytes from pending_length. The fix is to add the same three assignments (plus the typed desc/desc_wb pointers) after dma_mchp_desc_setup in G2's dma_mchp_config; the multi-block check from the same hunk set is already present in G2, so only part of the picked change is needed.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: lsm6dso16is: fix gyroscope full-scale encoding
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: lsm6dso16is: fix gyroscope full-scale encoding

The gyroscope full-scale tables were copied from the lsm6dso driver and
used that part's FS_G encoding, so a gyro-range of 2000 dps yielded a
zero gain (readings always 0 rad/s), 125 dps read past the end of the
tables, and the other ranges applied a wrong sensitivity. Lay the tables
out per the LSM6DSO16IS encoding and index them through a helper that
maps the FS_125 register value.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Cabé <benjamin@zephyrproject.org>
Assisted-by: Claude:fable-5

claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The fix re-lays out the LSM6DSO16IS gyro tables and returns a special code for 125 dps because, in the commit message's words, that driver's tables 'used that part's FS_G encoding' (the LSM6DSO one) instead of the LSM6DSO16IS one, in which 125 dps is code 0x10 (LSM6DSO16IS_DT_FS_125DPS in include/zephyr/dt-bindings/sensor/lsm6dso16is.h line 45). The ISM330DHCX driver has its own tables, and the comment at lines 69-82 says they are 'initialized in order to mimic the ism330dhcx_fs_g_t enum', with ISM330DHCX_125dps = 2, 250dps = 0, 500dps = 4, 1000dps = 8, 2000dps = 12 and 4000dps = 1. The map {250, 4000, 125, 0, 500, 0, 0, 0, 1000, 0, 0, 0, 2000} and the sensitivities {2, 32, 1, 0, 4, ..., 8, ..., 16} follow that enum, so the index returned by the loop at line 98 is the value passed to ism330dhcx_gy_full_scale_set (line 137) and the gain at line 241 uses the matching sensitivity; 125 dps is index 2, inside the table. The problem comes from the LSM6DSO16IS register encoding and does not exist in this device's encoding.

fix.subject: drivers: phy_ksz8081: Fix boot and link up
fix.message:
drivers: phy_ksz8081: Fix boot and link up

Two issues are being simultaneously address in this commit:

Issue 1:

Current issue is that zephyr boot / init is slow because it is blocked
by the phy ksz8081 init doing autonegotiation which can take on the
order of a few seconds.

Fix by now doing autonegotiation in the monitor handler instead of in
the cfg link call. The cfg link call will now only set the ANAR register
and a software flag to let the monitor handler know whether or not to
redo the autonegotiation sequence.

Issue 2:

The ksz8081 phy currently does not link up ever on cold boots on the NXP
RT platforms due to regression on mainline. My understanding of why is
not clear, but I found that re-setting the RMII override bit by the time
the monitor work handler runs with the change to fix the first issue,
makes the link come up.

Signed-off-by: Declan Snyder <declan.snyder@nxp.com>

fix.subject: lora: sx126x: apply silicon errata workarounds
fix.message:
lora: sx126x: apply silicon errata workarounds

Apply three documented SX1261/62 silicon errata from DS_SX1261-2_V1.2:

- IQ Polarity (chapter 15.4): after every SetPacketParams command,
  manually fix bit 2 of REG_IQ_POLARITY to match the requested IQ
  inversion setting. Without this, inverted-IQ packets (used by
  LoRaWAN downlinks) may be silently corrupted.

- TX Modulation Quality at 500 kHz (chapter 15.1): clear bit 2 of
  REG_TX_MODULATION when using 500 kHz bandwidth, set it otherwise.
  Without this, 500 kHz transmissions have degraded modulation quality.

- Register Retention: add REG_RX_GAIN and REG_TX_MODULATION to the
  chip's internal retention list so their values survive warm-start
  sleep cycles, matching the upstream Semtech reference driver.

Signed-off-by: Carlo Caione <ccaione@baylibre.com>

fix.subject: drivers: flash: stm32: xspi: fix XSPI page layout fallback
fix.message:
drivers: flash: stm32: xspi: fix XSPI page layout fallback

When no erase type is found, the erase exponent remains zero.
Applying BIT(0) produces an incorrect one-byte erase size and prevents
the fallback to SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE.

Signed-off-by: Julien Racki <julien.racki-ext@st.com>

lines: /* We need layout page size to be compatible with erase size */
LOG_DBG("layout page %u not compatible with erase size %u",
LOG_DBG("erase size will be used as layout page size");
/* Warn but accept layout page sizes that leave inaccessible
/* We need layout page size to be compatible with erase size */
LOG_DBG("layout page %u not compatible with erase size %u",
LOG_DBG("erase size will be used as layout page size");

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The XSPI hunk replaces `erase_size = BIT(value)` plus the `if (erase_size == 0)` fallback with `(value != 0U) ? BIT(value) : SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE`; the commit message says "When no erase type is found, the erase exponent remains zero. Applying BIT(0) produces an incorrect one-byte erase size and prevents the fallback to SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE." setup_pages_layout in flash_stm32_ospi.c (line 1785) is the same pre-fix code: value starts at 0, is only taken from erase types whose cmd is non-zero, and BIT(value) is then compared with 0, which can never be true because BIT(n) is (1UL << (n)) in include/zephyr/sys/util_macro.h. The OSPI driver can end up with no usable erase type: it memsets erase_types before decoding the BFP and sets cmd to 0 for every type the 4-byte address instruction table marks 0xff (line 2558); then erase_size is 1, the compatibility check at line 1811 never fires, and the layout keeps data->page_size (default SPI_NOR_PAGE_SIZE, 0x100) as its page size. flash_stm32_ospi_erase meanwhile rejects any size that is not a multiple of SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE (line 1195) and falls back to a 4 KiB sector erase, so the reported page cannot be erased on its own. The fix only uses SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE, which the same OSPI function already uses, and nothing else in the OSPI driver handles the zero-exponent case.

refs.quote: .page_size = SPI_NOR_PAGE_SIZE, /* by default, to be updated by sfdp */

claude.title: The STM32 OSPI flash driver never falls back to the 4 KiB sector size in its page layout when the flash reports no erase type, because BIT(0) is 1, not 0.
claude.summary: On 2026-09-16 (commit 0b92a79e) the STM32 XSPI flash driver fixed setup_pages_layout so that, when no erase type is found, the layout uses SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE instead of a one-byte erase size. The STM32 OSPI driver has the same function with the old code: it computes BIT(value) and only falls back when the result is 0, which never happens. When the flash's SFDP tables leave no erase type, the OSPI page layout reports the 256-byte program page as the erase page, while the driver's erase function refuses any size that is not a multiple of 4 KiB. Code that erases one layout page at a time through the flash page layout would then get an error. The change is a one-line copy with the same names.

physical address will be disabled. Valid entry will be somewhere

/* Check bounds of physical address space. */
/* Initial TLB mappings could point to non existing physical pages. */
* Flush the cache to make sure the backing physical page

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The picked hunk changes the Meteor Lake driver's sys_mm_drv_unmap_page to rewrite the entry as the default 1:1 entry (`pa_to_tlb_entry(va) | TLB_EXEC_BIT | TLB_WRITE_BIT`) with the enable bit cleared, instead of only clearing the enable bit; the commit message ties it to the context save: "Since in adsp_mm_save_context() routine we go through physical memory range, we need to include these pages in context save loop." That save routine exists only in mm_drv_intel_adsp_mtl_tlb.c (adsp_mm_save_context at line 883, which walks every used physical page and checks the TLB entry at its 1:1 index); mm_drv_intel_adsp_tlb.c has no save or restore routine, no physical page allocator, and nothing that reads the address bits of a disabled entry: sys_mm_drv_page_phys_get returns -EFAULT when the enable bit is clear (line 232) and sys_mm_drv_map_page overwrites the whole entry (line 130). The fix also needs TLB_EXEC_BIT and TLB_WRITE_BIT, which mm_drv_intel_adsp.h builds from the exec-bit-idx and write-bit-idx properties; the generic driver does not include that header, states "There are no caching mode, or R/W, or eXecution (etc.) bits.", and its only users, the cAVS 2.5 TLB nodes (compatible "intel,adsp-tlb"), set paddr-size but no exec-bit-idx or write-bit-idx. So the stale address left in a disabled entry is harmless there, and the change depends on a feature and entry bits the cAVS driver does not have.

refs.quote: There are no caching mode, or R/W, or eXecution (etc.) bits.

fix.subject: Bluetooth: HCI: spi_st: Fix a stale start event ending the reset wait
fix.message:
Bluetooth: HCI: spi_st: Fix a stale start event ending the reset wait

The driver waits for the vendor event with which the controller reports
its start: in open() when the node has reset-event, and with SPI
protocol v1 after an HCI Reset. An event that no wait had taken, such
as one that came after a wait had timed out, stayed in its semaphore
and ended the next wait at once, before the controller had reported
its new start.

Clear the semaphore ahead of both waits: before the reset line is
released, and once the HCI Reset has gone out, while the bus is still
held so that the event that follows cannot have been read yet. The
wait after an HCI Reset now requires reset-event too, as the one in
open() does, so that no wait goes without the clear.

Not tested on hardware.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5
Signed-off-by: Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@silabs.com>

The behavioural part of commit 0f40a81b, the one the message describes as "Clear the semaphore ahead of both waits", is in other hunks that were not picked: k_sem_reset(&sem_initialised) in bt_spi_send_raw after an HCI Reset and in bt_spi_open before the reset line is released (hci_spi_st.c lines 629-630 and 749). fix.subject: drivers: spi: silabs: Disable EUSART transceiver when idle
fix.message:
drivers: spi: silabs: Disable EUSART transceiver when idle

Disable the EUSART transmitter and receiver immediately upon
completion of a transfer, rather than deferring it to PM Device
Runtime suspend.

The transmitter and receiver are always re-enabled as part of
configuring a new transfer.

This fixes an issue when CONFIG_PM=y where the driver would
not block deep sleep when it was idle, but would wake up with
an inconsistent internal shift register state. Safely shut down
the transmitter and receiver whenever they are not used to
avoid this scenario.

Signed-off-by: Aksel Skauge Mellbye <aksel.mellbye@silabs.com>

claude.label: unsure
claude.evidence: The EUSART fix turns the transmitter and receiver off at the end of every transfer instead of in the PM suspend action, because with CONFIG_PM=y the driver "would not block deep sleep when it was idle, but would wake up with an inconsistent internal shift register state"; it relies on the EUSART driver re-enabling them in spi_silabs_eusart_configure before each transfer (eusart lines 243-245). spi_silabs_usart.c has no PM handling at all (no PM action is passed to SPI_DEVICE_DT_INST_DEFINE, no pm_policy_state_lock calls); it enables the USART once in spi_silabs_usart_init (line 371), never disables it, and spi_config does not re-enable it. So the matched lines 285-286 are generic spi_context calls, and the EUSART's pre-fix sequence (PM lock released while TX/RX stay on until a PM suspend) has no counterpart here. This driver serves the silabs,usart-spi nodes of Series 2 parts such as xG22 and xG27, so the USART can also stay enabled across deep sleep, which is the situation the EUSART fix avoids. Whether the USART, unlike the EUSART, wakes from deep sleep with a bad shift register state is a hardware property the repository does not document, so it cannot be decided from the code whether this driver has the same problem; if it does, the port would have to be adapted (enable TX/RX when a transfer starts and disable them when it ends).

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: fix thread function signatures
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: fix thread function signatures

Fix thread function signatures to avoid stack corruption on thread exit.

Signed-off-by: Benedikt Schmidt <benedikt.schmidt@embedded-solutions.at>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: Commit 191865b5 ("Fix thread function signatures to avoid stack corruption on thread exit") changed adxl362_thread and adxl372_thread from taking a struct pointer to the k_thread_entry_t form (void *p1, void *p2, void *p3), and dropped the (k_thread_entry_t) cast at k_thread_create; both source drivers still have that form. adxl367_trigger.c, a sibling of the same ADI trigger code, still has the pre-fix pattern in both places: `static void adxl367_thread(struct adxl367_data *drv_data)` at line 70 and `(k_thread_entry_t)adxl367_thread, drv_data,` at line 178, where k_thread_entry_t is `void (*)(void *p1, void *p2, void *p3)` (include/zephyr/arch/arch_interface.h:46), so the thread is started through a function pointer of a different type. Nothing in the ADXL367 driver handles this another way, and the fix only needs ARG_UNUSED and a local pointer, which are available. The runtime effect is small: the code is only built with the non-default ADXL367_TRIGGER_OWN_THREAD option, and the thread body is `while (true)` and never returns, so the "thread exit" case named in the commit cannot occur here; what remains is a call through a mismatched function type, which C leaves undefined.
claude.title: The ADXL367 trigger thread still has the wrong thread entry signature and is cast to k_thread_entry_t, the pattern the 2023 sensor-wide fix removed from ADXL362 and ADXL372.
claude.summary: On 2023-10-30 (commit 191865b5) Zephyr changed the trigger threads of 50 sensor driver files, including ADXL362 and ADXL372, to take (void *p1, void *p2, void *p3) instead of a driver data pointer, and removed the cast to k_thread_entry_t when creating the thread. The ADXL367 driver, written from the same ADI trigger code, still declares adxl367_thread with a struct pointer parameter and casts it at k_thread_create. Starting a thread through a function pointer of another type is undefined in C, but this thread never returns, so the stack corruption on thread exit that the commit describes cannot happen here and behaviour most likely stays the same. The fix can be copied as is with the names changed.
claude.impact_note: The thread loops forever and never returns, so the stack corruption on thread exit that the commit names cannot happen here; only the formally undefined call through a mismatched function type remains, and only with the non-default own-thread trigger mode.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_mcux_lpuart: ensure TX completes before reconfig
fix.message:
drivers: serial: uart_mcux_lpuart: ensure TX completes before reconfig

Add a wait for the Transmission Complete (TC) flag at the start of
mcux_lpuart_configure(). This prevents reconfiguration while the
hardware is still shifting out the final byte on the TX line.

Without this wait, uart_configure() could interrupt an ongoing
transmission, causing the last byte to not be fully sent on the UART
bus. This behavior was observed on NXP LPUART and tracked in issue
#109807.

Fixes #109807

Signed-off-by: Michal Chromec <michal.chromec@nxp.com>

lines: static int mcux_lpuart_config_get(const struct device *dev, struct uart_config *cfg)

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: Per the commit message, the fix adds "a wait for the Transmission Complete (TC) flag at the start of mcux_lpuart_configure()" because "uart_configure() could interrupt an ongoing transmission, causing the last byte to not be fully sent on the UART bus"; the LPUART driver still has it at the pinned commit, now bounded with WAIT_FOR on LPUART_STAT_TC_MASK. In uart_mcux.c, uart_mcux_configure is the runtime .configure callback and, like the pre-fix LPUART function, goes straight to re-initialization (UART_Init with the new baud rate and TX/RX enabled) without checking kUART_TransmissionCompleteFlag. The status bit the fix needs exists here: uart_mcux_irq_tx_complete already reads kUART_TransmissionCompleteFlag, while poll_out and fifo_fill only wait for kUART_TxDataRegEmptyFlag, so a byte can still be shifting out when configure is called; the sibling NXP driver uart_mcux_flexcomm.c guards the same step ("Wait for USART to finish transmission and turn off"). Confidence is medium because the body of UART_Init is in the NXP SDK, not in this repository, so it cannot be confirmed here whether it disables the transmitter or reprograms the baud rate mid-frame, and the commit reports the behaviour only "on NXP LPUART". The same function is also called from uart_mcux_init at boot, so the wait has to be added on the runtime path only.

refs.quote: /* Wait for USART to finish transmission and turn off */

claude.title: The Kinetis UART driver reconfigures the UART at run time without waiting for the last byte to finish sending.
claude.summary: In June 2026 the NXP LPUART driver (uart_mcux_lpuart.c) started waiting for the Transmission Complete flag before uart_configure() reconfigures the port, and later bounded that wait to 300 ms with -EBUSY, so that a byte still being sent is not cut off. The Kinetis UART driver uart_mcux.c still calls UART_Init with the new settings immediately in uart_mcux_configure, with no check of kUART_TransmissionCompleteFlag, even though the driver already reads that flag elsewhere. If an application changes baud rate or framing right after writing data, the last byte will likely go out truncated or garbled. What is missing to be certain: the body of UART_Init is in the NXP SDK, outside this repository, and the original report covered LPUART only; when porting, the wait belongs only on the runtime path because the same function also runs at boot from uart_mcux_init.

drivers: sam_can: fixed MCAN Register Base Address

Before that fix, the default mrba was used; added
DMA Base Address to DTSI. Fixes #68472

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The fix programs the upper 16 bits of the message RAM address into a separate DMA base register taken from a new devicetree reg block named dma_base (commit message: "Before that fix, the default mrba was used; added DMA Base Address to DTSI"), and the fixed driver can_sam.c now fills .dma_base only when DT_INST_REG_HAS_NAME(inst, dma_base) is true. The repository's atmel,sam-can binding describes that block as "Register block for the DMA Base Address (for samx7x SOCs)", and samx7x.dtsi is where reg-names "m_can", "dma_base" is set. The SAM0 CAN nodes in samc21.dtsi and same5x.dtsi have a single reg block, and the atmel,sam0-can binding defines no reg-names, so the other side has no such register to program. can_sam0.c handles message RAM addressing in its own way for its hardware: it passes mrba 0 to can_mcan_configure_mram and, on parts with more than 64 KB SRAM, places the buffers in a dedicated section so they lie in the first 64 KB of SRAM as its comment says the SAM D5x/E5x data sheet requires. The missing .dma_base line in can_sam0.c is therefore a hardware difference, not a missed fix.

fix.subject: usb: it82xx2: fix issue with the unexpected setting of the ready bit
fix.message:
usb: it82xx2: fix issue with the unexpected setting of the ready bit

In the IT82xx2 chip, the ready bit is automatically cleared by
hardware. When setting other bits, there is a chance that the ready bit
hasn't been cleared yet, leading to unexpected USB transactions. This
change ensures that the ready bit is always set to '0' when setting the
endpoint control value.

Signed-off-by: Ren Chen <Ren.Chen@ite.com.tw>

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The behavioural part of this commit (per its message, it "ensures that the ready bit is always set to '0' when setting the endpoint control value") is the read-modify-write in it82xx2_usb_ep_ctrl that masks ENDPOINT_READY_BIT; the hunk picked out only replaces ENDPOINT_EN with ENDPOINT_ENABLE_BIT in the bus-reset path. In the commit the removed macro was "#define ENDPOINT_EN BIT(0)" and the new one is "#define ENDPOINT_ENABLE_BIT BIT(0)", so the value written to the EP0 control register is the same before and after and the hunk is a rename. In udc_it82xx2.c ENDPOINT_EN is also BIT(0), equal to its own ENDPOINT_ENABLE_BIT, so line 752 already writes the post-fix value with the ready bit clear. The real fix is present there as well: it82xx2_usb_ep_ctrl builds the new value from ep_ctrl.value & ~ENDPOINT_READY_BIT.

fix.subject: drivers: entropy: stm32: Fix S2RAM sequence and ensure ISR pool filling
fix.message:
drivers: entropy: stm32: Fix S2RAM sequence and ensure ISR pool filling

Split the initialization function in 2 and call only hardware
initialization on S2RAM resume to fix an issue where S2RAM resume
previously called entropy_stm32_rng_init() and corrupted some software
resource like the system workqueue by calling k_work_init() on an
existing and possibly submitted work.

Prevent entry in PM suspend state unless the ISR random sample pools
are filled so that any interrupt requesting random bytes at wakeup have
a chance to get random bytes. As a side effect, this change makes
entropy_stm32_rng_pm_action() much simpler.

Rename device driver initialization function for consistency.
Signed-off-by: Etienne Carriere <etienne.carriere@st.com>

lines: * Avoid starting pool filling from ISR as it might require
* blocking if RNG is not available and a race condition could
* also occur if this ISR has interrupted the RNG ISR.
* If the TRNG has no IRQ line, always schedule the work item,
* as this is what fills the RNG pools instead of the ISR.
* to signal that all allocated regions are now read and could be
static int rng_pool_put(struct rng_pool *rngp, uint8_t byte)

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The picked hunk makes the STM32 rng_pool_get() call pool_refill_requested(), which takes the PM state lock as soon as a pool drops to its threshold; before the fix the lock was taken only in start_pool_filling(), which in ISR context is deferred to a work item (the k_is_in_isr() branch), leaving a window in which the SoC could suspend before the ISR pool was refilled (commit message: "Prevent entry in PM suspend state unless the ISR random sample pools are filled"). In entropy_smartbond.c the same threshold check in rng_pool_get() calls trng_enable(true) directly, also from ISR context, and trng_enable(true) immediately calls entropy_smartbond_pm_policy_state_lock_get(), which locks PM_STATE_STANDBY. That lock is released only by trng_enable(false) in smartbond_trng_isr() once new bytes no longer fit in either pool, so there is no deferred step and no window for the hunk to close; the difference is purely in how the code is written (enable synchronously instead of through a work item). Separately, trng_enable(true) has no guard like the STM32 pm_locked flag, so repeated threshold hits before the pools refill would take the reference-counted lock more than once against a single put; that is a different question, not addressed by this hunk and not judged here.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_infineon_pdl: fix async UART correctness issues
fix.message:
drivers: serial: uart_infineon_pdl: fix async UART correctness issues

Guard against NULL DMA pointer panics in TX abort and completion
callbacks, report actual transferred length when aborting TX, and
only arm TX timeout when flow control is active per the Zephyr UART
specification.

Signed-off-by: Vignesh Pandian <vignesh@aerlync.com>

lines: /* Not stopped; keep the ref, the DMA completion path releases it. */
LOG_WRN("Error getting Tx DMA status (%d), assuming 0 bytes sent", err);
/* DMA is stopped, so end the session; the event above already read buf. */

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk changes the PDL driver's ifx_cat1_uart_async_tx_abort() so that UART_TX_ABORTED carries buf_len - stat.pending_length instead of a fixed 0, and so that a dma_get_status() failure still delivers the event (with length 0) instead of jumping to unlock; the commit message calls this "report actual transferred length when aborting TX". uart_infineon.c (the legacy-HAL driver for the same infineon,uart compatible) has the same function with the pre-fix code: when dma_get_status() fails it logs "Error stopping Tx DMA" and does goto unlock, skipping the event, and otherwise it always sets evt.data.tx.len = 0; the TX timeout work calls this same function. Zephyr's UART API states that after uart_tx_abort "#UART_TX_ABORTED event will be generated with amount of data sent" and documents uart_event_tx.len as the "Number of bytes sent". Everything the fix needs exists on this side: dma_tx.buf_len is set in ifx_cat1_uart_async_tx(), the file already computes buf_len - stat.pending_length for RX from dma_get_status(), and the paired legacy DMA driver (dma_infineon.c) fills pending_length; nothing else in uart_infineon.c reports a transmitted count for an abort (dma_transmitted_bytes is only reset). The commit's other changes (NULL guards, arming the timeout only with flow control) are outside the picked hunk and are not judged here.

refs.quote: #UART_TX_ABORTED event will be generated with amount of data sent.

claude.title: The legacy Infineon UART driver's TX abort always reports 0 bytes sent, and sends no abort event at all if reading the DMA status fails.
claude.summary: On 2026-11-05 the Infineon PDL UART driver (uart_infineon_pdl.c) changed its async TX abort to report how many bytes were actually sent (buffer length minus the DMA's pending length) and to still deliver UART_TX_ABORTED when reading the DMA status fails. The legacy-HAL driver uart_infineon.c, built when USE_INFINEON_LEGACY_HAL is set, has the same abort function with the old code: it always reports a length of 0, and on a status-read error it returns without sending the event. An application that aborts a transfer, or whose transfer hits the TX timeout, is therefore told that nothing was sent even when part of the buffer already went out, which can lead to resending or losing track of data. The status-read error is probably rare, because the paired DMA driver's get_status fails only for an invalid channel, so the wrong length is the main practical effect.

lines: const struct spi_atcspi200_cfg * const cfg = dev->config;

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The picked hunks replace the per-call dfs = SPI_WORD_SIZE_GET(...) >> 3 in transceive() and in the RX branch of the ISR with data->dfs, which the same commit computes in configure() as the word size rounded up to whole bytes (3 mapped to 4), and add an early exit when both ctx->tx_buf and ctx->rx_buf are NULL; the commit message says "Fix incorrect behavior for non-8-bit SPI word sizes" and "Fix the handling when both TX and RX buffers are NULL". Before the fix the ATCSPI200 configure() accepted any word size, so >> 3 truncated sizes that are not multiples of 8. In spi_egis_et171.c configure() returns -ENOTSUP for every word size other than 8 and 16, so the >> 3 at lines 666 and 1182 always yields 1 or 2, exactly what the rounded data->dfs would give, and the two picked hunks would not change its behaviour. fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl372: re-arm stream after an orphaned interrupt
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: adxl372: re-arm stream after an orphaned interrupt

Once a stream is cancelled the FIFO keeps filling and INT1 fires with
no stream pending. The interrupt handler and the status callback then
return without clearing fifo_full_irq, so the next
adxl372_submit_stream() skips the FIFO flush and reconfiguration,
INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge.

Clear fifo_full_irq on those early returns, as the ADXL345 driver does
since commit c627cf26d123 ("drivers: sensor: adxl345: RTIO stream
fix").

Tested on an apard32690 with the eval_adxl372_ardz shield: the
restart_after_idle and restart_cycles tests of the RTIO stream suite
in #123186 fail without this change and pass with it.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5.5
Signed-off-by: Dimitrije Lilic <dimitrije.lilic@orioninc.com>

lines: static void adxl345_process_status1_cb(struct rtio *r, const struct rtio_sqe *sqe,
const struct adxl345_dev_config *cfg = (const struct adxl345_dev_config *) dev->config;
const struct adxl345_dev_config *cfg = (const struct adxl345_dev_config *) dev->config;
LOG_ERR("Failed to get sensor clock cycles");

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The picked hunk adds data->fifo_full_irq = 0 to the early returns taken when an ADXL372 interrupt arrives with no stream pending (data->sqe == NULL), so that the next adxl372_submit_stream() sees a changed flag and flushes and reconfigures the FIFO instead of waiting for an edge that never comes. adxl345_stream.c already does this under its own flag name: both adxl345_process_status1_cb() and adxl345_stream_irq_handler() set data->fifo_watermark_irq = 0 before returning when data->sqe == NULL, and adxl345_submit_stream() uses that same flag to decide whether to flush and reconfigure (if (fifo_watermark_irq != data->fifo_watermark_irq)). The commit message itself says it copies this driver: clear the flag "as the ADXL345 driver does since commit c627cf26d123". The candidate matched only the unchanged surrounding lines; the ADXL345 copy already contains the fix.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl372: re-arm stream after an orphaned interrupt
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: adxl372: re-arm stream after an orphaned interrupt

Once a stream is cancelled the FIFO keeps filling and INT1 fires with
no stream pending. The interrupt handler and the status callback then
return without clearing fifo_full_irq, so the next
adxl372_submit_stream() skips the FIFO flush and reconfiguration,
INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge.

Clear fifo_full_irq on those early returns, as the ADXL345 driver does
since commit c627cf26d123 ("drivers: sensor: adxl345: RTIO stream
fix").

Tested on an apard32690 with the eval_adxl372_ardz shield: the
restart_after_idle and restart_cycles tests of the RTIO stream suite
in #123186 fail without this change and pass with it.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5.5
Signed-off-by: Dimitrije Lilic <dimitrije.lilic@orioninc.com>

lines: static void adxl355_process_status1_cb(struct rtio *r, const struct rtio_sqe *sqe, int result,
LOG_ERR("Failed to get sensor clock cycles");

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: adxl355_stream.c is built the same way as the pre-fix ADXL372 code: adxl355_submit_stream() reprograms INT_MAP and flushes the FIFO (adxl355_flush_fifo(), then a STATUS read) only when fifo_watermark_irq differs from data->fifo_watermark_irq, and then arms the GPIO with GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE. adxl355_gpio_callback() disables the GPIO interrupt and calls adxl355_stream_irq_handler(), and both that handler (line 377) and adxl355_process_status1_cb() (line 259) simply return when data->sqe == NULL without resetting data->fifo_watermark_irq; no other code in the driver resets that flag. So after a stream is cancelled or between requests, an interrupt with no pending request leaves the FIFO untouched, and the next submit with the same trigger skips the flush and only re-arms an edge interrupt, which is the failure the commit message describes as "INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge". The fix needs only the existing fifo_watermark_irq field (adxl355.h), so it carries over as one assignment in each early return. Confidence is medium because whether the ADXL355 interrupt line stays asserted until the FIFO is flushed is a hardware property the repository does not state, although the driver itself re-enables the interrupt only after a flush in adxl355_flush_rtio().
claude.title: ADXL355 streaming can stall after an interrupt arrives while no stream request is pending, because the re-arm flag is never cleared.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-29 the ADXL372 driver was fixed to clear its FIFO-interrupt flag when an interrupt arrives with no stream request pending, so that the next stream request flushes and reconfigures the FIFO; the ADXL345 driver already did the same. The ADXL355 stream code follows the same template but still returns from adxl355_stream_irq_handler() and adxl355_process_status1_cb() without clearing data->fifo_watermark_irq. If the FIFO fills after a stream is cancelled or between requests, the next stream with the same trigger skips the flush and only waits for a new edge on the interrupt pin, so the new stream may never receive data. The fix is one assignment in each of the two early returns. Whether the ADXL355 interrupt line really stays asserted in this state is not stated in the repository and would need a hardware check.
claude.same_problem_note: Same unfixed code in adxl355_stream.c as zephyr-102: both fixes make a driver clear fifo_watermark_irq when an interrupt arrives with no pending stream request (ADXL345 on 2026-08-03, ADXL372 on 2026-10-29).

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: max30009_stream.c follows the same pattern as the pre-fix ADXL372 code: max30009_submit_stream() updates A_FULL_EN, flushes the FIFO (max30009_flush_dev()) and reads STATUS1 only when fifo_watermark_irq differs from data->fifo_watermark_irq, and then arms the GPIO with GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE. max30009_gpio_callback() disables the GPIO interrupt and calls max30009_stream_irq_handler(), and both that handler (line 418) and max30009_process_status1_cb() (line 280) return when data->sqe == NULL without resetting data->fifo_watermark_irq; nothing else in the driver resets that flag. claude.title: MAX30009 streaming can stall after an interrupt arrives while no stream request is pending, because the re-arm flag is never cleared.
claude.summary: On 2026-10-29 the ADXL372 driver was fixed to clear its FIFO-interrupt flag when an interrupt arrives with no stream request pending, so that the next stream request flushes the FIFO and re-reads the status; the ADXL345 driver already did the same. If the FIFO reaches its threshold after a stream is cancelled or between requests, the next stream with the same trigger skips the flush and the STATUS1 read and only waits for a new edge on the interrupt pin, so the new stream may never receive data. claude.evidence: The commit message says the fix is about timing, "so that device won't be recognized by host until user application invokes udc_enable()": in the UDC driver numaker_usbd_hw_setup() runs from udc_numaker_init() (udc_numaker.c line 2990) while the connect runs later from udc_numaker_enable() (line 2935), so the D+ pull-up set in hw_setup was on before the application asked to connect; the fix moves DPPUEN from hw_setup into sw_connect. In the legacy usb_dc_numaker.c the same ATTR write with USBD_ATTR_DPPUEN_Msk is in numaker_usbd_hw_setup() (line 393), but that function is only called from usb_dc_attach() (line 1244), which calls numaker_usbd_sw_connect() itself a few lines later (line 1257). usb_dc_attach() is in turn only called by the legacy stack's usb_enable() (subsys/usb/device/usb_device.c line 1638), and the driver's boot-time init numaker_udbd_init() (line 1923) does not touch the hardware. So the legacy driver model has no separate init and enable steps and no window where the pull-up is on before the application enables USB; the timing problem fixed in the UDC driver does not arise here.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: lsm6dsvxxx: fix double completion of one-shot reads
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: lsm6dsvxxx: fix double completion of one-shot reads

lsm6dsvxxx_submit_one_shot() issued a separate rtio_read_regs_async()
call per requested channel, each appending a completion callback that
completes the same iodev_sqe, so reading e.g. accel + gyro completed
(and freed) the request once per channel, handing the buffer to the
application before all transfers finished and corrupting the sqe pool.
Collect all requested register bursts into a single rtio_regs list and
issue one rtio_read_regs_async() call, so the request is completed
exactly once when the whole transaction is done.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Cabé <benjamin@zephyrproject.org>
Assisted-by: Claude:fable-5

lines: /* Get the buffer for the frame, it may be allocated dynamically by the rtio context */
LOG_ERR("Failed to get a read buffer of size %u bytes", min_buf_len);
static int32_t iis3dwb_set_range_raw(const struct device *dev, uint8_t range)
static int32_t iis3dwb_set_odr_raw(const struct device *dev, uint8_t odr)
static int iis3dwb_odr_set(const struct device *dev, const struct sensor_value *val)
static void iis3dwb_submit_one_shot(const struct device *dev, struct rtio_iodev_sqe *iodev_sqe)
/* Get the buffer for the frame, it may be allocated dynamically by the rtio context */
LOG_ERR("Failed to get a read buffer of size %u bytes", min_buf_len);

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The fix ("fix double completion of one-shot reads") replaces one rtio_read_regs_async() call per requested channel in lsm6dsvxxx_submit_one_shot() with a single call over a collected rtio_regs list; the hunk picked out adds the struct rtio_regs_list regs_list[3] and struct rtio_regs regs declarations for that. iis3dwb_submit_one_shot() already works this way: the channel loop (lines 171-189) only sets has_accel/has_temp, then the requested bursts are collected into struct rtio_regs_list regs_list[2] (lines 196-217) and a single rtio_read_regs_async() is issued at line 233, with a comment saying the callback "will be invoked once, when all the requested registers have been read". It also returns early with -EIO when nothing was requested (lines 191-193), matching the fixed version. The flagged lines (struct iis3dwb_data *data = dev->data; and the edata declaration) are only shared context; the file's history shows its own commit d6728a18ad "fix double completion of the same RTIO sqe".

claude.evidence: The commit message says "STM32L5 have a write block size of 8, but STM32U5 and STM32H5 have a write block size of 16" and converts write_dword()/flash_stm32_write_range() to write a write-block-size chunk at a time; flash_stm32l5x.c serves all three, as the U5 and H5 devicetrees use the st,stm32l5-flash-controller compatible with write-block-size = <16>. flash_stm32g4x.c is built only for the st,stm32g4-flash-controller (drivers/flash/CMakeLists.txt line 164), and the G4 devicetree declares write-block-size = <8> (dts/arm/st/g4/stm32g4.dtsi line 712); no G4 dtsi overrides it. The G4 code is consistently written for that 8-byte unit: write_dword() checks and programs two 32-bit words (lines 108-109 and 132-133) and flash_stm32_write_range() steps by 8 bytes (line 260), and the driver's own flash_stm32_valid_range() only accepts writes aligned to FLASH_STM32_WRITE_BLOCK_SIZE (line 53). fix.subject: drivers/sensor/st: ism330dhcx: fix odr setting
fix.message:
drivers/sensor/st: ism330dhcx: fix odr setting

Loop inside the odr array until we find the first
value which is "<=" (amd not "==") the argument.

Signed-off-by: Armando Visconti <armando.visconti@st.com>

lines: /* for valid index, return value from map */

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The hunk turns ism330dhcx_freq_to_odr_val from an exact match into picking the first table rate at or above the request; the commit message says "Loop inside the odr array until we find the first value which is "<=" (amd not "==") the argument", and the same author's matching iis2iclx commit c6f8d37056 states the intent: "Do not fail when requested rate passed in SENSOR_ATTR_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY is not matching any of the odr values supported by sensor. Instead, round it up to the next one." lsm6dsl_freq_to_odr_val (line 32) is the same lookup with the pre-fix exact test at line 37, and lsm6dsl_accel_odr_set / lsm6dsl_gyro_odr_set pass val->val1 straight to it and return its -EINVAL, so any rate that is not exactly a table value (for example 100 Hz) is rejected; nothing else in the driver rounds the request. The fix cannot be copied verbatim: the lsm6dsl table ends with 1 (index 11, documented as 1.6Hz in Kconfig), so it is not ascending, and the same function maps the saved rate back to an index on PM resume (line 856), so a plain <= would turn 1 Hz into 12.5 Hz. Confidence is low because exact matching in this older driver could be read as a deliberate API choice rather than a defect.
claude.title: The LSM6DSL driver rejects any requested sampling rate that is not exactly one of its table values, instead of rounding up to the next supported rate as the ISM330DHCX driver now does.
claude.summary: In 2024 the ISM330DHCX driver changed its rate lookup from an exact match to the first supported rate at or above the request (commit 50ad2e05), and the same author made the same change in IIS2ICLX. The LSM6DSL driver still uses the exact match in lsm6dsl_freq_to_odr_val, so setting SENSOR_ATTR_SAMPLING_FREQUENCY to a value outside its table returns -EINVAL and the sensor keeps its old rate. The change has to be adapted rather than copied, because the LSM6DSL table puts the 1.6 Hz entry last and the same function restores the saved rate on PM resume, so a request or saved value of 1 must still map to index 11. It is not certain that maintainers regard exact matching as a bug in this driver rather than a deliberate API choice.

fix.subject: drivers: audio: dmic_stm32_mdf: fix the clamp on 24-bit samples
fix.message:
drivers: audio: dmic_stm32_mdf: fix the clamp on 24-bit samples

BIT() has an unsigned type, so -BIT(23) is evaluated using unsigned
arithmetic and wraps to a large positive value instead of producing
-8388608. As a result, the bounds passed to CLAMP() are invalid. Use
explicitly signed constants for the 24-bit PCM limits instead.

Heard on an STM32N6570-DK, whose microphone produced a full-scale square
wave at pcm_width 24 and now records what is said to it.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Benjamin Cabé <benjamin@zephyrproject.org>

lines: /* A 24-bit sample has no limit macros of its own, and BIT() is unsigned */
static void dmic_stm32_mdf_write_sample(uint8_t *dst, uint8_t size, int32_t sample)
struct dmic_stm32_mdf_data *data = CONTAINER_OF(hmdf, struct dmic_stm32_mdf_data, hmdf);
static void dmic_stm32_dfsdm_write_sample(uint8_t *dst, uint8_t sample_size, int32_t sample)

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The MDF fix replaces CLAMP(sample, -BIT(23), BIT(23) - 1) with signed limits because, in the commit's words, "BIT() has an unsigned type, so -BIT(23) is evaluated using unsigned arithmetic and wraps to a large positive value instead of producing -8388608. As a result, the bounds passed to CLAMP() are invalid", which on hardware gave "a full-scale square wave at pcm_width 24". dmic_stm32_dfsdm_write_sample (line 133) is the same helper with the same int32_t sample and the identical pre-fix line 143; BIT is (1UL << (n)) in util_macro.h and CLAMP compares val against low first (util.h line 531), so every non-negative sample is clamped to the wrapped low bound and small negative samples to the high bound. The 24-bit case is reachable: sample_size is DIV_ROUND_UP(pcm_width, 8) (line 168), configure accepts pcm_width up to DFSDM_DATA_RES = 24 (lines 50, 755), and without a DMA channel the driver runs HAL_DFSDM_FilterRegularStart_IT (line 515), whose conversion callback writes each sample through this helper. Nothing in the DFSDM driver defines signed 24-bit limits or otherwise avoids the wrap; only the DMA path, which does not use this helper, is unaffected.

refs.quote: static void dmic_stm32_dfsdm_write_sample(uint8_t *dst, uint8_t sample_size, int32_t sample)

claude.title: The STM32 DFSDM microphone driver clamps 24-bit samples against an unsigned -BIT(23) bound, so in interrupt mode every 24-bit sample comes out as full-scale positive or negative.
claude.summary: In September 2026 the STM32 MDF microphone driver replaced the 24-bit clamp bounds -BIT(23) and BIT(23) - 1 with signed constants, because the unsigned BIT() made the lower bound wrap to a huge positive number and turned recordings into a full-scale square wave. The STM32 DFSDM microphone driver has the same write-sample helper with the identical clamp line and still uses the unsigned bounds. When it is configured for 17 to 24-bit samples without DMA, each non-negative sample is written as -8388608 and each small negative sample as 8388607, so the recorded audio is lost. Defining signed 24-bit limits as the MDF driver did fixes it.

fix.subject: driver: sensor: adxl345: Bug fix for q31_t conv

driver: sensor: adxl345: Bug fix for q31_t conv

This is a bug fix for adxl345_accel_convert_q31 functions.
Functions are used to convert samples received from
sensor to q31_t format when RTIO stream is used.

Signed-off-by: Dimitrije Lilic <dimitrije.lilic@orioninc.com>

lines: /* Read FIFO and call back to rtio with rtio_sqe completion */
/* Read FIFO and call back to rtio with rtio_sqe completion */

claude.evidence: The picked hunk copies two new ADXL345 settings, is_full_res and selected_range, into the FIFO header so that the reworked adxl345_accel_convert_q31 can pick the sign-extension width and scale for the configured g-range and the DATA_FORMAT FULL_RES bit (the commit message: "This is a bug fix for adxl345_accel_convert_q31 functions"). fix.subject: drivers: pwm: Fix NXP TPM without combine channel feature

drivers: pwm: Fix NXP TPM without combine channel feature

Build error occurs for such socs because of accessing unavailable
struct member in hal.
Fix it by adding #if directive to check the feature presence.

Signed-off-by: Michal Smola <michal.smola@nxp.com>

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The hunk is a build fix: the commit message says "TMP variant without combine channel feature is used in some NXP SoCs. Build error occurs for such socs because of accessing unavailable struct member in hal", so pwm_mcux_tpm.c now sets firstEdgeDelayPercent only when FSL_FEATURE_TPM_HAS_COMBINE is set. pwm_rv32m1_tpm.c does still set the member unguarded in rv32m1_tpm_init (line 164), but that driver is only built for the openisa,rv32m1-tpm compatible (DT_DRV_COMPAT at line 10, Kconfig depends on DT_HAS_OPENISA_RV32M1_TPM_ENABLED), which appears in the RV32M1 SoC devicetree, whereas the SoCs the fix is about use the nxp,kinetis-tpm driver. fix.subject: drivers: sensor: paa3905: fix dangling stream SQE on bus error
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: paa3905: fix dangling stream SQE on bus error

The stream completion callback armed the data-ready backup timer before
flushing the bus CQEs, then errored the SQE without clearing
data->stream.iodev_sqe, so the timer later dereferenced an SQE already
returned to the RTIO pool. Arm the timer only after the error check, use
handle_result_on_error() on the failure path, and stop the timer there.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Cabé <benjamin@zephyrproject.org>
Assisted-by: Claude:fable-5

lines: /** Attempt chip recovery if erratic behavior is detected  */
LOG_WRN("CHIP OK register indicates issues. Attempting chip recovery");
LOG_ERR("Failed to allocate RTIO work request");
LOG_ERR("Failed to get a read buffer of size %u bytes", min_buf_len);
* Acquire the chain's five SQEs atomically: the bus RTIO context is
* shared across reads, so a per-SQE acquire that falls back to
* rtio_sqe_drop_all could free an SQE still in flight from another

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The commit message describes the bug as "The stream completion callback armed the data-ready backup timer before flushing the bus CQEs, then errored the SQE without clearing data->stream.iodev_sqe, so the timer later dereferenced an SQE already returned to the RTIO pool"; the hunk moves the timer start after the error check and switches to handle_result_on_error(), which stops that timer and clears the pointer. The RM3100 stream code has no backup timer at all (no k_timer anywhere in the driver), so nothing fires after rm3100_complete_result errors the SQE at line 62. The only other reader of data->stream.iodev_sqe is rm3100_stream_get_data, reached from rm3100_gpio_callback, which disables the data-ready interrupt before reading (line 198); the interrupt is only re-enabled in rm3100_stream_submit after the new SQE has been stored (lines 224 and 229), so the stale pointer left by lines 62 and 101 is never dereferenced. The matching lines are just the generic rtio_iodev_sqe_err() completion call; the use-after-free the fix removes depends on the PAA3905 backup-timer mechanism that RM3100 lacks.

allows use of touch_sensor, rtc_counter, and wdt simultaneously by enabling
ESP_INTR_FLAG_SHARED when calling esp_intr_alloc()

Signed-off-by: Marcio Ribeiro <marcio.ribeiro@espressif.com>

lines: LOG_WRN("GPTimer sleep retention init failed (%d) group=%u index=%u", err,
/* Return value is not checked below, as clock might have been already enabled

static int counter_esp32_get_value(const struct device *dev, uint32_t *ticks)
static int counter_esp32_get_value_64(const struct device *dev, uint64_t *ticks)
static int counter_esp32_set_alarm_64(const struct device *dev, uint8_t chan_id,
static int counter_esp32_cancel_alarm(const struct device *dev, uint8_t chan_id)

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The commit makes the RTC counter's RTC_CNTL interrupt shared ("allows use of touch_sensor, rtc_counter, and wdt simultaneously by enabling ESP_INTR_FLAG_SHARED when calling esp_intr_alloc()"), and the picked hunk adds the matching guard in its ISR: read RTC_CNTL_INT_ST_REG and return unless RTC_CNTL_MAIN_TIMER_INT_ST_M is set, so the counter does not run its alarm handling for another driver's interrupt. The lines matched in counter_esp32_tmr.c (145, 209, 218 and so on) are only the common `struct counter_esp32_data *data = dev->data;` declaration in unrelated functions such as init, start and stop. The TMR driver's own ISR, counter_esp32_isr at line 767, already starts with the equivalent guard for its timer-group hardware: it reads timer_ll_get_intr_status() (line 775) and returns unless its own TIMER_LL_EVENT_ALARM bit is set (line 777), before clearing the status and calling any callback. fix.subject: drivers: sensor: tdk: fix APEX pedometer cadence conversion
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: tdk: fix APEX pedometer cadence conversion

The cadence value is in u6.2 format, so the number of samples between
two steps is raw_val / 4, but the conversion divided by
raw_val + (raw_val & 0x03), double-counting the fractional bits and
dividing by zero when no cadence had been reported yet. Divide by
raw_val alone and report 0 steps/s when raw_val is 0.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Cabé <benjamin@zephyrproject.org>
Assisted-by: Claude:fable-5

lines: * raw_val is the number of samples between two steps, in u6.2 format:

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The fix rewrites the APEX pedometer cadence conversion because, per the commit message, "The cadence value is in u6.2 format, so the number of samples between two steps is raw_val / 4, but the conversion divided by raw_val + (raw_val & 0x03), double-counting the fractional bits and dividing by zero when no cadence had been reported yet." icm566xx_apex_pedometer_cadence_convert (line 145) is the same function with the same uint8_t raw_val and dmp_odr_hz parameters, the same "Converting u6.2" comment (line 150) and the identical pre-fix formula at line 151. It is called the same way: in pedometer mode the SENSOR_CHAN_APEX_MOTION read in icm566xx.c (line 440) passes data->pedometer_cadence, which is only written from ped_data.step_cadence after a step-detect event (apex line 117) and otherwise keeps its zero initial value in the static device data (icm566xx.c line 815), with dmp_odr_hz set to 50 (apex line 163). So the ICM566xx driver both miscomputes the cadence whenever the two fractional bits are non-zero and divides by zero if the channel is read before the first step; it has no guard elsewhere, and the fix needs nothing beyond the function's own arguments.
claude.title: The ICM566xx driver converts the APEX pedometer cadence with the old formula, which reports a wrong step rate and divides by zero before the first step.
claude.summary: In 2026 the ICM45686 and ICM42x70 drivers corrected their pedometer cadence conversion: the u6.2 raw value is now divided as is, and a raw value of 0 reports 0 steps/s instead of dividing by zero. The ICM566xx driver, added with a copy of the same helper, still divides by raw_val + (raw_val & 0x03), so any cadence with non-zero fractional bits comes out too low. Reading the pedometer channel before the sensor has reported a step passes a cadence of 0 and divides by zero. The fixed function can be copied over with only the name changed.
