fix.subject: drivers: i2c: i2c_max32.c: Fix handling of 0-length I2C scan transactions
fix.message:
drivers: i2c: i2c_max32.c: Fix handling of 0-length I2C scan transactions

The I2C shell allows a user to input "i2c scan i2c0" for instance, to
scan addresses on the i2c0 bus enabled in DT. This currently causes
an infinite loop when CONFIG_I2C_MAX32_INTERRUPT is enabled.
The infinite loops happens because 0-length transactions
(tx_len == rx_len == 0) not being handled both by the Async
i2c_max32_transfer and by the controller ISR.

This commit makes two changes:
1) [ISR] When an address ACK is received, if there is simply no data to
send or receive, then just give up the semaphore, preventing the
i2c_max32_transfer function from waiting infinitely.
2) [i2c_max32_transfer] After getting the semaphore back, if there is no
data to send or receive, then avoid waiting for the BUSY flag to clear
since clock stretching should not occur by definition for transactions
which merely contain an address ACK.

Signed-off-by: Brandon Hurst <brandon.hurst@analog.com>

lines: /* 0-length transactions are needed for I2C scans.
* In these cases, just give up the semaphore.
/* We are done, stop sending more data */

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The picked hunk adds an else-branch to the ADDR_ACK case of i2c_max32_isr_controller() in i2c_max32.c that gives the xfer semaphore when tx_len == rx_len == 0; the commit message says such 0-length transactions, sent by "i2c scan", were "not being handled both by the Async i2c_max32_transfer and by the controller ISR" and caused "an infinite loop when CONFIG_I2C_MAX32_INTERRUPT is enabled". i2c_max32_rtio.c, which drivers/i2c/CMakeLists.txt builds instead of i2c_max32.c when CONFIG_I2C_RTIO is set, has the same controller ISR with the unchanged pre-fix ADDR_ACK branch (lines 206-214, which only enables TX_THD or RX_THD|DONE when there is data left), and max32_msg_start() starts a 0-length write the same way (tx_len = buf_len, ERR and ADDR_ACK interrupts, START plus the address byte). In this ISR the only ways to finish a message are the ERR path, the TX path guarded by req->tx_len (line 216), and the RX path, each leading to complete_flag == 1 (line 266) and max32_complete(); an ACKed 0-length write such as the shell scan's (i2c_shell.c line 76) therefore never completes, and i2c_rtio_transfer() waits forever in rtio_submit(r, 1) (i2c_rtio.c line 184) while holding ctx->lock (line 173). The RTIO driver has no xfer semaphore, so the fix must be adapted to signal completion through complete_flag/max32_complete(); the commit's second change (skip the BUSY wait) has no counterpart because the RTIO path does not busy-wait.
claude.title: The MAX32 RTIO I2C driver never completes a zero-length transfer whose address is ACKed, so "i2c scan" and any other 0-length write hang forever.
claude.summary: Commit 7ae44ec850 (2025-04) fixed i2c_max32.c so that its controller ISR releases the waiting thread when a target ACKs its address and the message carries no data, which stopped "i2c scan" from looping forever in interrupt mode. The RTIO variant i2c_max32_rtio.c, built instead of i2c_max32.c when CONFIG_I2C_RTIO is enabled, still has the old ADDR_ACK branch, and none of its other completion paths fire for a message with no data, so such a transfer is never completed. The caller then blocks forever in rtio_submit() while holding the bus lock, so the scan stops at the first device that answers and every later transfer on that I2C controller also blocks. The port has to be adapted: the RTIO driver signals completion with complete_flag and max32_complete() instead of a semaphore, and probably needs to issue the STOP itself. Separately, max32_complete() already returns without completing anything when the bus runs at the standard-speed clock setting (line 319), so this gap is what blocks the scan at the other speeds; none of this has been confirmed on hardware.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: lis2de12: fix read accel via spi
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: lis2de12: fix read accel via spi

The lis2de12 sensor driver spi interface was calling spi read api.
This leads to a single byte operation on reading acceleration data
which is a multi byte operation. Fix it by adding a call to spi read
incr api instead. Added a length check to handle both single and multi
byte read properly.

Signed-off-by: Mayank Narang <narang.may77@gmail.com>

lines: * Instantiation macros used when a device is on a SPI bus.
* Instantiation macros used when a device is on an I2C bus.
* Instantiation macros used when a device is on an I2C bus.

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The picked hunk switches the lis2de12 SPI context from STMEMSC_CTX_SPI to STMEMSC_CTX_SPI_INCR, whose read routine sets bit 6 of the register address for multi-byte reads; the commit message says plain SPI reads turned the "multi byte" acceleration read into "a single byte operation" on lis2de12. stmemsc.h describes the _INCR helpers as ones that "set reg_addr bit6 to '1' in order to allow multiple read/write operations. This is common in some STMEMSC drivers", i.e. a per-sensor addressing scheme (the standalone lis2dh SPI code pairs the same BIT(6) flag with a 6-bit address mask), and before the fix lis2de12 already used the matching STMEMSC_CTX_I2C_INCR on I2C (line 456), just as iis2dh uses _INCR on both buses. iis2iclx.c uses the plain variants on both buses (STMEMSC_CTX_SPI at line 659, STMEMSC_CTX_I2C at line 673), like lsm6dso, so its multi-byte reads such as iis2iclx_acceleration_raw_get() (line 186) are written for a sensor that auto-increments without an address flag, and nothing in the repository marks IIS2ICLX as using the bit-6 scheme. The matched line is only the generic context macro shared by many ST drivers; the deciding fact, the IIS2ICLX register map in the external hal_st module, is not in this repository, hence medium confidence.

multiple read/write operations. This is common in some STMEMSC drivers

fix.subject: drivers: flash_stm32_qspi: fix conditional to assing jedec_id property
fix.message:
drivers: flash_stm32_qspi: fix conditional to assing jedec_id property

the jedec_id field is only available if CONFIG_FLASH_JESD216_API is set

Signed-off-by: Martin Gysel <me@bearsh.org>

lines: .page_size = SPI_NOR_PAGE_SIZE, /* by default, to be updated by sfdp */

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The commit message says 'the jedec_id field is only available if CONFIG_FLASH_JESD216_API is set': in flash_stm32_ospi.c the jedec_id array lives in struct flash_stm32_ospi_data under '#if defined(CONFIG_FLASH_JESD216_API)' (line 146-148), while its initializer was guarded only by the devicetree property, so a board with a jedec-id property and JESD216 API disabled failed to build; the fix adds the Kconfig check to the initializer's #if. In flash_stm32_qspi.c the line that matches the old text guards a different field: jedec_id there is a member of the config struct flash_stm32_qspi_config, declared under the very same condition '#if DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(DT_INST(0, st_stm32_qspi_nor), jedec_id)' (lines 174-175) as its initializer in flash_stm32_qspi_cfg (lines 1780-1781), and nothing in the QSPI file declares jedec_id under CONFIG_FLASH_JESD216_API. Declaration and initializer therefore always appear together, the guard mismatch the fix repairs does not exist, and adding '&& defined(CONFIG_FLASH_JESD216_API)' only to the QSPI initializer would instead break the build when the property is set and the API is off.

fix.subject: driver: sensor: adxl372: Bug fix for q31_t conv
fix.message:
driver: sensor: adxl372: Bug fix for q31_t conv

This is a bug fix for adxl372_accel_convert_q31 function.
Function is used to convert samples received from
sensor to q31_t format when RTIO stream is used.

Signed-off-by: Vladislav Pejic <vladislav.pejic@orioninc.com>

lines: * Sensor resolution is 100mg/LSB, 12-bit value needs to be right
* shifted by 4 or divided by 16. Overall this results in a scale of 160
static inline void adxl372_accel_convert_q31(q31_t *out, const uint8_t *buff)
static int adxl372_decode_stream(const uint8_t *buffer, struct sensor_chan_spec chan_spec,

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The ADXL372 commit ('This is a bug fix for adxl372_accel_convert_q31 function') replaced the micro-m/s^2 value that was clamped into q31 by a q31 scale factor (SENSOR_QSCALE_FACTOR) plus a header shift; the listed hunk is the macro part of that change, dropping SENSOR_SCALING_FACTOR. In adxl345_decoder.c the leftover '#define SENSOR_SCALING_FACTOR' at line 91 is never referenced: a search of the whole adxl345 driver directory finds only the definition. The ADXL345 conversion already works the way the fix intends: adxl345_accel_convert_q31 multiplies the sample by per-range q31 factors (qscale_factor_full_res / qscale_factor_no_full_res) and the decoders set data->shift from range_to_shift. That change came in the ADXL345's own commit 5ee9d7a869 'driver: sensor: adxl345: Bug fix for q31_t conv', which removed the old 'micro_ms2' / CLAMP conversion there, so only an unused macro remains and nothing needs to be carried over.

fix.subject: serial: stm32: fix dropped `UART_TX_DONE` events
fix.message:
serial: stm32: fix dropped `UART_TX_DONE` events

Fix dropped `UART_TX_DONE` events when poll out and async APIs are used
on the same port. Clearing `tx_poll_stream_on` is required to prevent
`uart_stm32_isr` from prematurely clearing the TC status bit.

Signed-off-by: Jordan Yates <jordan@embeint.com>

lines: LOG_DBG("channel=%d, status=%d, dma_tx.counter=%d", channel, status, data->dma_tx.counter);
/* Generate TX_DONE event when TX is done */

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The STM32 commit ('Fix dropped UART_TX_DONE events when poll out and async APIs are used on the same port. Clearing tx_poll_stream_on is required to prevent uart_stm32_isr from prematurely clearing the TC status bit') adds 'data->tx_int_stream_on = false;' under #ifdef CONFIG_PM to async_evt_tx_done/async_evt_tx_abort; those flags belong to the STM32 power-management bookkeeping in which poll_out enables the TC interrupt and uart_stm32_isr consumes TC for a poll stream. uart_bee.c has none of this: struct uart_bee_data has no tx_poll_stream_on or tx_int_stream_on member and the file contains no CONFIG_PM code at all. uart_bee_poll_out just busy-waits until the TX FIFO drains without touching any interrupt, uart_bee_isr handles only the RX idle flag and errors (no transmission-complete flag), and UART_TX_DONE is raised directly from the DMA callback uart_bee_dma_tx_cb. The matching lines in async_evt_tx_done/async_evt_tx_abort are only the shared buffer reset; the state and ISR path the fix corrects do not exist in this driver.

fix.subject: drivers/sensor: lsm6dsv16x: fix DT configuration read for int1/int2
fix.message:
drivers/sensor: lsm6dsv16x: fix DT configuration read for int1/int2

Since lsm6dsv16x may be multi-instantiated, triggers must be enabled
and configured on DT basis and not only thru CONFIG_LSM6DSV16X_TRIGGER
macro; if either int1-gpios of int2-gpios (or both) are configured
in DT, the flag trig_enable is set to 'true' for that instance.
The previous implentation was lacking the check of those two Device
Tree properties, so trig_enabled was always true for all instances.

Signed-off-by: Armando Visconti <armando.visconti@st.com>

lines: * Instantiation macros used when a device is on a SPI bus.
* Instantiation macros used when a device is on a SPI bus.

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The LSM6DSV16X commit fixes that 'trig_enabled was always true for all instances' by including the IRQ part of the config only when 'either int1-gpios of int2-gpios (or both) are configured in DT'; the listed hunk is the part that moves '.drdy_pulsed = DT_INST_PROP(inst, drdy_pulsed)' into the CFG_IRQ macro, while the other hunk wraps that macro in IF_ENABLED(UTIL_OR(...)). lis2de12.c already has both halves of the fixed form: LIS2DE12_CFG_IRQ sets drdy_pulsed itself (line 420), and LIS2DE12_CONFIG_COMMON includes LIS2DE12_CFG_IRQ only inside IF_ENABLED(UTIL_OR(DT_INST_NODE_HAS_PROP(inst, int1_gpios), DT_INST_NODE_HAS_PROP(inst, int2_gpios))) (lines 433-435). An instance without interrupt GPIOs therefore leaves trig_enabled false and lis2de12_init skips interrupt setup ('if (cfg->trig_enabled)', line 385). The matched lines 417-419 are unchanged context of the hunk, present in the fixed driver too, and the added line differs only by its trailing comma, so the script did not recognise it.

drivers/sensor: lsm6dsv16x: fix DT configuration read for int1/int2

Since lsm6dsv16x may be multi-instantiated, triggers must be enabled
and configured on DT basis and not only thru CONFIG_LSM6DSV16X_TRIGGER
macro; if either int1-gpios of int2-gpios (or both) are configured
in DT, the flag trig_enable is set to 'true' for that instance.
The previous implentation was lacking the check of those two Device
Tree properties, so trig_enabled was always true for all instances.

Signed-off-by: Armando Visconti <armando.visconti@st.com>

lines: * Instantiation macros used when a device is on a SPI bus.

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The LSM6DSV16X commit says 'trig_enabled was always true for all instances' because LSM6DSV16X_CFG_IRQ was pasted into every config; the listed hunk wraps it in IF_ENABLED(UTIL_OR(int1_gpios, int2_gpios)) and moves drdy_pulsed into that macro. In lsm6dso.c the matched line 939 sets drdy_pulsed unconditionally, which is harmless because lsm6dso.h declares 'uint8_t drdy_pulsed;' outside the CONFIG_LSM6DSO_TRIGGER block. The part that matters is already guarded: LSM6DSO_CONFIG_COMMON includes LSM6DSO_CFG_IRQ (which sets '.trig_enabled = true' and reads irq_gpios) only through COND_CODE_1(DT_INST_NODE_HAS_PROP(inst, irq_gpios), (LSM6DSO_CFG_IRQ(inst)), ()), so an instance without an interrupt GPIO keeps trig_enabled false and lsm6dso_init skips interrupt setup. The check uses irq_gpios instead of int1/int2 because the LSM6DSO binding defines a single 'irq-gpios' property, so the driver already handles the same problem in its own way.

fix.subject: drivers: flash: stm32_qspi: Fix page size for dual-flash
fix.message:
drivers: flash: stm32_qspi: Fix page size for dual-flash

When dual-flash mode is enabled, even bytes are written to the first
flash memory and odd bytes to the second flash memory. This means, from
the flash driver's point of view, the size of a flash page is twice the
size of a single flash memory's page.

So if each flash memory has 256-byte pages, 512 bytes should be used as
page size by the flash driver. Using 256 bytes was working fine but is
suboptimal.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Altenbach <altenbach.thomas@gmail.com>

lines: LOG_ERR("Failed to abort memory-mapped access before write");
/* Don't write more than a page. */
/* Don't write across a page boundary */
/* Don't write more than a page. */
/* Don't write across a page boundary */
LOG_DBG("Using read mode: %d, instr: 0x%X, dummy cycles: %u",

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The commit message says the old behaviour was not wrong: 'So if each flash memory has 256-byte pages, 512 bytes should be used as page size by the flash driver. Using 256 bytes was working fine but is suboptimal.' Both listed hunks only scale the page size by STM32_QSPI_DOUBLE_FLASH (the QSPI 'dual-flash' devicetree property): the write loop now uses 'SPI_NOR_PAGE_SIZE << STM32_QSPI_DOUBLE_FLASH', which equals SPI_NOR_PAGE_SIZE whenever dual-flash is off, and the SFDP page size is shifted the same way, so the change is a throughput gain in dual-flash mode rather than a correction of wrong behaviour. It would also change nothing in flash_stm32_ospi.c: that driver always sets 'DualQuad = HAL_OSPI_DUALQUAD_DISABLE' and its binding has no dual-flash property, so the matched loop (lines 1565-1573) and the page_size assignment (line 2213) are already correct for its single-flash setup.

fix.subject: drivers: pwm: ehrpwm: fix uninitialized upper bits in cycles_per_sec
fix.message:
drivers: pwm: ehrpwm: fix uninitialized upper bits in cycles_per_sec

- ti_ehrpwm_get_cycles_per_sec() passes a 64-bit cycles pointer to
  clock_control_get_rate() cast down to uint32_t*, which only writes
  the lower 32 bits of the rate. The upper 32 bits of *cycles were left
  uninitialized, so callers computing cycles_per_sec as a 64-bit value
  could read garbage in the high word.

- Zero *cycles before the call so the unwritten upper bits are
  well-defined.

Signed-off-by: Yash Srivastava <y-srivastava@ti.com>

lines: static int ti_ehrpwm_get_cycles_per_sec(const struct device *dev, uint32_t channel,
static int ti_ecap_get_cycles_per_sec(const struct device *dev, uint32_t channel, uint64_t *cycles)
static int ti_ecap_enable_capture(const struct device *dev, uint32_t channel)

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The EHRPWM commit says passing the 64-bit cycles pointer 'cast down to uint32_t*' to clock_control_get_rate() 'only writes the lower 32 bits of the rate. The upper 32 bits of *cycles were left uninitialized', and states the remedy as 'Zero *cycles before the call so the unwritten upper bits are well-defined'; the listed hunk does this with a local uint32_t rate copied into *cycles. ti_ecap_get_cycles_per_sec in pwm_ti_am3352_ecap.c already zeroes the output with '*cycles = 0;' (line 122) right before the same cast call (line 123), so the high word is never left as garbage. The remaining difference is style: the ECAP form relies on the 32-bit store landing in the low half, which holds on a little-endian target. The SoCs that instantiate ti,am3352-ecap (dts/vendor/ti/am64x_main.dtsi, am62l-main.dtsi) belong to the TI K3 family, none of whose Kconfig files select BIG_ENDIAN, and arch/Kconfig says little-endian is the default.

refs.quote: static int ti_ecap_get_cycles_per_sec(const struct device *dev, uint32_t channel, uint64_t *cycles)
Little-endian architecture is the default and should leave this option

/* Translate UART API enum to LPUART enum from HAL */
(101 more lines in this hunk, not shown)

claude.label: not_a_fix
claude.evidence: The picked hunk only rewrites `uart_config.stopBitCount = ...` as `uart_config->stopBitCount = ...` with the same values; this follows from the commit moving the code out of mcux_lpuart_configure_init() into a new helper mcux_lpuart_configure_basic(), which now receives `lpuart_config_t *uart_config` as a pointer. fix.subject: drivers: serial: silabs_eusart: Fix transceiver state after sleep
fix.message:
drivers: serial: silabs_eusart: Fix transceiver state after sleep

The transceiver must be manually shut down prior to going to
deep sleep, otherwise the state will be inconsistent on wakeup.

Register a PM notifier to disable and reenable the transceiver.

In the future, this should be implemented as a power management
TURN_ON/TURN_OFF callback called from a power domain driver.
Since no such driver exists yet for Series 2, deal with it ad-hoc
from the UART driver itself.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5.5
Signed-off-by: Aksel Skauge Mellbye <aksel.mellbye@silabs.com>

lines: /* The PM notifier callbacks carry no context, so wrap the common handlers per instance. */

claude.label: unsure
claude.evidence: The picked hunks wire a per-instance PM notifier into the EUSART init macro; the notifier disables TX/RX before EM2/EM3 and re-enables them after, because, in the fix's words, "EUSART instances in power domain PD1 are not EM2-capable: their clock is gated in EM2, and if the transmitter or receiver is left enabled across the sleep, the transceiver FIFO state is corrupted", and it follows "the EM2 entry sequence documented for the peripheral" using EUSART-only constructs (EUSART_EM2_CAPABLE(EUSART_NUM(...)), EUSART_SYNCBUSY_TXDIS, EUSART_STATUS_TXENS). uart_silabs_usart.c drives a different peripheral through em_usart.h and is structurally like the pre-fix EUSART driver: it only takes PM locks during active transfers, its data struct has no notifier, and it disables the USART only on device-PM SUSPEND, so an idle enabled instance can enter EM2 with TX/RX on. Whether the USART peripheral loses its transceiver state the same way, or which USART instances are EM2-capable, is not visible in this repository (the per-instance capability macros live in the Silicon Labs device headers, which are not part of the zephyr tree). The same author carried other EUSART PM fixes over to USART a few days later (f764977314 "silabs_usart: Hold TX PM lock until TXC") but not this one, which hints at an EUSART-specific issue without proving it.

refs.quote: EUSART instances in power domain PD1 are not EM2-capable: their clock

fix.subject: drivers: dai: intel: alh: make get_properties safe for concurrency
fix.message:
drivers: dai: intel: alh: make get_properties safe for concurrency

The current dai_alh_get_properties() implementation requires additional
layer of locking on user side as the properties object is modified in
the function, but the data is not same for TX and RX directions. If the
DAI is used concurrently for TX and RX, this can lead to a race with
invalid data returned.

Fix the issue and align the alh driver to other DAI drivers by
separating TX and RX state, and only modifying object for one
direction at a time.

Signed-off-by: Kai Vehmanen <kai.vehmanen@linux.intel.com>

lines: static const struct dai_properties *dai_alh_get_properties(const struct device *dev,
static const struct dai_properties *dai_hda_get_properties(const struct device *dev,

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The ALH fix splits the single props object into props[2] because, in the commit's words, "the properties object is modified in the function, but the data is not same for TX and RX directions", so concurrent TX and RX calls could return "invalid data"; in alh.c the values really depend on the direction and stream (fifo_address uses ALH_TXDA_OFFSET or ALH_RXDA_OFFSET plus ALH_STREAM_OFFSET * stream_id, dma_hs_id comes from alh_handshake_map[stream_id]). In hda.c, dai_hda_get_properties() does use one shared object (`&hda->props`, line 86), but it only writes the constants fifo_address = 0, dma_hs_id = 0 and stream_id = 0 and ignores dir and stream_id, and no other code in hda.c or hda.h writes props. A TX call and an RX call therefore store identical values, so the race the fix removes cannot produce wrong data for either direction. The matching line is the same text but not the same logic: the HDA DAI's properties are direction-independent by design.

fix.subject: serial: allow callback setting to be exclusive
fix.message:
serial: allow callback setting to be exclusive

Both the IRQ API and Asynchronous API support callback.
However, since they are both interrupt driven, having
callbacks on both API would interfere with each other
in almost all cases. So this adds a kconfig to signal
that the callbacks should be exclusive to each other.
In other words, if one is set, the other should not
be active. Drivers implementing both APIs have been
updated to remove the callbacks from the other API.
Though, this still leaves the option to disable
the kconfig and allows both APIs to have callbacks
if one desires.

Fixes #48606

Signed-off-by: Daniel Leung <daniel.leung@intel.com>

lines: static inline void uart_stm32_dma_tx_enable(const struct device *dev)
static void uart_bee_irq_callback_set(const struct device *dev, uart_irq_callback_user_data_t cb,
int uart_bee_line_ctrl_set(const struct device *dev, uint32_t ctrl, uint32_t val)
static int uart_bee_async_callback_set(const struct device *dev, uart_callback_t callback,
static inline void async_user_callback(struct uart_bee_data *data, struct uart_event *event)

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The fix makes the two callback setters exclusive because, per the commit, "having callbacks on both API would interfere with each other in almost all cases"; the CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS option it adds (still present, default y, depends on UART_ASYNC_API && UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN) documents that "calling uart_callback_set() would disable the callback previously set via uart_irq_callback_set()". uart_bee.c implements both APIs (Kconfig.bee selects SERIAL_SUPPORT_INTERRUPT and SERIAL_SUPPORT_ASYNC, the API table has both .irq_callback_set and .callback_set) and uses the very same field names as uart_stm32.c, but uart_bee_irq_callback_set() (lines 432-433) and uart_bee_async_callback_set() (lines 494-495) only store their own callback, and nothing else in the file ever clears user_cb or async_cb. Its ISR has the same shape as the pre-fix STM32 one: uart_bee_isr() calls data->user_cb whenever it is set and then runs the async RX-idle handling, so a leftover interrupt-driven callback keeps running during async transfers. The generic wrappers in include/zephyr/drivers/uart/uart_internal.h just forward to the driver, so nothing outside the driver enforces exclusivity; maintainers still treat the omission as a defect (2026 commit 1718448d76 "silabs_eusart: Respect exclusive API callbacks").
claude.title: The Realtek Bee UART driver does not clear the other API's callback when one is set, so the interrupt-driven and async callbacks can both stay active even though exclusive callbacks are enabled by default.
claude.summary: In 2022 commit 9f02eead added CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS (default y when both the interrupt-driven and async APIs are enabled) and changed drivers such as uart_stm32.c so that setting the IRQ callback clears the async callback and vice versa. The Realtek Bee driver received its async API in August 2026 (eb525902e0) with the same field names (user_cb/user_data, async_cb/async_user_data), but uart_bee_irq_callback_set() and uart_bee_async_callback_set() still only store the new callback. Because uart_bee_isr() calls the interrupt-driven callback on every UART interrupt before handling async RX idle, a callback installed earlier (for example by a console or shell) keeps running during async transfers and can read or react to data meant for the DMA receiver, against the documented Kconfig behaviour. The problem only shows when both APIs are used on the same UART instance; the four-line #if CONFIG_UART_EXCLUSIVE_API_CALLBACKS blocks from uart_stm32.c can be copied as is.

fix.subject: drivers/sensor/st: iis2iclx: (fix) convert range into mg
fix.message:
drivers/sensor/st: iis2iclx: (fix) convert range into mg

Fix the sensor range setting at runtime which is currently returning error,
converting the SI (ms2) value passed thru SENSOR_ATTR_FULL_SCALE in mg (and
not in g) as this is the unit used in the driver internals.

Signed-off-by: Armando Visconti <armando.visconti@st.com>

lines: static int iis2iclx_accel_range_set(const struct device *dev, int32_t range)
fs = iis2iclx_accel_range_to_fs_val(range * 1000); /* pass range in mg */
static int ism330dhcx_accel_range_set(const struct device *dev, int32_t range)

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The fix multiplies the range by 1000 in iis2iclx_accel_range_set because iis2iclx_accel_fs_map is {500, 3000, 1000, 2000} with the comment "fs in mg", while its caller passes sensor_ms2_to_g(val), which returns whole g ("@return The converted value, in Gs."); the commit message says the value must be converted "in mg (and not in g) as this is the unit used in the driver internals." In ism330dhcx.c the matching line in ism330dhcx_accel_range_set calls ism330dhcx_accel_range_to_fs_val, which compares range against ism330dhcx_accel_fs_map = {2, 16, 4, 8}, a table in g. Both callers already pass g: the SENSOR_ATTR_FULL_SCALE path passes sensor_ms2_to_g(val), and init passes the devicetree accel-range, which the binding documents as "Range in g" with enum [16, 8, 4, 2]. So the textually identical line is not the same logic: there is no unit mismatch here, and multiplying by 1000 would make every valid range fail with -EINVAL at runtime and at init. The mismatch came from the iis2iclx table being kept in mg (it has a 500 mg entry), which this device's table does not share.

fix.subject: drivers: ethernet: dwc_mac: stm32: configure the DMA bus mode
fix.message:
drivers: ethernet: dwc_mac: stm32: configure the DMA bus mode

The bus mode register was left at its reset value, so the AHB master
issued undefined length bursts and did not align them. Utilize fixed
length bursts with address aligned beats instead.

Signed-off-by: Tim Pambor <tim.pambor@codewrights.de>

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The fix adds `DWMAC_REG_WRITE(DWMAC_DMABMR, DWMAC_DMABMR_AAL | DWMAC_DMABMR_FB);` to the STM32 dwmac_platform_init; the commit message says "The bus mode register was left at its reset value, so the AHB master issued undefined length bursts and did not align them. Utilize fixed length bursts with address aligned beats instead." The NXP glue's dwmac_platform_init already programs the same two settings for its core: it writes DMA_SYSBUS_MODE_AAL | DMA_SYSBUS_MODE_FB to DMA_SYSBUS_MODE a few lines after the matched lines. ETH_NXP_DWC_ETHER_QOS selects ETH_DWC_ETHER_QOS_CORE, and in eth_dwmac_priv.h DWMAC_DMABMR and its AAL/FB bits exist only in the CONFIG_ETH_DWC_ETHER_1000_CORE section, while the QoS section defines DMA_MODE at 0x1000 and the AAL/FB bits in DMA_SYSBUS_MODE at 0x1004, so the STM32 line cannot be carried over as is and the NXP code already uses the QoS equivalent. The write is not undone by a later reset: the QoS core's dwmac_probe issues the DMA_MODE_SWR software reset first and calls dwmac_platform_init afterwards.

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: lsm6dsvxxx: fix int32 overflow decoding high-g accel
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: lsm6dsvxxx: fix int32 overflow decoding high-g accel

Q31_SHIFT_MICROVAL casts its argument to int64_t only after it is
evaluated, so `scale * raw` was computed in 32-bit arithmetic. For the
256g/320g ranges (scale 76570/102155 um/s^2 per LSB) the product
overflows INT32_MAX for readings above roughly 219g, corrupting exactly
the high-g samples these parts exist to capture. Widen the scale to
int64_t before multiplying in both the one-shot and FIFO decode paths.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Cabé <benjamin@zephyrproject.org>
Assisted-by: Claude:fable-5

lines: static int generate_gyro_output(const uint8_t *buffer, int count, uint16_t gy_count,

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The fix casts scale to int64_t before `scale * x` in the lsm6dsvxxx decoder because, in the commit message's words, "For the 256g/320g ranges (scale 76570/102155 um/s^2 per LSB) the product overflows INT32_MAX for readings above roughly 219g". The iis3dwb FIFO and one-shot decode paths have the same expression, with `const int32_t scale = accel_scaler[header->range];` and int16_t samples, so the product is also computed in 32 bits before Q31_SHIFT_MICROVAL widens it. But this device's scale values are far smaller: accel_scaler has only the 2 g, 4 g, 8 g and 16 g entries (the decoder header's range is a 2-bit field, and the dt-bindings header defines only IIS3DWB_DT_FS_2G/16G/4G/8G), and the largest entry is SENSOR_SCALE_UG_TO_UMS2(8 * GAIN_UNIT) with GAIN_UNIT = 61 and SENSOR_G = 9806650, i.e. 488 * 9806650 / 1000000 = 4785 um/s^2 per LSB. With |raw| <= 32768 the largest product is 4785 * 32768 = 156,794,880, about 7% of INT32_MAX (2,147,483,647), so the overflow cannot occur here; the difference comes from the device's full-scale ranges, not from how the code is written.

fix.subject: drivers: lora: native: sx126x: configure the GFSK modem
fix.message:
drivers: lora: native: sx126x: configure the GFSK modem

Set the radio up for GFSK: modulation and packet parameters of its own,
the sync word written to the register the modem matches on, and the CRC
and whitening seeds LoRaWAN's FSK datarate asks for. A bandwidth request
takes the narrowest receive filter at least as wide.

All of that lives in sx126x_gfsk.c, built only when the modem is wanted,
so the shared file carries neither it nor the guards it would need. The
handful of helpers it calls lose their static.

The whitening seed is a nine-bit value and only the low bit of its high
byte belongs to it. What the rest of that register holds is the radio's,
so the byte is read back and only the one bit replaced.

Bit rate, deviation and their combined occupied bandwidth are held to the
ranges the datasheet gives, which also keeps the values inside the
registers they are written to. A fixed-length frame is clocked out at the
configured length, so any other length is refused rather than putting
whatever the buffer still held on air, and airtime reports that length.

Frequency and transmit power are reached the same way whichever modem
follows, so they move into a helper the two configurations share, as does
taking and releasing the radio. Selecting the modem resets part of the
radio, so it now comes before that rather than after.

The packet status bytes mean different things under the two modems, so
the read follows the one in use. The four operating paths each rebuilt
the LoRa packet parameters by hand to set a payload length; they call one
function now, which builds them for the modem the radio is on.

The packet type was selected once, while bringing the radio up. Adding a
path that selects the other one left nothing to put it back, so from the
first GFSK setup onwards LoRa parameters went to the GFSK modem and
nothing left the antenna. It is stated on every configuration now.

Signed-off-by: JaeHwan Jin <jaehwan.jin@rakwireless.com>

fix.subject: drivers: display: sdl: Fix asserts in sdl_display_write
fix.message:
drivers: display: sdl: Fix asserts in sdl_display_write

The asserts and validation code were incorrectly mixing pitch and
width.  These incorrect checks were preventing rendering code from
re-using a smaller section of a buffer allocated to fit the full
screen. We expect to be able to update a portion of the display from a
portion of the buffer, in which case pitch must remain the screen
width. Expecting x + pitch to be smaller than the screen width is
incorrect.

Signed-off-by: Nathan Collins <nathan.collins@kdab.com>

lines: "Pitch in descriptor is larger than screen size");
"Height in descriptor is larger than screen size");
"Writing outside screen boundaries in horizontal direction");
"Writing outside screen boundaries in vertical direction");
"Pitch in descriptor is larger than screen size");
"Height in descriptor is larger than screen size");
"Writing outside screen boundaries in horizontal direction");
"Writing outside screen boundaries in vertical direction");

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The SDL fix replaces `x + desc->pitch` with `x + desc->width` in both the horizontal-bound assert and the -EINVAL check of sdl_display_write; the commit message says "We expect to be able to update a portion of the display from a portion of the buffer, in which case pitch must remain the screen width. Expecting x + pitch to be smaller than the screen width is incorrect." The display API defines pitch as the "Number of pixels between consecutive rows in the data buffer", so it says nothing about where the written area ends on screen. dummy_display_write in display_dummy.c (lines 46 and 52) has the identical pre-fix assert and check, in the same order and with the same messages as the SDL code before the fix, and the function then just returns 0. Nothing in the dummy driver depends on hardware or configuration that would make the pitch-based bound correct there: its config holds only width and height and it accepts the same display_buffer_descriptor. A write at x > 0 from a buffer whose pitch is the full screen width is therefore rejected with -EINVAL (or trips the assert with CONFIG_ASSERT) even though the written area fits.

refs.quote: static int dummy_display_write(const struct device *dev, const uint16_t x,
Enable dummy display driver compliant with display driver API.
/** Number of pixels between consecutive rows in the data buffer */

claude.title: The dummy display driver bounds horizontal writes by the buffer pitch instead of the written width, so it rejects valid partial-screen writes.
claude.summary: In April 2024 the SDL display driver (commit acc2b51959) changed its write bounds check from `x + desc->pitch` to `x + desc->width`, because pitch is the row stride of the source buffer and a partial update taken from a full-screen buffer keeps pitch equal to the screen width. dummy_display_write in drivers/display/display_dummy.c still has the identical pre-fix assert and -EINVAL check. Any write with x > 0 from a buffer whose pitch is the full screen width therefore fails with -EINVAL, or trips the assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT is on, even though the area fits on the screen. Since the dummy display renders nothing, only applications and tests running against it see the spurious error; the fix is the same two-word change as in SDL.
claude.impact_note: The dummy display draws nothing and only stands in for a real panel, so the effect is a spurious -EINVAL or assertion for code and tests running against it, not wrong output on hardware.

fix.message:
drivers/sensor: lis3mdl: fix lis3mdl_sample_fetch API

Fix a runtime bug when both CONFIG_LIS3MDL_TRIGGER and CONFIG_ASSERT
are set. The correct assertion should verify that sensor channel is
either SENSOR_CHAN_ALL or SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ.

Signed-off-by: Armando Visconti <armando.visconti@st.com>

lines: int lis3mdl_sample_fetch(const struct device *dev, enum sensor_channel chan)
* the chip doesn't allow fetching temperature data in

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The lis3mdl fix widens the sample_fetch assertion from `chan == SENSOR_CHAN_ALL` to also accept SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ; the commit message says it fixes "a runtime bug when both CONFIG_LIS3MDL_TRIGGER and CONFIG_ASSERT are set. The correct assertion should verify that sensor channel is either SENSOR_CHAN_ALL or SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ." (the in-tree x_nucleo_iks01a1 sample sets `trig.chan = SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ` and calls `sensor_sample_fetch_chan(dev, trig->chan)` from its data-ready handler). hmc5883l_sample_fetch has the identical pre-fix line `__ASSERT_NO_MSG(chan == SENSOR_CHAN_ALL);` followed by an unconditional burst read of all three axes, exactly like lis3mdl_sample_fetch, and its channel_get supports SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ. The hmc5883l trigger code also hands the caller's own trigger back to the data-ready handler, so the same handler pattern reaches the assertion. Nothing hardware- or configuration-specific separates the two: the fix only uses the generic SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ enum, and hmc5883l does not handle the channel anywhere else in sample_fetch.
claude.title: The HMC5883L driver asserts that sample_fetch is only called with SENSOR_CHAN_ALL, so a fetch of SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ trips the assertion.
claude.summary: In February 2025 the LIS3MDL magnetometer driver (commit b6604f160c) relaxed its sample_fetch assertion to accept SENSOR_CHAN_MAGN_XYZ as well as SENSOR_CHAN_ALL, because a data-ready handler that calls sensor_sample_fetch_chan(dev, trig->chan) with a MAGN_XYZ trigger crashed on the assertion. The HMC5883L magnetometer driver still has the identical `__ASSERT_NO_MSG(chan == SENSOR_CHAN_ALL);` in front of a read that fetches all three axes anyway, and it supports MAGN_XYZ in channel_get and passes the caller's trigger back to the handler. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, an application that fetches the MAGN_XYZ channel (for example from a data-ready trigger set on that channel) stops on the assertion. Release builds without assertions are unaffected, so this is a debug-build problem fixed by the same one-line change.
claude.impact_note: Only builds with CONFIG_ASSERT enabled are affected, where a valid MAGN_XYZ fetch halts on the assertion; without assertions the function already reads all three axes and behaves correctly.

claude.title: The ENE KB1200 GPIO driver's port_set_masked_raw only ORs bits into the output register, so it can never drive a masked pin low.
claude.summary: In July 2026 the ENE KB106x GPIO driver (commit b6b79411bc) fixed port_set_masked_raw to clear the masked bits before setting them, added a spinlock around output and interrupt register updates, masked ISR pending flags with the interrupt-enable register and cleared them before running callbacks. The older KB1200 GPIO driver from the same vendor still has the pre-fix `GPIOD |= (value & mask)`, so gpio_port_set_masked_raw (and gpio_port_set_masked) can raise pins but never lower them, and pins keep a stale high level. Its ISR and interrupt-configure code also keep the pre-fix pattern of firing callbacks for unmasked pending flags and clearing the write-1-to-clear pending register with read-modify-write, which can drop events that arrive meanwhile. The output-register fix can be copied directly, while the interrupt changes need to be rewritten for KB1200's differently structured function, and the wake-mask change to get_pending_int does not apply because KB1200 has no wake support in its driver.

fix.subject: drivers: adc: Fix AD7124 new_cfg zero initialized
fix.message:
drivers: adc: Fix AD7124 new_cfg zero initialized

Initialized new_cfg in adc_ad7124_channel_setup.
In order to determine if two channel configurations
are identical, memcmp is used. The channel configurations
are stored in structs, which means that there are padding
bytes which are also compared when using memcmp.
The proposed solution is to initialize the struct with 0,
which forces the padding bytes to also be zero. Later,
when assigning values to the actual fields of the structure,
the padding remains 0. This means that comparing two
zero-initialized structs with memcmp will only compare
the respective values of the fields inside the struct,
which is the expected behavior. A better idea might be
to actually compare field-by-field values.

Signed-off-by: Raluca Bozdog <raluca.bozdog@analog.com>

lines: static int adc_ad7124_channel_setup(const struct device *dev, const struct adc_channel_cfg *cfg)
static int adc_ad4130_channel_setup(const struct device *dev, const struct adc_channel_cfg *cfg)

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The AD7124 fix zero-initializes new_cfg because, in the commit's words, "memcmp is used. The channel configurations are stored in structs, which means that there are padding bytes which are also compared when using memcmp"; the compared AD7124 struct ad7124_config_props mixes three enums, a uint16_t odr_sel_bits and three bools, so it carries padding. AD4130 also leaves new_cfg uninitialized (line 557) and compares with memcmp, but only over sizeof(struct ad4130_config_props), and that struct holds just two enum members (ref_sel and gain) whose enumerators all fit in 0..7, so there is no mixed-size member to leave padding bytes. Both of those members are always written by adc_ad4130_create_new_cfg (lines 482 and 514) before find_similar_configuration runs, and the function returns early on any error, so the memcmp never reads an uninitialized byte. The remaining fields of new_cfg (cfg_slot, live_cfg) are assigned before the memcpy and are never compared, so the problem the commit fixes does not arise with the AD4130 driver's smaller configuration struct.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_bee: claim DMA channels via dma_request_channel
fix.message:
drivers: serial: uart_bee: claim DMA channels via dma_request_channel

The async driver reserved its devicetree-assigned RX/TX DMA channels by
poking the DMA controller's dma_context atomic bitmap directly with
atomic_set_bit(). That bypassed the public DMA API, never detected a
channel that was already in use, and dereferenced dma_rx/dma_tx.dma_dev
unconditionally: when only one direction is wired to DMA the other
dma_dev is NULL, so the reservation crashed on a NULL pointer.

Reserve each channel through dma_request_channel() with a BIT(channel)
filter instead. This forces exactly the devicetree channel, registers it
in the same allocation bitmap that dma_request_channel(dev, NULL) callers
(such as memory-to-memory transfers) consult, and returns an error when
the channel is already taken. Each direction is now guarded by its own
NULL check, fixing the single-direction crash.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Yuzhuo Liu <yuzhuo_liu@realsil.com.cn>

lines: * Claim the devicetree-assigned channels through the DMA controller's
* allocation bitmap so that dma_request_channel() (e.g. a memory-to-memory
* user on the same controller) can never hand them out again. Using a
* BIT(channel) filter forces exactly the DT channel and fails loudly if it
LOG_ERR("UART RX DMA channel %u already in use",
LOG_ERR("UART TX DMA channel %u already in use",
/* Disable both UART TX and UART RX DMA requests */
/* Disable both TX and RX DMA requests */

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The uart_bee commit names three problems with reserving the devicetree DMA channels via atomic_set_bit: it "bypassed the public DMA API, never detected a channel that was already in use, and dereferenced dma_rx/dma_tx.dma_dev unconditionally", and replaces it with per-direction NULL checks plus dma_request_channel() that "returns an error when the channel is already taken". In uart_ameba_async_init the NULL-pointer crash is already handled differently (each atomic_set_bit sits inside its own `dma_dev != NULL` check, lines 1120 and 1125), and the cast still hits the right bitmap because dma_ameba_data has struct dma_context as its first member, with atomic pointing at channels_atomic. What is still missing is conflict detection: atomic_set_bit marks the channel taken even when it already was, so a second user of the same channel is never reported, and the amebag2.dtsi defaults put uart0 to uart3 all on RX channel 2 (and TX channel 3), so enabling two async UARTs makes them share channels silently; dma_ameba_configure and dma_ameba_start do not check for a busy channel either. The fix cannot be copied verbatim: the Ameba DMA chan_filter compares the filter value with the channel number (`channel == requested_channel`) instead of testing a BIT(ch) mask as the Bee filter does, so the Ameba version has to pass the channel number itself.
claude.title: The Ameba UART async driver reserves its devicetree DMA channels with a bare atomic_set_bit, so a channel that is already taken is never reported.
claude.summary: In August 2026 the Realtek Bee UART driver (commit bd38a7e708) stopped reserving its RX/TX DMA channels by setting bits in the DMA controller's bitmap directly and switched to dma_request_channel() with a filter, adding per-direction NULL checks and failing init when a channel is already in use. The Ameba UART driver already has the per-direction NULL checks, so the single-direction crash the commit describes does not happen there, and its bitmap write does mark the channel for later dma_request_channel(dev, NULL) callers. It still uses atomic_set_bit, though, so a channel that another user already holds is shared without any error; the amebag2.dtsi defaults give every UART the same RX and TX channels, so a board that enables two async UARTs would get colliding DMA transfers instead of an init error. Porting needs adapting because the Ameba DMA filter expects the channel number rather than a BIT() mask, and this is a hardening gap rather than a crash, which is why confidence is medium.
claude.impact_note: With distinct devicetree channels the behaviour is unchanged; the missing check only turns a channel conflict from silent sharing into a reported init error.

fix.subject: drivers: flash: stm32_qspi: Fix status register access for dual-flash
fix.message:
drivers: flash: stm32_qspi: Fix status register access for dual-flash

When dual-flash mode is enabled, two identical flash memories are
connected to the QUADSPI peripheral, each having its own set of
registers. This means that when reading or writing a flash register,
this has to be made for both flash memories.

For example, when reading a status register (1 byte), the QUADSPI
peripheral must be configured to read two bytes of data, which
correspond respectively to the value of the register in the first and
second flash memory. Same thing when writing.

Before this commit, when dual-flash mode was enabled, only the register
of the first flash memory was considered, which means the second flash
memory could be incorrectly configured and that any write/erase
operation could be considered as completed too early, if the operation
takes more time to complete for the second flash memory.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Altenbach <altenbach.thomas@gmail.com>

lines: * SPI_NOR_4BYTE_BIT is BIT 5 for Macronix and 0 for Micron or Windbond
* Moreover bit value meaning is also vendor-specific
/* no QE bit, device detects reads based on opcode */
/* exit early if QE bit is already set */
/* validate that QE bit is set */
LOG_ERR("Status Register %u [0x%02x] not set", qe_reg_num, reg);
LOG_ERR("Status Register %u [0x" FLASH_REG_FMT "] not set", qe_reg_num,
static int stm32_ospi_write_status_register(const struct device *dev, uint8_t reg_num, uint8_t reg)
static int stm32_ospi_program_addr_4b(const struct device *dev, bool write_enable)

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The QSPI commit only matters in dual-flash mode; its message says "When dual-flash mode is enabled, two identical flash memories are connected to the QUADSPI peripheral, each having its own set of registers", and the new struct flash_reg only gains a second byte under STM32_QSPI_DOUBLE_FLASH, which comes from the dual-flash property of the quadspi node (flash_stm32_qspi.c line 67, binding st,stm32-qspi.yaml line 57). The matched OSPI lines are in stm32_ospi_enable_qe, which does have the pre-fix logic (a uint8_t reg checked with (reg & qe_bit) == 0U), but the OSPI driver never runs two memories in parallel: it hard-codes dev_data->hospi.Init.DualQuad = HAL_OSPI_DUALQUAD_DISABLE (line 2361), and neither the st,stm32-ospi nor the st,stm32-ospi-nor binding has a dual-flash property (their only mentions of "dual" refer to 2-data-line (dual SPI) commands and the dual transfer rate). With a single memory, stm32_ospi_read_status_register reads exactly one byte from one device (line 1856), so the one-byte check is correct and there is no second register to miss. The hunks' other matched lines (struct flash_stm32_ospi_data *data = dev->data; in unrelated functions) are only textual matches.

drivers: sensor: adxl345: RTIO stream fix

Fix for RTIO streaming. When stream is canceled
with rtio_sqe_cancel before IRQ or when sequence
for getting data from FIFO, data->sqe is set to NULL.
This will result with early exit from some functions.
Because data->fifo_watermark_irq remain set, it was
not possible to start new stream.

Signed-off-by: Vladislav Pejic <vladislav.pejic@orioninc.com>

static void adxl355_process_status1_cb(struct rtio *r, const struct rtio_sqe *sqe, int result,
LOG_ERR("Failed to get sensor clock cycles");

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The selected hunk adds data->fifo_watermark_irq = 0; to the data->sqe == NULL early return of adxl345_process_status1_cb (the same commit also adds it to adxl345_stream_irq_handler), and the message says "Because data->fifo_watermark_irq remain set, it was not possible to start new stream." adxl355_process_status1_cb (line 248) has the same pre-fix early return at line 259, adxl355_stream_irq_handler has another at line 377, and nothing else in the ADXL355 driver ever clears data->fifo_watermark_irq (declared in adxl355.h line 316). adxl355_submit_stream uses the same caching as ADXL345: only when fifo_watermark_irq != data->fifo_watermark_irq (line 59) does it flush the FIFO (line 70) and read ADXL355_STATUS (line 72), and it then arms the pin as GPIO_INT_EDGE_TO_ACTIVE (line 79), while the GPIO callback disables the pin before calling the stream handler (adxl355_trigger.c line 48). The mechanism is spelled out in the repository: the ADXL345 comment at adxl345_stream.c lines 16-17 says the FIFO keeps "the edge-triggered interrupt line asserted; clearing fifo_watermark_irq makes the next stream reconfigure and flush the FIFO", and the ADXL372 port of this fix (commit 384e1f966f) says that without it "INT1 stays high and the new stream never gets an edge" (adxl372_stream.c line 325 now has data->fifo_full_irq = 0;). The fix only uses a field the ADXL355 driver already has, so nothing it depends on is missing; confidence is medium because the stall also assumes the ADXL355 INT pin stays asserted while STATUS is unread, which the repository only suggests (the trigger thread comments "Clear the status" before reading ADXL355_STATUS, adxl355_trigger.c line 20).

fifo_watermark_irq makes the next stream reconfigure and flush the FIFO.

claude.title: The ADXL355 stream code keeps its cached FIFO-watermark interrupt flag when it drops an interrupt that arrives with no pending stream request, so a restarted stream can get stuck with no data.
claude.summary: On 2026-08-03 the ADXL345 driver (commit c627cf26d123) began clearing data->fifo_watermark_irq when its status callback or interrupt handler finds no pending stream request, and in October 2026 the ADXL372 driver got the same change. The ADXL355 stream code, added in March 2026 with the same design, still just returns from adxl355_process_status1_cb and adxl355_stream_irq_handler when data->sqe is NULL, and still flushes the FIFO and reads STATUS in adxl355_submit_stream only when the cached flag changes. So after a stream is cancelled and the FIFO keeps filling, starting a new stream with the same watermark trigger skips the flush, the interrupt line can stay asserted, and the edge-triggered GPIO never fires, leaving the new stream without data. The fix is the same one-line reset in both early returns, using a field the driver already has. What the repository does not show directly is that the ADXL355 INT pin stays asserted while STATUS is unread; this is inferred from the sibling drivers' comments and the ADXL372 commit message.

fix.subject: drivers: flash_stm32_xspi: Fix Dummy Cycles on MX66UM1G45G NOR at 200MHz
fix.message:
drivers: flash_stm32_xspi: Fix Dummy Cycles on MX66UM1G45G NOR at 200MHz

This commit is fixing configuration of mx66uw1g45g NOR when working
at 200MHz.
According to its specification, when running at 200MHz, this memory should
use a Number Dummy Cycles configuration of 20 (DC bits in CFGR2), which is
the device's default configuration.
Applying the 66MHz configuration as done today was preventing flash to run
at frequency higher than 100Mhz.

This commit doesn't solve the more generic problem of this driver which
is applying this 66MHz configuration universally, irrespective of the
frequency and the memory device, but fixes the configuration which was
reported broken today.

Providing a global change would require starting a clear split between XSPI
controller configuration an bus device configuration, which is what new
MSPI API intend to solve, so this will be tackled once this driver will be
available.

Signed-off-by: Erwan Gouriou <erwan.gouriou@st.com>

claude.evidence: The only behavioural change in the selected hunks is the early return in stm32_xspi_write_cfg2reg_dummy when dev_cfg->max_frequency == MHZ(200) (the other hunks only pass dev instead of the HAL handle), and the message scopes it to one memory and one clock: "This commit is fixing configuration of mx66uw1g45g NOR when working at 200MHz" and "This commit doesn't solve the more generic problem of this driver which is applying this 66MHz configuration universally, irrespective of the frequency and the memory device, but fixes the configuration which was reported broken today." The OSPI driver does have the same unconditional write (stm32_ospi_write_cfg2reg_dummy, lines 702 and 705, called from stm32_ospi_config_mem at line 817 in octal mode), so it shares the generic limitation the message leaves open. But the configuration the workaround targets exists in the tree only on the XSPI side: stm32n6570_dk describes its MX66UW1G45G with st,stm32-xspi-nor at ospi-max-frequency = <DT_FREQ_M(200)>, while the boards that use st,stm32-ospi-nor run it at 25 MHz (stm32l4r9i_disco, octal mode), 26 MHz (b_l4s5i_iot01a) and 40 MHz (mini_stm32h7b0), where the max_frequency == MHZ(200) branch would never run. fix.subject: drivers: counter: tpm: fix init sequence
fix.message:
drivers: counter: tpm: fix init sequence

The current code is enabling the IRQ before calling the TPM_Init()
function which (beside being incorrect by design) opens the door to a
spurious irq to cause the isr function call before the init.  This
corner case can be easily observed for example when running the code
inside a hypervisor/jailhouse where restarting the cell without
previous proper exit (device deinit) can cause a crash (null pointer
dereference) when an IRQ is triggered before the init.

Signed-off-by: Marouen Ghodhbane <marouen.ghodhbane@nxp.com>

claude.label: fixed_differently
claude.evidence: The TPM commit moves IRQ_CONNECT/irq_enable out of the per-instance init wrapper into an irq_config_func that mcux_tpm_init calls after TPM_Init, because, as the message says, "enabling the IRQ before calling the TPM_Init() function ... opens the door to a spurious irq to cause the isr function call before the init"; the selected hunk is the config field that holds this function. The FTM driver already has that field (line 25, filled per instance at line 214 with mcux_ftm_irq_config_##n, which does IRQ_CONNECT and irq_enable), registers mcux_ftm_init itself as the device init function (line 217), and calls config->irq_config_func(dev) only after FTM_Init (lines 149 and 151). Its ISR also checks data->top_callback != NULL before calling it (line 76). The script matched only the neighbouring struct fields (ftm_clock_source, prescale); the only difference from the fixed TPM code is that FTM's callback takes a device pointer, so the problem is already handled on this side.

fix.subject: drivers: serial: uart_mcux_lpuart: Switch to using DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX
fix.message:
drivers: serial: uart_mcux_lpuart: Switch to using DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX

After #63289, multi-level interrupts are now encoded using macro
magic. This means that using the generic DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX() to
fetch the INTID is no longer an option as the queried INTID will
be the one specified through the node's `interrupts` properties.
To fix this, switch to using DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX() which will
return the correctly encoded INTID.

Signed-off-by: Laurentiu Mihalcea <laurentiu.mihalcea@nxp.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The LPUART hunk replaces DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq) with DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX(n, i) in IRQ_CONNECT, because, as the message says, with multi-level interrupts "using the generic DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX() to fetch the INTID is no longer an option as the queried INTID will be the one specified through the node's `interrupts` properties"; devicetree.h confirms that DT_IRQN_BY_IDX encodes the number through DT_MULTI_LEVEL_IRQN_INTERNAL when CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS is set and reduces to DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, irq) only for a level-1 node (lines 3404 and 3460-3462). The IUART driver's MCUX_IUART_IRQ_INIT, compiled under CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN, still has the identical pre-fix IRQ_CONNECT(DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq), ...) at line 284 (and irq_enable with the raw cell at line 288), and nothing else in the driver encodes the number. Most IUART nodes are level-1 (the Cortex-M i.MX8M dtsi inherits interrupt-parent = <&nvic> from armv7-m.dtsi, the A53 dtsi nodes use interrupt-parent = <&gic>), so there the two macros agree, but dts/xtensa/nxp/nxp_imx8m.dtsi puts IUART uart4 behind IRQSTEER master0 (lines 64, 69, 84), and the imx8mp_evk_mimx8ml8_adsp board uses it as console and shell UART with CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS=y (defconfig lines 21-22, board dts lines 19-20); since the IUART selects SERIAL_SUPPORT_INTERRUPT, an application that enables the shell gets the interrupt-driven serial backend by default, which selects UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN, and this code then registers the ISR for that node under the un-encoded number. Impact is light because the same node's comment says "This INTID is just a dummy" "until we can support UART interrupts" (lines 66-67), so UART interrupts on that DSP do not work either way today.

refs.quote: /* TODO: This INTID is just a dummy
until we can support UART interrupts

claude.title: The i.MX IUART driver connects its interrupt using the raw devicetree interrupt cell instead of the multi-level encoded number, which is the wrong number for its node behind the i.MX8M audio DSP's IRQSTEER controller.
claude.summary: In January 2024 the LPUART driver (commit c82789c5ff8f) switched IRQ_CONNECT from DT_INST_IRQ_BY_IDX(n, i, irq) to DT_INST_IRQN_BY_IDX(n, i), because for nodes behind a second-level interrupt controller the raw interrupt cell is no longer the Zephyr interrupt number. The IUART driver's MCUX_IUART_IRQ_INIT still passes the raw cell to IRQ_CONNECT and irq_enable. On the Cortex-M4/M7 and Cortex-A53 i.MX8M SoCs every IUART node sits directly under the NVIC or GIC, where both macros give the same value, so nothing changes there. The i.MX8MP audio DSP board, however, uses an IUART (uart4) behind IRQSTEER master0 as its console and shell UART with multi-level interrupts enabled, so in interrupt-driven mode the handler is registered under the un-encoded number. Because that node's interrupt number is explicitly a placeholder until UART interrupts are supported on the DSP, the fix mainly matters once real UART interrupts are wired up there.
claude.impact_note: Every IUART node on the Cortex-M and Cortex-A i.MX8M SoCs is wired directly to the NVIC or GIC, where both macros give the same number, and the only IUART node behind a second-level controller (the i.MX8M DSP uart4) has an interrupt number its own devicetree calls a placeholder until UART interrupts are supported, so no working configuration behaves differently today.

fix.subject: drivers: virtio: accumulate MMIO driver feature bits in a shadow
fix.message:
drivers: virtio: accumulate MMIO driver feature bits in a shadow

DRIVER_FEATURES is a write-only register per the virtio specification
(4.2.2.2), but virtio_mmio_write_driver_feature_bit() did a
read-modify-write on it. Reads return 0, so every call only ever wrote
the single current mask bit and erased all feature bits previously
written to the same 32-bit word -- e.g. a device driver negotiating a
feature bit in word 1 (bits 33..63) silently dropped VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1
set during transport init.

Accumulate the feature bits in a per-device shadow and write complete
words instead. This also drops the sys_cpu_to_le32() applied to the
mask, which was wrong because virtio_mmio_write32() already performs
the conversion (a no-op on little-endian hosts, corruption on
big-endian ones).

Fixes #115150

Signed-off-by: Hongquan Li <hongquan.li@processmission.com>

lines: /* number of 32-bit words needed to hold all negotiable feature bits */
/* shadow of the write-only DRIVER_FEATURES register */
static inline uint32_t virtio_mmio_read32(const struct device *dev, uint32_t offset)

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The fix adds a driver-side shadow because, in the commit's words, "DRIVER_FEATURES is a write-only register per the virtio specification (4.2.2.2)" for the MMIO transport, so the read-modify-write in virtio_mmio_write_driver_feature_bit read 0 and erased earlier feature bits; the picked hunk is the new shadow array in struct virtio_mmio_data. virtio_pci.c also does a read-modify-write (virtio_pci_write_driver_feature_bit reads the word at line 391 and writes it back), but it goes through the PCI common configuration structure, whose driver_feature field the code documents as read-write (line 49), unlike device_feature which is marked read-only for the driver. Reading driver_feature therefore returns the bits written before, so no bits are lost and a shadow is not needed; the matched lines 92-93 are just the shared virtqueues fields. The commit's second point (a double little-endian conversion of the mask) does not appear either: the PCI mask is a plain BIT() and the conversion is done once in the word helpers (lines 366 and 376).

refs.quote: /* shadow of the write-only DRIVER_FEATURES register */

fix.subject: drivers: i2c: stm32_v2: abort pending controller START on ADDR
fix.message:
drivers: i2c: stm32_v2: abort pending controller START on ADDR

In multi-master scenarios, controller mode may mark itself active before
START is actually issued. If the controller then waits for BUSY while an
ADDR event arrives in target mode, target IRQ handling can be blocked,
which may leave the bus stuck.

Abort the pending controller START when ADDR is detected so target-side
handling can proceed correctly.

Fixes #99074

Signed-off-by: Narek Aydinyan <aydinyan.narek@gmail.com>

lines: /* NACK received, a STOP will automatically be sent */
/* STOP detected, either caused by automatic STOP after NACK or

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The fix ('drivers: i2c: stm32_v2: abort pending controller START on ADDR') adds a branch to the v2 event ISR: when controller_active is set and the v2 ISR register shows ADDR, it treats ADDR as an own-address match, clears ADDR and the pending CR2 START ('Follow the STM32 errata workaround for own-address recognition while START is still pending in controller mode'), and hands over to target handling; this works because the v2 controller path never consumes ADDR, and the follow-up 879678acbb for the same issue speaks only of 'the STM32 I2C v2 peripheral'. i2c_stm32_v1.c drives the separate 'st,stm32-i2c-v1' block and has the same guard text at line 590, but its controller path treats ADDR as the controller's own address-phase event (lines 600-601 call handle_addr(), which clears ADDR at line 282), and START/STOP are driven through CR1 (lines 37-44), not CR2. So controller_active together with ADDR is the normal v1 controller sequence, and the v2 detection and CR2 START abort cannot be carried over without breaking every v1 controller transfer. The repository shows no v1 erratum or report of the same race; a v1 variant, if one exists, would need a different detection, so this is not a missed copy of this fix.

claude.title: The STM32 I2C v2 RTIO driver does not hand an own-address match to target handling while its own controller START is still pending, so the target transfer is not serviced and the bus can hang.
claude.summary: Commit dd9b1122e1 (2026-04-29) changed the non-RTIO STM32 I2C v2 driver so that an own-address match (ADDR) seen while the controller is marked active aborts the pending controller START and switches to target handling; follow-up 879678acbb for the same issue #99074 refined it, and neither touched the RTIO driver. i2c_stm32_v2_rtio.c, which drives the same v2 block, still sets controller_active before generating START, keeps the ADDR interrupt enabled while a target is registered, and its event ISR only goes to target handling when controller_active is false, while its controller path never checks or clears ADDR. If another controller on the bus addresses this device while its own transfer is waiting to start, the target callbacks do not run and ADDR stays pending, which per the commit message 'may leave the bus stuck'. The port has to be adapted because the RTIO data structure has no current.is_arlo or device_sync_sem, so the aborted request must be completed through the RTIO completion path. This is from reading the code only; the race needs a multi-controller bus with a registered target and has not been reproduced.

fix.subject: drivers/i2c: ite: Add handling for read operation with 0-byte length
fix.message:
drivers/i2c: ite: Add handling for read operation with 0-byte length

The current I2C driver assumes that at least one byte will be read in CQ
(command queue) mode. However, when a 0-byte read is issued
(e.g., by cmd_i2c_scan),
The read handler uses (len - 1) to set the command queue length.
When len is 0, this underflows to 0xFF, leading to an incorrect transfer
length and possible crash.

To fix this, add a check in cq_mode_allowed() for reads with length 0:

-Fallback to PIO mode in such cases.
-Properly handle 0-byte reads by issuing STOP (E_FINISH) when the slave
 address is acknowledged.
-Add appropriate handling for NACK conditions when the slave address is
 not acknowledged.

Signed-off-by: Tim Lin <tim2.lin@ite.corp-partner.google.com>

/* Disable SMB channels in FIFO mode. */

fix.subject: drivers: sensor: adxl345: implement proper interrupt configuration
fix.message:
drivers: sensor: adxl345: implement proper interrupt configuration

Fix interrupt enable/disable sequence per ADXL345 datasheet
recommendations.

The ADXL345 datasheet (page 19) states: "When initially configuring
the interrupt pins, it is recommended that the functions and interrupt
mapping be done before enabling the interrupts."

Main changes:

1. Remove adxl345_interrupt_config() which incorrectly enabled
   interrupts during driver initialization without proper sequencing.
   It's not clear to me what was the purpose of this function as all
   the required logic (setting gpio interrups, adxl mapping and enabling
   happens already in tigger_set).
   I checked other drivers and this seems to be the common pattern.

2. Implement proper INT_ENABLE disable/enable sequence in
   adxl345_submit_stream() when reconfiguring watermark interrupts:
   - Disable watermark interrupt in INT_ENABLE
   - Configure interrupt mapping in INT_MAP
   - Flush FIFO
   - Re-enable watermark interrupt in INT_ENABLE

3. Add datasheet-based comments in adxl345_trigger.c explaining
   non-obvious register operations:
   - AC/DC coupling modes (ACT_INACT_CTL register)
   - INT_MAP routing logic (0=INT1, 1=INT2)
   - Interrupt clearing by reading data registers

4. Fix bug in adxl345_trigger_set() where ADXL345_INT_MAP_DATA_RDY_MSK
   was hardcoded instead of using the correct int_mask variable.

Fixes #100891

Tested on ebyte_e73_tbb with samples `accel_polling` and `accel_trig`

Signed-off-by: Tobias Kässer <t.kaesser@gmail.com>

lines: /* Disable watermark interrupt in INT_ENABLE before reconfiguring INT_MAP */
/* Flush the FIFO by disabling it. Save current mode for after the reset. */
/* Re-enable watermark interrupt in INT_ENABLE after configuration */
LOG_ERR("Failed to update interrupt map: %d", ret);

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The hunk adds a write that clears the watermark bit in ADXL345_INT_ENABLE before ADXL345_INT_MAP is changed, following the quoted ADXL345 datasheet advice that 'the functions and interrupt mapping be done before enabling the interrupts'; it relies on the ADXL345 having a separate enable register (ADXL345_INT_ENABLE 0x2E) next to a pure routing register (ADXL345_INT_MAP 0x2F, '0=INT1, 1=INT2'). The ADXL355 header defines no separate interrupt-enable register: its only interrupt register is ADXL355_INT_MAP (line 82), whose bits are per-pin enables such as ADXL355_INT_MAP_FIFO_FULL_EN1_MSK and ADXL355_INT_MAP_FIFO_FULL_EN2_MSK (lines 115 and 119). In adxl355_submit_stream() the single adxl355_reg_update() at lines 61-64 sets or clears the FIFO-full enable bit for the chosen pin, so enabling and routing are one bit and there is no earlier enable to turn off; the host GPIO interrupt is also disabled first at line 45. The fix therefore depends on a register layout the ADXL355 does not have.

lines: /* Disable watermark interrupt in INT_ENABLE before reconfiguring INT_MAP */

/* Re-enable watermark interrupt in INT_ENABLE after configuration */
LOG_ERR("Failed to update interrupt enable register: %d", ret);

claude.label: not_applicable
claude.label_text: Fix does not apply to the copy
claude.evidence: The hunk adds a write that clears the watermark bit in ADXL345_INT_ENABLE before ADXL345_INT_MAP is changed, following the quoted ADXL345 datasheet advice that 'the functions and interrupt mapping be done before enabling the interrupts'; it relies on the ADXL345 routing each interrupt to INT1 or INT2 through a separate INT_MAP register (ADXL345_INT_MAP 0x2F next to ADXL345_INT_ENABLE 0x2E). The MAX30009 driver has nothing to remap: max30009.h defines interrupt enable registers (MAX30009_INTERRUPT_ENABLE1 at line 99) but no interrupt map register, and the device config has a single interrupt_gpio (line 536) with no INT2 routing option. In max30009_submit_stream() the only register write at lines 74-76 toggles the enable bit MAX30009_INTERRUPT_ENABLE1_A_FULL_EN_MSK itself, after the host GPIO interrupt has been disabled at line 57; the INT pin function is set once at trigger init (max30009_trigger.c line 253), not per stream request. So the disable-before-remap ordering the fix adds has no counterpart in this chip's register layout.

fix.subject: dma: iproc_pax_v2: delay initialization after pcie
fix.message:
dma: iproc_pax_v2: delay initialization after pcie

The Broadcom pcie setup has a devicetree dependency like:

/pcie/paxdma -> /pcie/pcie -> /soc/pl330

Add a separate init symbol for iproc_pax_v2 so that these gets
initialized in order, fixes this error:

$ west build -p -b bcm958402m2_m7 tests/kernel/common \
	-DCONFIG_CHECK_INIT_PRIORITIES=y
...
ERROR: /pcie/paxdma@4e100800 POST_KERNEL 40 < \
	/pcie/pcie@4e100000 POST_KERNEL 50

Signed-off-by: Fabio Baltieri <fabiobaltieri@google.com>

claude.label: missing
claude.evidence: The hunk moves the PAX v2 DMA device from CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY to a new CONFIG_DMA_IPROC_PAX_V2_INIT_PRIORITY (default 51) because, in the commit message's words, "The Broadcom pcie setup has a devicetree dependency" and the build reported "/pcie/paxdma@4e100800 POST_KERNEL 40 < /pcie/pcie@4e100000 POST_KERNEL 50"; at the fix's parent v1 and v2 had identical code here. dma_iproc_pax_v1.c still has the pre-fix logic: its config takes pcie_dev from the required pcie-ep phandle (line 981), dma_iproc_pax_init returns -ENODEV when device_is_ready(cfg->pcie_dev) is false (lines 594-596), and the device is defined at POST_KERNEL with CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY (line 990), whose default is KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT = 40. The only PCIe endpoint driver, pcie_ep_iproc.c (compatible brcm_iproc_pcie_ep, which DMA_IPROC_PAX pairs with via select PCIE_ENDPOINT), initializes at CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE = 50, and device_is_ready() just returns dev->state->initialized, so with default settings the v1 DMA runs its init before its endpoint and fails; with CONFIG_CHECK_INIT_PRIORITIES (default y) the build is rejected instead. Kconfig.iproc_pax adds a priority symbol only for DMA_IPROC_PAX_V2 and nothing else in the v1 driver orders it after the endpoint. Caveat that lowers confidence: no in-tree devicetree uses brcm,iproc-pax-dma-v1 (the only PAX DMA node, in viper-common.dtsi, is v2), so only out-of-tree boards would hit this.
claude.title: The Broadcom PAX v1 DMA driver still starts at the generic DMA init priority, before the PCIe endpoint it requires, so its init fails or the default init-priority check rejects the build.
claude.summary: In July 2023 the PAX v2 DMA driver got its own init priority symbol (default 51) so that it starts after the iProc PCIe endpoint driver it depends on through the pcie-ep phandle. The PAX v1 driver, which had the same code at that time, still uses CONFIG_DMA_INIT_PRIORITY (default 40) while the PCIe endpoint driver starts at 50, and its init function returns -ENODEV when the endpoint is not yet initialized. On a board that uses the v1 compatible, the default build-time priority check would reject the build, and with that check off the DMA device would fail to initialize at boot. The port is the same Kconfig symbol under a v1 name used in v1's device definition. No in-tree devicetree enables brcm,iproc-pax-dma-v1, so only out-of-tree boards are affected, which is why confidence is medium.

Neither the adi,max32-i3c binding nor i3c-controller.yaml gives these properties a default, and i3c-controller.yaml says that when i3c-scl-hz is undefined the driver should "use the controller default", so omitting them is a valid devicetree that the MAX32 driver turns into an init failure; nothing else in i3c_max32.c writes scl.i2c or scl.i3c. refs.quote: /* Currently can only act as primary controller. */
use the controller default or as specified by the I3C specification.

claude.title: The MAX32 I3C controller fails to initialize when the devicetree omits i2c-scl-hz or i3c-scl-hz, because init never fills in default SCL rates.
claude.summary: In 2024 the NXP MCUX I3C driver was fixed to fill in default I2C and I3C SCL rates in its init function when the devicetree leaves them out, because its configure function rejects a zero rate and init otherwise failed. The MAX32 I3C driver, added in 2025, has the same structure: the rates come from DT_INST_PROP_OR(..., 0), max32_i3c_configure returns -EINVAL for a zero rate, and max32_i3c_init calls it without setting any defaults. On a board or overlay that enables the MAX32 I3C controller without both rate properties, which the binding allows and says should mean the controller default, the controller fails to initialize and the bus is unusable. The NXP HAL default-config call does not exist for MAX32 and the MAX32 HAL is not in this repository, so the port has to choose default rates itself. The in-tree max32657evkit board sets both properties, so it is not affected today.

fix.subject: drivers: udc_dwc2: Properly revive STALLed endpoints
fix.message:
drivers: udc_dwc2: Properly revive STALLed endpoints

DWC2 documentation unfortunately assigns somewhat confusing semantics to
endpoint "enable"/"disable" and "activate"/"deactivate". The Zephyr USB
device stack endpoint enable/disable refers to DWC2 activate/deactivate.
The DWC2 endpoint enable/disable actions can be loosely referred to
Zephyr USB stack enqueue/dequeue.

Rename the functions and rework internal working to match DWC2
Programming Guide. This makes endpoint halt work as expected by the
stack and therefore fixes all classes that rely on correct STALL
handling. Most notable STALL user is the Mass Storage class.

Signed-off-by: Tomasz Moń <tomasz.mon@nordicsemi.no>

* Busy looping is most likely fine unless profiling shows otherwise.

* receiving IN token from host even if there is packet available in TxFIFO.
* Disabled OUT endpoint means that device will NAK (isochronous: discard data)
* incoming OUT data (or HS PING) even if there is space available in RxFIFO.
* Set stall parameter to true if caller wants to send STALL instead of NAK.

/* For IN endpoints STALL is set in addition to SNAK */

(45 more lines in this hunk, not shown)
