fix.message:
bsp: fm33lc026: Fix GPIO IRQ map lookup

Keep pin2irqindex within the pin_irq_map bounds and handle the first map entry without reading index -1. Pass encoded pin values to the IRQ map lookup path, and validate the lookup result before indexing the map.

Generated-by: OpenAI Codex
Signed-off-by: Old-Ding <35417409+Old-Ding@users.noreply.github.com>

lines: static rt_err_t fm33_pin_dettach_irq(struct rt_device *device, rt_base_t pin)
static rt_err_t ft32_pin_dettach_irq(struct rt_device *device, rt_base_t pin)
static rt_err_t ft32_pin_irq_enable(struct rt_device *device, rt_base_t pin,

claude.label: already_ok
claude.evidence: The listed hunks fix fm33lc026's range-based lookup: pin2irqindex walks a pin_irq_map whose entries hold the highest encoded pin number of each 4-pin EXTI group, and the fix stops the loop from reading one entry past the end ("<= ITEM_NUM" became "< ITEM_NUM") and from reading entry -1 at index 0, and makes fm33_pin_dettach_irq and the disable branch of fm33_pin_irq_enable pass the encoded pin instead of the PIN_STPIN bit mask, which that range search cannot match (commit message: "Keep pin2irqindex within the pin_irq_map bounds ... Pass encoded pin values to the IRQ map lookup path"). The ft32 copy has no pin2irqindex and no range-encoded map: its struct pin_irq_map holds a pinbit, the table has one entry per pin bit, and the index comes from bit2bitno, which returns the bit position or -1 and is always followed by an explicit "< 0 || >= ITEM_NUM(pin_irq_map)" check, so there is no read past the end and no read of entry -1. Its detach path (bit2bitno(PIN_FTPIN(pin))) and disable path (get_pin_irq_map(PIN_FTPIN(pin))) pass the bit mask on purpose, because bit2bitno and get_pin_irq_map(uint32_t pinbit) take a bit mask, and attach and enable compute the index from the same PIN_FTPIN(pin) key, so all four paths agree. Hunk 2 therefore has no counterpart on the ft32 side, and hunks 1 and 3 correspond to ft32 code written so that the key mismatch never existed.

fix.subject: [bsp][n32] n32hxxx: bound the XSPI waits and fix I2C/SPI/NAND edge cases
fix.message:
[bsp][n32] n32hxxx: bound the XSPI waits and fix I2C/SPI/NAND edge cases

- qspi: both XSPI variants poll the status flags with no bound, so an
  unresponsive bus hangs the caller and silently defeats the timeout it
  passed in. Route every wait through the timeout-carrying helpers,
  return -RT_ETIMEOUT and disable the controller on failure, and replace
  the "poll then send" loops with one bounded wait per element.
- hard_i2c: the interrupt receive path programs the BYTENUM window once
  and never reloads it, so a longer message was truncated and still
  reported as success; refuse it with -RT_EINVAL (enable RX DMA for
  longer reads) instead of capping XferSize. Stop capping the transmit
  byte count at the window size as well: BYTENUM counts received bytes
  only, and the cap stopped feeding DAT after byte 255 while TXDATE
  stayed asserted. Reject RT_I2C_NO_START/RT_I2C_NO_STOP on the series
  without frame chaining, where they would silently become a fresh START
  and a STOP, and tear the DMA channel down when the address phase times
  out instead of leaving it armed against a buffer about to unwind.
- spi: the H7xx LLI chain advanced the memory side by SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX
  bytes although BlkTfrSize counts elements, so a 16-bit transfer walked
  half a word early per node; advance by elements and scale both the
  chunk offset and the staging buffer by the data width. Propagate the
  DMA arm failure that was ignored.
- nand: an odd data length has no halfword-only encoding on the 16-bit
  bus and padding would program a byte the caller never asked for, so
  refuse it before the command phase; issue the empty-page dummy store
  as a halfword there too, where 8-bit AHB writes are unsupported.
- Kconfig: gate the Ethernet/SDRAM/LCD/QSPI/NAND options behind
  BSP_PERIPH_PIN_CFG_READY on all three boards. The peripheral clock and
  IO are not configured for these boards yet, so selecting one of them
  builds a driver whose pins stay in the reset function.

lines: /* Mark a non-first chunk of a 4-wire full-duplex message for the
* arm (fd_chunk_cont): chunks keep the engine on, so this chunk's
* SPI_DMA_TransmitReceive arm must re-arm the live engine warm
* rather than drop SPIEN and re-enable -- that mid-message cycle
* puts CPOL=1 SCK edges onto the enabled slave and shifts its frame
* grid (see the warm re-arm note). Slaves never chunk below
* SPI_DMA_CHAIN_MAX and ignore the flag anyway. */
* already_send_length counts elements while the buffers are byte
* addressed, so this chunk's offset must be scaled by the data width
* (16-bit data = 2 bytes per element). Without it every chunk after
* the first starts one byte early per element -- half the real offset
* -- and the DMA walks the wrong half of the buffer. */
rt_uint32_t *dma_aligned_buffer = RT_NULL; /* TX staging buffer (copy path only) */
rt_uint32_t *dma_rx_staging = RT_NULL;     /* RX staging buffer (copy path only) */
rt_uint32_t *p_tx_buffer = RT_NULL;        /* real source that TX DMA reads   */
rt_uint32_t *p_rx_buffer = RT_NULL;        /* real destination RX DMA writes to */
/* Which legs of this chunk the DMA serves: the PIO length gate plus
* two exceptions - a slave never PIO-polls, and neither does a
* 3-wire master receive (see the dispatch note for the measured
* reason). The 3-wire exception is receive-only by construction
/* Build an LLI chain for a 'size'-byte transfer: the memory side advances
* 4095B per node while the peripheral (DAT) address stays fixed. Only the
* last node has IntEn=1, so the whole chain raises a single TC interrupt. */

claude.label_text: Not needed: the copy does not have this feature or code
claude.evidence: The four listed hunks fix the n32hxxx SPI DMA path: spixfer scales each DMA chunk's buffer offset by the data width because already_send_length counts elements, n32_spi_lli_build advances each linked-list node's memory address by SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX elements times the transfer width instead of SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX bytes, and SPI_DMA_Transmit / SPI_DMA_Receive now return -RT_ERROR when n32_spi_dma_arm fails (commit message: "the H7xx LLI chain advanced the memory side by SPI_DMA_BLOCK_MAX bytes although BlkTfrSize counts elements" and "Propagate the DMA arm failure that was ignored"). The tm4c123 copy has none of this code: its whole transfer is a polled loop in spixfer that pushes message->length frames through SSIDataPut / SSIBusy / SSIDataGet in a single pass, with no DMA, no chunking (no already_send_length or chunk offset), no linked-list descriptors and no DMA-arm call whose result could be dropped. The BSP_SPIx_TX/RX_USING_DMA options in the tm4c123 board Kconfig are not referenced anywhere in drv_spi.c, and struct tm4c123_spi_config holds only the SSI base address and the bus name, so there is no DMA channel to set up. Separately, the polled loop indexes both buffers one byte per frame with no data-width scaling; that is a different matter from the DMA chunk and LLI offsets these hunks fix.

fix.subject: [stm32][pandora] fix LCD init ahead PWM
fix.message: [stm32][pandora] fix LCD init ahead PWM

lines: * Set background color and foreground color

claude.label: already_ok
claude.evidence: The fix ("[stm32][pandora] fix LCD init ahead PWM") moves Pandora's rt_hw_lcd_init, which turns on the backlight through rt_device_find("pwm4"), from INIT_DEVICE_EXPORT to INIT_COMPONENT_EXPORT, so it runs after stm32_pwm_init, which the shared STM32 PWM driver registers with INIT_DEVICE_EXPORT; at the same level the LCD init could run before the PWM device exists. The rt-spark LCD driver has no rt_hw_lcd_init; its hardware bring-up function drv_lcd_init, which calls LCD_PWM_BackLightInit (rt_device_find(PWM_BL_NAME)) and LCD_BackLightSet(80) when BSP_USING_ONBOARD_LCD_PWM_BL is set, is already registered with INIT_COMPONENT_EXPORT. Its only device-level function, drv_lcd_hw_init, just fills in and registers the "lcd" device and does not touch PWM. So the rt-spark side already runs its PWM-dependent LCD init after the PWM devices are registered, which is the ordering the fix establishes.

claude.evidence: The commit message says (translated) "the UART timeout check logic has a problem" and "fix uart bug"; the hunk changes the wait loop in stm32_putc from block_timeout-- to --block_timeout, because with post-decrement the rt_uint32_t counter wraps past zero when the wait expires, so the following (block_timeout != 0) check reports success instead of -1. This is a real fix, but it lives entirely in the transmit-timeout counter. The other side's matching function ch32_putc has no such counter: it spins on USART_FLAG_TC without any limit, writes DATAR and always returns 1, struct ch32_uart has no tx_block_timeout member, and the word timeout does not occur anywhere in drv_usart_v2.c. With no timeout counter or timeout result check, the wrap-around the fix removes cannot happen there.

fix.message: [bsp][stm32]fix stm32h7 spi transmit fail probelm.

claude.label: not_needed_hw
claude.label_text: Not needed: different chip, device or board
claude.evidence: The commit "[bsp][stm32]fix stm32h7 spi transmit fail probelm." changes Init.FifoThreshold from SPI_FIFO_THRESHOLD_08DATA to SPI_FIFO_THRESHOLD_01DATA inside the STM32H7-only branch of stm32_spi_init (now shared with MP1 and N6), i.e. it retunes the configurable FIFO threshold of that chip family's SPI peripheral. The other side is the TI TM4C123 driver, which configures its SSI through TivaWare (SSIConfigSetExpClk with protocol, mode, bit rate and data width, then SSIEnable) and moves one frame at a time with SSIDataPut, SSIBusy and SSIDataGet; it has no FIFO threshold setting and no SOC_SERIES_STM32H7 branch. The repository's TivaWare register map for the TM4C123 SSI lists only CR0, CR1, DR, SR, CPSR, IM, RIS, MIS, ICR, DMACTL, PP and CC, and ssi.h describes the FIFO interrupt levels as fixed ("TX FIFO half full or less", "RX FIFO half full or more"). So the configurable FIFO threshold the fix depends on does not exist on that chip.
